cues.zh: 如果你把目前为止的曲线外推一下，对吧？
cues.en: If you extrapolate the curves that we’ve had so far, right?

cues.zh: 如果你说，“嗯，我不知道，我们开始达到博士水平了，去年还是本科水平，前一年还是高中生水平”，同样，你可以对具体任务和适用范围提出质疑。
cues.en: If you say, “Well, I don’t know, we’re starting to get to PhD level, and last year we were at undergraduate level, and the year before we were at the level of a high school student,” again, you can quibble with what tasks and for what.

cues.zh: “我们还缺一些模态，但这些正在被加上，”比如加入了计算机使用，比如加入了图像生成。
cues.en: “We’re still missing modalities, but those are being added,” like computer use was added, like image generation has been added.

cues.zh: 如果你只是大致看一眼这些能力增长的速度，确实会让你觉得我们会在2026或2027年达到那一步。
cues.en: If you just kind of eyeball the rate at which these capabilities are increasing, it does make you think that we’ll get there by 2026 or 2027.

cues.zh: 我认为仍然存在100年内不会发生这种情况的可能。
cues.en: I think there are still worlds where it doesn’t happen in 100 years.

cues.zh: 但这些可能性的数量正在迅速减少。
cues.en: The number of those worlds is rapidly decreasing.

cues.zh: 我们正在迅速耗尽真正有说服力的阻碍因素，真正令人信服的理由来说明这不会在未来几年内发生。
cues.en: We are rapidly running out of truly convincing blockers, truly compelling reasons why this will not happen in the next few years.

cues.zh: 规模扩展非常快。
cues.en: The scale-up is very quick.

cues.zh: 今天我们就是这么做的：先做出一个模型，然后部署成千上万个，甚至几万个实例。
cues.en: We do this today, we make a model, and then we deploy thousands, maybe tens of thousands of instances of it.

cues.zh: 我认为到那时，肯定在两到三年内，不管我们有没有这些超强 AI，集群规模都会大到能部署数百万个这样的实例。
cues.en: I think by the time, certainly within two to three years, whether we have these super powerful AIs or not, clusters are going to get to the size where you’ll be able to deploy millions of these.

cues.zh: 我对意义持乐观态度。
cues.en: I am optimistic about meaning.

cues.zh: 我担心的是经济和权力集中。
cues.en: I worry about economics and the concentration of power.

cues.zh: 其实我更担心的是权力滥用。
cues.en: That’s actually what I worry about more, the abuse of power.

cues.zh: 而 AI 增加了世界上的权力总量。
cues.en: And AI increases the amount of power in the world.

cues.zh: 如果你集中这种权力并滥用它，就会造成不可估量的损害。
cues.en: And if you concentrate that power and abuse that power, it can do immeasurable damage.

cues.zh: 是的，这非常可怕。
cues.en: Yes, it’s very frightening.

cues.zh: 这非常可怕。
cues.en: It’s very frightening.

cues.zh: 以下是与 Dario Amodei 的对话，他是 Anthropic 的 CEO，这家公司创造了 Claude，目前经常位居大多数 LLM 基准排行榜榜首。
cues.en: The following is a conversation with Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, the company that created Claude, that is currently and often at the top of most LLM benchmark leader boards.

cues.zh: 除此之外，Dario和Anthropic团队一直直言不讳地倡导要认真对待AI安全这一议题。
cues.en: On top of that, Dario and the Anthropic team have been outspoken advocates for taking the topic of AI safety very seriously.

cues.zh: 他们持续发表了大量关于这一议题及其他主题的精彩AI研究。
cues.en: And they have continued to publish a lot of fascinating AI on this and other topics.

cues.zh: 之后还有两位来自Anthropic的杰出人士加入了我。
cues.en: I’m also joined afterwards by two other brilliant people from Anthropic.

cues.zh: 首先是Amanda Askell，她是一位研究员，负责Claude的对齐和微调工作，包括设计Claude的性格和个性。
cues.en: First Amanda Askell, who is a researcher working on alignment and fine-tuning of Claude, including the design of Claude’s character and personality.

cues.zh: 有几个人告诉我，她可能是Anthropic里与Claude对话最多的人。
cues.en: A few folks told me she has probably talked with Claude more than any human at Anthropic.

cues.zh: 所以和她聊提示工程以及如何充分发挥Claude潜力的实用建议，绝对是非常有趣的。
cues.en: So she was definitely a fascinating person to talk to about prompt engineering and practical advice on how to get the best out of Claude.

cues.zh: 之后，Chris Olah也过来聊了聊。
cues.en: After that, Chris Olah stopped by for a chat.

cues.zh: 他是机制可解释性领域的先驱之一，这是一系列令人兴奋的努力，旨在对神经网络进行逆向工程，弄清楚内部发生了什么，从网络内部的神经激活模式中推断行为。
cues.en: He’s one of the pioneers of the field of mechanistic interpretability, which is an exciting set of efforts that aims to reverse engineering neural networks, to figure out what’s going on inside, inferring behaviors from neural activation patterns inside the network.

cues.zh: 这是保障未来超级智能AI系统安全的一个非常有前景的方法。
cues.en: This is a very promising approach for keeping future super-intelligent AI systems safe.

cues.zh: 比如，通过从激活中检测出模型何时试图欺骗正在与它对话的人类。
cues.en: For example, by detecting from the activations when the model is trying to deceive the human it is talking to.

cues.zh: 这是Lex Fridman播客。
cues.en: This is the Lex Fridman podcast.

cues.zh: 为了支持它，请查看简介中的赞助商。
cues.en: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 现在，亲爱的朋友们，有请Dario Amodei。
cues.en: And now, dear friends, here’s Dario Amodei.

cues.zh: 让我们从缩放定律和缩放假设这个宏大理念开始。
cues.en: Let’s start with a big idea of scaling laws and the scaling hypothesis.

cues.zh: 它是什么？
cues.en: What is it?

cues.zh: 它的历史如何，我们今天又处于什么位置？
cues.en: What is its history, and where do we stand today?

cues.zh: 我只能结合自己的经历来描述，但我在AI领域已经大约10年了，这是我很早以前就注意到的事情。
cues.en: So I can only describe it as it relates to my own experience, but I’ve been in the AI field for about 10 years and it was something I noticed very early on.

cues.zh: 我最初进入AI世界是在2014年底与Andrew Ng在百度共事时，那几乎正好是10年前。
cues.en: So I first joined the AI world when I was working at Baidu with Andrew Ng in late 2014, which is almost exactly 10 years ago now.

cues.zh: 我们最先研究的是语音识别系统。
cues.en: And the first thing we worked on, was speech recognition systems.

cues.zh: 那时候，我觉得深度学习还是个新鲜事物。
cues.en: And in those days I think deep learning was a new thing.

cues.zh: 它已经取得了很大进展，但大家总在说：“我们还没有成功所需的算法。
cues.en: It had made lots of progress, but everyone was always saying, “We don’t have the algorithms we need to succeed.

cues.zh: 我们只匹配了一小部分。
cues.en: We are only matching a tiny fraction.

cues.zh: 在算法上，我们还有太多需要探索。
cues.en: There’s so much we need to discover algorithmically.

cues.zh: 我们还没找到如何匹配人脑的蓝图。”
cues.en: We haven’t found the picture of how to match the human brain.”

cues.zh: 某种程度上这很幸运，你几乎能享受到新手的好运。
cues.en: And in some ways it was fortunate, you can have almost beginner’s luck.

cues.zh: 我就像是这个领域的新人。
cues.en: I was like a newcomer to the field.

cues.zh: 我看着我们用于语音的神经网络，也就是循环神经网络，我说：“我不知道，如果把它们做大，给它们更多层会怎样？
cues.en: And I looked at the neural net that we were using for speech, the recurrent neural networks, and I said, “I don’t know, what if you make them bigger and give them more layers?

cues.zh: 如果同时扩大数据规模呢？”我只是把这些看作可以独立调节的旋钮。
cues.en: And what if you scale up the data along with this?” I just saw these as independent dials that you could turn.

cues.zh: 我注意到，随着你给模型提供更多数据、扩大模型规模、延长训练时间，模型的表现越来越好。
cues.en: And I noticed that the models started to do better and better as you gave them more data, as you made the models larger, as you trained them for longer.

cues.zh: 那时候我没有精确测量，但我和同事们都有一种直观感受：你投入的数据越多、算力越多、训练越多，这些模型的表现就越好。
cues.en: And I didn’t measure things precisely in those days, but along with colleagues, we very much got the informal sense that the more data and the more compute and the more training you put into these models, the better they perform.

cues.zh: 所以一开始我的想法是：“嘿，也许这只是语音识别系统的情况。
cues.en: And so initially my thinking was, “Hey, maybe that is just true for speech recognition systems.

cues.zh: 也许这只是某个特定的怪现象，某个特定领域。”我想直到2017年我第一次看到GPT-1的结果，我才恍然大悟：语言很可能就是我们可以做到这一点的领域。
cues.en: Maybe that’s just one particular quirk, one particular area.” I think it wasn’t until 2017 when I first saw the results from GPT-1 that it clicked for me that language is probably the area in which we can do this.

cues.zh: 我们可以获取数万亿词的語言数据，并在此基础上训练。
cues.en: We can get trillions of words of language data, we can train on them.

cues.zh: 那时候我们训练的模型都很小。
cues.en: And the models we were trained in those days were tiny.

cues.zh: 用一到八块 GPU 就能训练，而现在动辄用上万块 GPU，很快会到几十万块。
cues.en: You could train them on one to eight GPUs, whereas now we train jobs on tens of thousands, soon going to hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

cues.zh: 所以当我把这两件事放在一起看时，还有少数人，比如你采访过的 Ilya Sudskever，也有类似的观点。
cues.en: And so when I saw those two things together, and there were a few people like Ilya Sudskever who you’ve interviewed, who had somewhat similar views.

cues.zh: 他可能是第一个，不过我觉得也有几个人在同一时期得出了类似看法，对吧？
cues.en: He might’ve been the first one, although I think a few people came to similar views around the same time, right?

cues.zh: 有 Rich Sutton 的“苦涩教训”，Gwern 也写过关于扩展假设的文章。
cues.en: There was Rich Sutton’s bitter lesson, Gwern wrote about the scaling hypothesis.

cues.zh: 但我觉得大约在 2014 到 2017 年间，我才真正想通了，真正有了信念：“嘿，只要把模型规模扩大，我们就能完成这些极其广泛的认知任务。”
cues.en: But I think somewhere between 2014 and 2017 was when it really clicked for me, when I really got conviction that, “Hey, we’re going to be able to these incredibly wide cognitive tasks if we just scale up the models.”

cues.zh: 而在扩展的每个阶段，总会有各种争论。
cues.en: And at every stage of scaling, there are always arguments.

cues.zh: 说实话，我第一次听到这些说法时，心想：“大概是我错了吧，这个领域的专家们才是对的。
cues.en: And when I first heard them honestly, I thought, “Probably I’m the one who’s wrong and all these experts in the field are right.

cues.zh: 他们比我更了解情况，对吧？”有乔姆斯基的论点：“你能搞定句法，但搞不定语义。”还有这种说法：“哦，你能让一个句子有意义，但没法让一个段落有意义。”今天最新的说法是：“我们的数据快用完了，或者数据质量不够高，或者模型不会推理。”
cues.en: They know the situation better than I do, right?” There’s the Chomsky argument about, “You can get syntactics but you can’t get semantics.” There was this idea, “Oh, you can make a sentence make sense, but you can’t make a paragraph make sense.” The latest one we have today is, “We’re going to run out of data, or the data isn’t high quality enough or models can’t reason.”

cues.zh: 而每一次，我们总能要么找到绕过去的办法，要么扩展规模本身就是绕过去的办法。
cues.en: And each time, every time, we manage to either find a way around or scaling just is the way around.

cues.zh: 有时是前者，有时是后者。
cues.en: Sometimes it’s one, sometimes it’s the other.

cues.zh: 所以我现在到了这个阶段，我仍然觉得这始终相当不确定。
cues.en: And so I’m now at this point, I still think it’s always quite uncertain.

cues.zh: 我们只能靠归纳推理来判断未来两年会不会和过去十年一样。
cues.en: We have nothing but inductive inference to tell us that the next two years are going to be like the last 10 years.

cues.zh: 但这部电影我看过太多次，这个故事我见过太多遍，所以我真的相信，扩展大概率会继续下去，而且这里面有种魔力，我们还没在理论层面真正解释清楚。
cues.en: But I’ve seen the movie enough times, I’ve seen the story happen for enough times to really believe that probably the scaling is going to continue, and that there’s some magic to it that we haven’t really explained on a theoretical basis yet.

cues.zh: 当然，这里的扩展指的是更大的网络、更多的数据、更大的算力？
cues.en: And of course the scaling here is bigger networks, bigger data, bigger compute?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 所有这些？
cues.en: All of those?

cues.zh: 尤其是线性扩展更大的网络、更长的训练时间和越来越多的数据。
cues.en: In particular, linear scaling up of bigger networks, bigger training times and more and more data.

cues.zh: 所以所有这些，几乎就像化学反应，反应里有三种成分，你需要把三种成分都线性扩展上去。
cues.en: So all of these things, almost like a chemical reaction, you have three ingredients in the chemical reaction and you need to linearly scale up the three ingredients.

cues.zh: 如果你只扩大其中一个，其他试剂就会耗尽，反应就会停止。
cues.en: If you scale up one, not the others, you run out of the other reagents and the reaction stops.

cues.zh: 但如果你按顺序扩大所有环节，反应就能继续进行。
cues.en: But if you scale up everything in series, then the reaction can proceed.

cues.zh: 当然，既然你有了这种经验科学/艺术，你就可以把它应用到其他更细微的方面，比如把缩放定律应用到可解释性上，或者把缩放定律应用到后训练上。
cues.en: And of course now that you have this kind of empirical science/art, you can apply it to other more nuanced things like scaling laws applied to interpretability or scaling laws applied to post-training.

cues.zh: 或者只是看看这个东西是如何扩展的。
cues.en: Or just seeing how does this thing scale.

cues.zh: 但大的缩放定律，我猜其背后的缩放假设与大型网络、大数据带来智能有关？
cues.en: But the big scaling law, I guess the underlying scaling hypothesis has to do with big networks, big data leads to intelligence?

cues.zh: 是的，我们已经在语言之外的许多领域记录了缩放定律。
cues.en: Yeah, we’ve documented scaling laws in lots of domains other than language.

cues.zh: 所以最初，我们那篇首次展示它的论文是在2020年初，当时我们首次在语言领域展示了它。
cues.en: So initially the paper we did that first showed it, was in early 2020, where we first showed it for language.

cues.zh: 然后在2020年末有一些工作，我们展示了在其他模态上也是如此，比如图像、视频、文本到图像、图像到文本、数学。
cues.en: There was then some work late in 2020 where we showed the same thing for other modalities like images, video, text to image, image to text, math.

cues.zh: 它们都有相同的模式。
cues.en: They all had the same pattern.

cues.zh: 你说得对，现在还有其他阶段，比如后训练，或者有新型的推理模型。
cues.en: And you’re right, now there are other stages like post-training or there are new types of reasoning models.

cues.zh: 在我们测量过的所有这些情况中，我们都看到了类似类型的缩放定律。
cues.en: And in all of those cases that we’ve measured, we see similar types of scaling laws.

cues.zh: 这有点偏哲学问题，但对于为什么在网络规模和数据规模上越大越好，你的直觉是什么？
cues.en: A bit of a philosophical question, but what’s your intuition about why bigger is better in terms of network size and data size?

cues.zh: 为什么它会带来更智能的模型？
cues.en: Why does it lead to more intelligent models?

cues.zh: 在我之前的生物物理学家职业生涯中……我本科读的是物理，研究生读的是生物物理。
cues.en: So in my previous career as a biophysicist… So I did a physics undergrad and then biophysics in grad school.

cues.zh: 所以我回想作为物理学家所知道的东西，实际上比我在Anthropic的一些同事在物理专业知识方面要少得多。
cues.en: So I think back to what I know as a physicist, which is actually much less than what some of my colleagues at Anthropic have in terms of expertise in physics.

cues.zh: 有个概念叫 1/f 噪声和 1/x 分布，通常就像你把一堆自然过程加起来会得到高斯分布，而如果你把一堆分布各异的自然过程加起来……如果你拿个探头接到电阻上，电阻里热噪声的分布就是按频率分之一变化的。
cues.en: There’s this concept called the one over F noise and one over X distributions, where often, just like if you add up a bunch of natural processes, you get a Gaussian, if you add up a bunch of differently-distributed natural processes… If you take a probe and hook it up to a resistor, the distribution of the thermal noise in the resistor goes as one over the frequency.

cues.zh: 这算是某种自然收敛的分布。
cues.en: It’s some kind of natural convergent distribution.

cues.zh: 我觉得它的实质是，如果你观察很多由某种自然过程产生的东西，而这个过程有很多不同的尺度，那就不是高斯分布——高斯分布算是比较窄的分布——而是如果我看那些导致电噪声的大大小小涨落，它们就呈现这种衰减的 1/x 分布。
cues.en: And I think what it amounts to, is that if you look at a lot of things that are produced by some natural process that has a lot of different scales, not a Gaussian, which is kind of narrowly distributed, but if I look at large and small fluctuations that lead to electrical noise, they have this decaying one over X distribution.

cues.zh: 所以现在我会想到物理世界或语言中的模式。
cues.en: And so now I think of patterns in the physical world or in language.

cues.zh: 如果想想语言中的模式，有一些非常简单的模式，有些词比其他词常见得多，比如“the”。
cues.en: If I think about the patterns in language, there are some really simple patterns, some words are much more common than others, like the.

cues.zh: 然后是基本的名词-动词结构。
cues.en: Then there’s basic noun-verb structure.

cues.zh: 然后是名词和动词必须一致、必须协调这一点。
cues.en: Then there’s the fact that nouns and verbs have to agree, they have to coordinate.

cues.zh: 还有更高层次的句子结构。
cues.en: And there’s the higher-level sentence structure.

cues.zh: 然后是段落的主题结构。
cues.en: Then there’s the thematic structure of paragraphs.

cues.zh: 所以存在这种层层递进的模式结构，你可以想象，随着你把网络做得更大，它们首先捕捉到的是非常简单的关联、非常简单的模式，然后还有一条长长的其他模式的长尾。
cues.en: And so the fact that there’s this regressing structure, you can imagine that as you make the networks larger, first they capture the really simple correlations, the really simple patterns, and there’s this long tail of other patterns.

cues.zh: 而如果这条其他模式的长尾像电阻等物理过程中的 1/f 噪声那样非常平滑，那么你可以想象，随着你把网络做得更大，它就在捕捉这个分布中越来越多的部分。
cues.en: And if that long tail of other patterns is really smooth like it is with the one over F noise in physical processes like resistors, then you can imagine as you make the network larger, it’s kind of capturing more and more of that distribution.

cues.zh: 因此，这种平滑性会反映在模型预测的准确度和表现上。
cues.en: And so that smoothness gets reflected in how well the models are at predicting and how well they perform.

cues.zh: 语言是一个演化过程。
cues.en: Language is an evolved process.

cues.zh: 我们发展出了语言，有常用词和不常用词。
cues.en: We’ve developed language, we have common words and less common words.

cues.zh: 我们有常用表达和不常用表达。
cues.en: We have common expressions and less common expressions.

cues.zh: 我们有频繁表达的想法和陈词滥调，也有新颖的想法。
cues.en: We have ideas, cliches, that are expressed frequently, and we have novel ideas.

cues.zh: 这个过程经过数百万年与人类一起发展演化。
cues.en: And that process has developed, has evolved with humans over millions of years.

cues.zh: 所以猜测——这纯粹是推测——这些想法的分布可能存在某种长尾分布。
cues.en: And so the guess, and this is pure speculation, would be that there’s some kind of long tail distribution of the distribution of these ideas.

cues.zh: 所以存在长尾，但同时你所构建的概念层级的高度也在增加。
cues.en: So there’s the long tail, but also there’s the height of the hierarchy of concepts that you’re building up.

cues.zh: 所以网络越大，想必你就有更高的能力去——
cues.en: So the bigger the network, presumably you have a higher capacity to-

cues.zh: 正是如此。
cues.en: Exactly.

cues.zh: 如果你的网络很小，就只能学到常见的东西。
cues.en: If you have a small network, you only get the common stuff.

cues.zh: 如果我用一个很小的神经网络，它很擅长理解一个句子必须有动词、形容词、名词，但在决定这些动词、形容词和名词应该是什么，以及它们是否说得通方面，表现很差。
cues.en: If I take a tiny neural network, it’s very good at understanding that a sentence has to have verb, adjective, noun, but it’s terrible at deciding what those verb adjective and noun should be and whether they should make sense.

cues.zh: 如果我把它稍微变大一点，它在这方面就变好了，然后突然它擅长处理句子了，但不擅长处理段落。
cues.en: If I make it just a little bigger, it gets good at that, then suddenly it’s good at the sentences, but it’s not good at the paragraphs.

cues.zh: 所以，随着我给网络增加更多容量，这些更罕见、更复杂的模式就会被捕捉到。
cues.en: And so these rarer and more complex patterns get picked up as I add more capacity to the network.

cues.zh: 那么，自然的问题就是，这件事的上限是什么？
cues.en: Well, the natural question then is what’s the ceiling of this?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 现实世界有多复杂？
cues.en: How complicated and complex is the real world?

cues.zh: 有多少东西可供学习？
cues.en: How much is the stuff is there to learn?

cues.zh: 我认为我们没有人知道这个问题的答案。
cues.en: I don’t think any of us knows the answer to that question.

cues.zh: 我的强烈直觉是，在人类水平之下不存在上限。
cues.en: My strong instinct would be that there’s no ceiling below the level of humans.

cues.zh: 我们人类能够理解这些各种各样的模式。
cues.en: We humans are able to understand these various patterns.

cues.zh: 所以这让我觉得，如果我们继续扩大这些模型的规模，开发新的训练和扩展方法，那至少能达到我们人类已经达到的水平。
cues.en: And so that makes me think that if we continue to scale up these models to kind of develop new methods for training them and scaling them up, that will at least get to the level that we’ve gotten to with humans.

cues.zh: 那么问题就来了：比人类理解得更多，能多到什么程度？
cues.en: There’s then a question of how much more is it possible to understand than humans do?

cues.zh: 比人类更聪明、更有洞察力，能到什么程度？
cues.en: How much is it possible to be smarter and more perceptive than humans?

cues.zh: 我猜答案一定取决于具体领域。
cues.en: I would guess the answer has got to be domain-dependent.

cues.zh: 如果看生物学这样的领域，我写过一篇《Machines of Loving Grace》，在我看来，人类理解生物学的复杂性是很吃力的。
cues.en: If I look at an area like biology, and I wrote this essay, Machines of Loving Grace, it seems to me that humans are struggling to understand the complexity of biology.

cues.zh: 如果你去斯坦福、哈佛或伯克利，那里有整系的团队在研究免疫系统或代谢通路，每个人都只懂一小块，只专精其中一部分。
cues.en: If you go to Stanford or to Harvard or to Berkeley, you have whole departments of folks trying to study the immune system or metabolic pathways, and each person understands only a tiny bit, a part of it, specializes.

cues.zh: 他们艰难地试图把自己的知识与其他人的知识结合起来。
cues.en: And they’re struggling to combine their knowledge with that of other humans.

cues.zh: 所以我凭直觉感到，AI 在智能提升上还有很大空间。
cues.en: And so I have an instinct that there’s a lot of room at the top for AIs to get smarter.

cues.zh: 如果想到物理世界中的材料，或者解决人与人之间的冲突之类的问题，我的意思是，其中一些问题并非无法解决，而是要难得多。
cues.en: If I think of something like materials in the physical world, or addressing conflicts between humans or something like that, I mean it may be there’s only some of these problems are not intractable, but much harder.

cues.zh: 而且在这些事情上，你能做到的也许就是有限的。
cues.en: And it may be that there’s only so well you can do at some of these things.

cues.zh: 就像语音识别一样，我能听清你说话的程度也是有限的。
cues.en: Just like with speech recognition, there’s only so clear I can hear your speech.

cues.zh: 所以我认为在某些领域，天花板可能非常接近人类已经达到的水平。
cues.en: So I think in some areas there may be ceilings that are very close to what humans have done.

cues.zh: 在其他领域，这些天花板可能还很遥远。
cues.en: In other areas, those ceilings may be very far away.

cues.zh: 我觉得只有当我们真正构建出这些系统时才会知道。
cues.en: I think we’ll only find out when we build these systems.

cues.zh: 很难事先判断。
cues.en: It’s very hard to know in advance.

cues.zh: 我们可以推测，但无法确定。
cues.en: We can speculate, but we can’t be sure.

cues.zh: 而且在某些领域，天花板可能跟人类的官僚体制之类的东西有关，就像你写到的那样。
cues.en: And in some domains, the ceiling might have to do with human bureaucracies and things like this, as you write about.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 所以人类从根本上必须参与在这个循环中。
cues.en: So humans fundamentally has to be part of the loop.

cues.zh: 这才是天花板的成因，而不是智力的极限。
cues.en: That’s the cause of the ceiling, not maybe the limits of the intelligence.

cues.zh: 是的，我认为在很多情况下，理论上技术可以变化得非常快。
cues.en: Yeah, I think in many cases, in theory, technology could change very fast.

cues.zh: 比如我们在生物学方面可能发明的所有东西，但别忘了，要真正把这些东西用于人类，还得经过临床试验体系。
cues.en: For example, all the things that we might invent with respect to biology, but remember, there’s a clinical trial system that we have to go through to actually administer these things to humans.

cues.zh: 我觉得这混合了官僚体制中不必要的东西，以及保护社会完整性的东西。
cues.en: I think that’s a mixture of things that are unnecessary in bureaucratic and things that kind of protect the integrity of society.

cues.zh: 整个挑战在于很难分辨到底发生了什么。
cues.en: And the whole challenge is that it’s hard to tell what’s going on.

cues.zh: 很难分辨哪个是哪个。
cues.en: It’s hard to tell which is which.

cues.zh: 就药物研发而言，我认为我们太慢了，也太保守了。
cues.en: I think in terms of drug development, my view is that we’re too slow and we’re too conservative.

cues.zh: 但当然，如果这些事搞错了，过于鲁莽可能会危及人们的生命。
cues.en: But certainly if you get these things wrong, it’s possible to risk people’s lives by being too reckless.

cues.zh: 所以至少其中一些人类制度实际上是在保护人们。
cues.en: And so at least some of these human institutions are in fact protecting people.

cues.zh: 所以关键在于找到平衡。
cues.en: So it’s all about finding the balance.

cues.zh: 我强烈怀疑，平衡更偏向于希望让事情更快发生，但确实存在一个平衡。
cues.en: I strongly suspect that balance is kind of more on the side of wishing to make things happen faster, but there is a balance.

cues.zh: 如果我们真的遇到极限，如果扩展定律真的出现放缓，你觉得原因会是什么？
cues.en: If we do hit a limit, if we do hit a slowdown in the scaling laws, what do you think would be the reason?

cues.zh: 是受算力限制，还是受数据限制？
cues.en: Is it compute-limited, data-limited?

cues.zh: 还是别的什么？
cues.en: Is it something else?

cues.zh: 受想法限制？
cues.en: Idea limited?

cues.zh: 所以有几点，现在我们说的是在达到人类水平和人类技能之前就撞上了极限。
cues.en: So a few things, now we’re talking about hitting the limit before we get to the level of humans and the skill of humans.

cues.zh: 所以我认为当下流行的一个限制，也是我们可能撞上的限制——像大多数限制一样，我赌它不会发生，但确实有可能——就是我们单纯把数据用完了。
cues.en: So I think one that’s popular today, and I think could be a limit that we run into, like most of the limits, I would bet against it, but it’s definitely possible, is we simply run out of data.

cues.zh: 互联网上的数据就那么多，而且数据质量也有问题。
cues.en: There’s only so much data on the internet, and there’s issues with the quality of the data.

cues.zh: 你可以在互联网上获取数百万亿个词，但其中很多是重复的，或者是搜索引擎优化的废话，或者未来甚至可能是AI自己生成的文本。
cues.en: You can get hundreds of trillions of words on the internet, but a lot of it is repetitive or it’s search engine optimization drivel, or maybe in the future it’ll even be text generated by AIs itself.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这种方式能产生的东西是有限度的。
cues.en: And so I think there are limits to what can be produced in this way.

cues.zh: 话虽如此，我们，我猜还有其他公司，都在研究合成数据的方法，用模型生成更多已有类型的数据，甚至从零生成数据。
cues.en: That said, we, and I would guess other companies, are working on ways to make data synthetic, where you can use the model to generate more data of the type that you have already, or even generate data from scratch.

cues.zh: 想想 DeepMind 的 AlphaGo Zero，他们让一个机器人从完全不会下围棋，一路提升到超越人类水平，靠的就是自我对弈。
cues.en: If you think about what was done with DeepMind’s AlphaGo Zero, they managed to get a bot all the way from no ability to play Go whatsoever to above human level, just by playing against itself.

cues.zh: AlphaGo Zero 这个版本不需要任何人类示例数据。
cues.en: There was no example data from humans required in the AlphaGo Zero version of it.

cues.zh: 另一个方向当然是这些推理模型，它们会做思维链，停下来思考并反思自己的思考过程。
cues.en: The other direction of course, is these reasoning models that do chain of thought and stop to think and reflect on their own thinking.

cues.zh: 某种意义上，这是另一种合成数据，结合了强化学习。
cues.en: In a way that’s another kind of synthetic data coupled with reinforcement learning.

cues.zh: 所以我猜，用其中一种方法，我们就能绕开数据限制，或者可能还有其他可用的数据来源。
cues.en: So my guess is with one of those methods, we’ll get around the data limitation or there may be other sources of data that are available.

cues.zh: 我们可以这样看：即使数据没问题，当我们开始扩大模型规模时，它们就是不再变好了。
cues.en: We could just observe that, even if there’s no problem with data, as we start to scale models up, they just stopped getting better.

cues.zh: 这似乎是一个可靠的观察：它们曾经变得更好，但可能由于我们无法理解的原因，在某个时刻就停止了。
cues.en: It seemed to be a reliable observation that they’ve gotten better, that could just stop at some point for a reason we don’t understand.

cues.zh: 答案可能是，我们需要发明一些新的架构。
cues.en: The answer could be that we need to invent some new architecture.

cues.zh: 过去确实出现过问题，比如模型的数值稳定性，当时看起来像是性能趋于平缓，但实际上当我们找到正确的突破口后，它们并没有真的停滞。
cues.en: There have been problems in the past with say, numerical stability of models where it looked like things were leveling off, but actually when we found the right unblocker, they didn’t end up doing so.

cues.zh: 所以也许我们需要一些新的优化方法或新技术来突破瓶颈。
cues.en: So perhaps there’s some new optimization method or some new technique we need to unblock things.

cues.zh: 到目前为止，我还没有看到这方面的证据，但如果进展真的放缓，那或许会是一个原因。
cues.en: I’ve seen no evidence of that so far, but if things were to slow down, that perhaps could be one reason.

cues.zh: 那算力的限制呢？也就是说，建设越来越大的数据中心成本高昂，这会带来什么影响？
cues.en: What about the limits of compute, meaning the expensive nature of building bigger and bigger data centers?

cues.zh: 所以目前，我猜大多数前沿模型公司大致都在10亿美元的量级上运营，上下浮动三倍左右。
cues.en: So right now, I think most of the frontier model companies, I would guess, are operating in roughly 1 billion scale, plus or minus a factor of three.

cues.zh: 这些是现在已经存在或正在训练的模型。
cues.en: Those are the models that exist now or are being trained now.

cues.zh: 我认为明年我们会达到几十亿，然后到2026年，可能会超过100亿。
cues.en: I think next year we’re going to go to a few billion, and then 2026, we may go to above 10 billion.

cues.zh: 而大概到2027年，他们的目标是建设千亿美元级的集群。
cues.en: And probably by 2027, their ambitions to build hundred billion dollar clusters.

cues.zh: 我认为这一切实际上都会发生。
cues.en: And I think all of that actually will happen.

cues.zh: 大家有很强的决心去建设算力，而且是在这个国家内部完成，我猜这真的会实现。
cues.en: There’s a lot of determination to build the compute, to do it within this country, and I would guess that it actually does happen.

cues.zh: 现在，就算达到一千亿，算力还是不够，规模还是不够，那要么需要更大的规模，要么得想办法更高效地做到，把曲线往上移。
cues.en: Now, if we get to a hundred billion, that’s still not enough compute, that’s still not enough scale, then either we need even more scale, or we need to develop some way of doing it more efficiently of shifting the curve.

cues.zh: 我觉得在所有这些之中，我对强大AI这么快到来持乐观态度的一个原因就是，只要把曲线上接下来几个点外推一下，我们很快就会接近人类水平的能力。
cues.en: I think between all of these, one of the reasons I’m bullish about powerful AI happening so fast, is just that if you extrapolate the next few points on the curve, we’re very quickly getting towards human level ability.

cues.zh: 我们开发的一些新模型，还有其他公司的一些推理模型，已经开始达到我所说的博士或专业水平。
cues.en: Some of the new models that we developed, some reasoning models that have come from other companies, they’re starting to get to what I would call the PhD or professional level.

cues.zh: 看看它们的编程能力，我们发布的最新模型Sonnet 3.5，新的或更新版本，在SWE-bench上能拿到大约50%。
cues.en: If you look at their coding ability, the latest model we released, Sonnet 3.5, the new or updated version, it gets something like 50% on SWE-bench.

cues.zh: SWE-bench 就是一个例子，它包含一堆专业的真实世界软件工程任务。
cues.en: And SWE-bench is an example of a bunch of professional real-world software engineering tasks.

cues.zh: 今年年初，我记得最先进的水平大概是 3% 到 4%。
cues.en: At the beginning of the year, I think the state of the art was 3 or 4%.

cues.zh: 所以十个月内，我们在这个任务上从 3% 提升到了 50%。
cues.en: So in 10 months we’ve gone from 3% to 50% on this task.

cues.zh: 我觉得再过一年，我们大概能达到 90%。
cues.en: And I think in another year we’ll probably be at 90%.

cues.zh: 我是说，不确定，甚至可能比那还少。
cues.en: I mean, I don’t know, but might even be less than that.

cues.zh: 我们在研究生级别的数学、物理和生物领域也看到了类似的情况，比如 OpenAI 的 o1 这类模型。
cues.en: We’ve seen similar things in graduate-level math, physics, and biology from models like OpenAi’s o1.

cues.zh: 所以如果我们继续按照现有的技能水平外推，我觉得如果沿直线曲线外推，几年之内，这些模型就会在人类最高专业水平之上。
cues.en: So if we just continue to extrapolate this in terms of skill that we have, I think if we extrapolate the straight curve, within a few years, we will get to these models being above the highest professional level in terms of humans.

cues.zh: 那么，这条曲线会持续下去吗？
cues.en: Now, will that curve continue?

cues.zh: 你指出过，我也指出过很多可能导致它不会持续的原因。
cues.en: You’ve pointed to, and I’ve pointed to a lot of possible reasons why that might not happen.

cues.zh: 但如果外推曲线继续延伸，那就是我们正在走的轨迹。
cues.en: But if the extrapolation curve continues, that is the trajectory we’re on.

cues.zh: Anthropic有好几个竞争对手。
cues.en: So Anthropic has several competitors.

cues.zh: 很想听听你对这一切的看法。
cues.en: It’d be interesting to get your sort of view of it all.

cues.zh: OpenAI、Google、XAI、Meta。
cues.en: OpenAI, Google, XAI, Meta.

cues.zh: 在这个领域，从广义上赢得竞争需要什么？
cues.en: What does it take to win in the broad sense of win in this space?

cues.zh: 好，我想把几件事分开来说，对吧？
cues.en: Yeah, so I want to separate out a couple things, right?

cues.zh: Anthropic的使命是努力让这一切顺利发展。
cues.en: Anthropic’s mission is to kind of try to make this all go well.

cues.zh: 我们有一个变革理论，叫“争相登顶”。
cues.en: And we have a theory of change called Race to the Top.

cues.zh: “争相登顶”是通过树立榜样，推动其他参与者做正确的事。
cues.en: Race to the Top is about trying to push the other players to do the right thing by setting an example.

cues.zh: 这不是关于自己当好人，而是创造条件，让我们所有人都能当好人。
cues.en: It’s not about being the good guy, it’s about setting things up so that all of us can be the good guy.

cues.zh: 我举几个例子。
cues.en: I’ll give a few examples of this.

cues.zh: 在Anthropic早期，我们的一位联合创始人Chris Olah——我相信你很快会采访他——他是机制可解释性领域的联合创始人，这个领域试图理解AI模型内部发生了什么。
cues.en: Early in the history of Anthropic, one of our co-founders, Chris Olah, who I believe you’re interviewing soon, he’s the co-founder of the field of mechanistic interpretability, which is an attempt to understand what’s going on inside AI models.

cues.zh: 于是我们让他和我们的一个早期团队专注于可解释性这个领域，我们认为这对让模型更安全、更透明很有好处。
cues.en: So we had him and one of our early teams focus on this area of interpretability, which we think is good for making models safe and transparent.

cues.zh: 有三四年时间，这完全没有商业应用。
cues.en: For three or four years that had no commercial application whatsoever.

cues.zh: 现在也仍然没有。
cues.en: It still doesn’t.

cues.zh: 今天我们做了一些早期的测试版，可能最终会有商业应用，但这是一条非常非常长的研究路，而且我们是在公开环境下构建并公开分享成果的。
cues.en: Today we’re doing some early betas with it, and probably it will eventually, but this is a very, very long research bed, and one in which we’ve built in public and shared our results publicly.

cues.zh: 我们这么做是因为我们认为这是让模型更安全的一种方式。
cues.en: And we did this because we think it’s a way to make models safer.

cues.zh: 有意思的是，随着我们这么做，其他公司也开始这么做了。
cues.en: An interesting thing is that as we’ve done this, other companies have started doing it as well.

cues.zh: 有些是因为受到了启发，有些是因为担心如果其他公司在做这件事、显得更负责任，他们也想要显得更负责任。
cues.en: In some cases because they’ve been inspired by it, in some cases because they’re worried that if other companies are doing this, look more responsible, they want to look more responsible too.

cues.zh: 没人想显得像个不负责任的参与者。
cues.en: No one wants to look like the irresponsible actor.

cues.zh: 于是他们也照做了。
cues.en: And so they adopt this as well.

cues.zh: 人们来到Anthropic时，可解释性往往是个吸引点，我跟他们说：“你没去的那些地方，告诉他们你为什么来这里。”然后你很快会发现，别处也有可解释性团队。
cues.en: When folks come to Anthropic, interpretability is often a draw, and I tell them, “The other places you didn’t go, tell them why you came here.” And then you see soon that there’s interpretability teams elsewhere as well.

cues.zh: 这某种程度上削弱了我们的竞争优势，因为就像，“哦，现在别人也在做了。”但这对整个体系是好事，所以我们必须发明一些别人也没在做的新东西。
cues.en: And in a way that takes away our competitive advantage, because it’s like, “Oh, now others are doing it as well.” But it’s good for the broader system, and so we have to invent some new thing that we’re doing that others aren’t doing as well.

cues.zh: 希望这基本上能抬高做正确之事的重要性。
cues.en: And the hope is to basically bid up the importance of doing the right thing.

cues.zh: 这并不关乎我们自身。
cues.en: And it’s not about us in particular.

cues.zh: 也不关乎有没有一个特定的好人。
cues.en: It’s not about having one particular good guy.

cues.zh: 其他公司也能做到这一点。
cues.en: Other companies can do this as well.

cues.zh: 如果他们加入这场竞赛，那就是有史以来最好的消息。
cues.en: If they join the race to do this, that’s the best news ever.

cues.zh: 关键在于塑造向上的激励，而不是塑造向下的激励。
cues.en: It’s about shaping the incentives to point upward instead of shaping the incentives to point downward.

cues.zh: 我们应该说，机制可解释性领域的这个例子，只是严谨而非含糊其辞地做AI安全——
cues.en: And we should say this example of the field of mechanistic interpretability is just a rigorous non-hand wavy wave doing AI safety-

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: ……或者说它正朝那个方向发展。
cues.en: … or it’s tending that way.

cues.zh: 正在努力。
cues.en: Trying to.

cues.zh: 我是说，我认为我们在观察能力方面还处于早期，但我一直很惊讶，我们竟然能如此深入地窥视这些系统内部，并理解我们所看到的东西。
cues.en: I mean, I think we’re still early in terms of our ability to see things, but I’ve been surprised at how much we’ve been able to look inside these systems and understand what we see.

cues.zh: 不像缩放定律那样，感觉有某种规律在驱动这些模型表现更好，而在内部，模型并不是……它们没有理由被设计成让我们能理解它们，对吧？
cues.en: Unlike with the scaling laws where it feels like there’s some law that’s driving these models to perform better, on the inside, the models aren’t… There’s no reason why they should be designed for us to understand them, right?

cues.zh: 它们的设计目的是运行，是为了工作。
cues.en: They’re designed to operate, they’re designed to work.

cues.zh: 就像人脑或人体生化系统一样。
cues.en: Just like the human brain or human biochemistry.

cues.zh: 它们的设计初衷并不是让人打开舱门、窥探内部并理解它们。
cues.en: They’re not designed for a human to open up the hatch, look inside and understand them.

cues.zh: 但我们发现，你可以和 Chris 更详细地讨论这一点，当我们打开它们、真正观察内部时，会发现一些令人惊讶的有趣东西。
cues.en: But we have found, and you can talk in much more detail about this to Chris, that when we open them up, when we do look inside them, we find things that are surprisingly interesting.

cues.zh: 而作为一个副作用，你还能看到这些模型的美。
cues.en: And as a side effect, you also get to see the beauty of these models.

cues.zh: 你可以通过 MEC 和 TERP 这类方法，探索大型神经网络的美妙本质。
cues.en: You get to explore the beautiful nature of large neural networks through the MEC and TERP kind of methodology.

cues.zh: 我惊讶于它竟然如此清晰。
cues.en: I’m amazed at how clean it’s been.

cues.zh: 我惊讶于归纳头这类现象。
cues.en: I’m amazed at things like induction heads.

cues.zh: 我惊讶于我们可以用稀疏自编码器在网络中找到这些方向，而且这些方向对应着非常清晰的概念。
cues.en: I’m amazed at things like that we can use sparse auto-encoders to find these directions within the networks, and that the directions correspond to these very clear concepts.

cues.zh: 我们通过金门大桥版 Claude 演示了一下。
cues.en: We demonstrated this a bit with the Golden Gate Bridge Claude.

cues.zh: 这个实验里，我们在神经网络某一层找到了一个对应金门大桥的方向。
cues.en: So this was an experiment where we found a direction inside one of the neural networks layers that corresponded to the Golden Gate Bridge.

cues.zh: 然后我们直接把这个方向调大。
cues.en: And we just turned that way up.

cues.zh: 我们把这个模型作为演示发布出去，有点半开玩笑，只上线了几天，但它很好地说明了我们开发的方法。
cues.en: And so we released this model as a demo, it was kind of half a joke, for a couple days, but it was illustrative of the method we developed.

cues.zh: 你可以拿这个模型问任何问题。
cues.en: And you could take the model, you could ask it about anything.

cues.zh: 比如你问“你今天过得怎么样？”，不管问什么，因为这个特征被激活了，它都会联系到金门大桥。
cues.en: It would be like you could say, “How was your day?” And anything you asked, because this feature was activated, it would connect to the Golden Gate Bridge.

cues.zh: 它会说，我感觉放松而开阔，就像金门大桥的拱形，或者——
cues.en: So it would say, I’m feeling relaxed and expansive, much like the arches of the Golden Gate Bridge, or-

cues.zh: 它会巧妙地把话题转到金门大桥上，并把它融入回答。
cues.en: It would masterfully change topic to the Golden Gate Bridge and integrate it.

cues.zh: 它对金门大桥的特别关注，也带着一丝伤感。
cues.en: There was also a sadness to the focus it had on the Golden Gate Bridge.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们很快就喜欢上它了。
cues.en: I think people quickly fell in love with it, I think.

cues.zh: 所以人们已经开始想念它了，因为它被下架了，我记得是在一天之后。
cues.en: So people already miss it, because it was taken down, I think after a day.

cues.zh: 不知怎的，这些对模型的干预——你调整它的行为——在情感上让它显得比任何其他版本的模型都更像人。
cues.en: Somehow these interventions on the model, where you kind of adjust its behavior, somehow emotionally made it seem more human than any other version of the model.

cues.zh: 它有很强的个性，很强的身份认同。
cues.en: It’s a strong personality, strong identity.

cues.zh: 它有很强的个性。
cues.en: It has a strong personality.

cues.zh: 它有这种近乎执着的兴趣。
cues.en: It has these kind of obsessive interests.

cues.zh: 我们都能想到某个对某件事着迷的人。
cues.en: We can all think of someone who’s obsessed with something.

cues.zh: 所以这确实让它感觉更像人了一点。
cues.en: So it does make it feel somehow a bit more human.

cues.zh: 我们来聊聊现在。
cues.en: Let’s talk about the present.

cues.zh: 我们来聊聊 Claude。
cues.en: Let’s talk about Claude.

cues.zh: 今年发生了很多事。
cues.en: So this year, a lot has happened.

cues.zh: 三月。
cues.en: In March.

cues.zh: Claude 3 Opus、Sonnet、Haiku 发布了。
cues.en: Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, Haiku were released.

cues.zh: 然后，7 月发布的 Claude 3.5 Sonnet，刚刚又推出了更新版本。
cues.en: Then Claude 3.5 Sonnet in July, with an updated version just now released.

cues.zh: 接着 Claude 3.5 Haiku 也发布了。
cues.en: And then also Claude 3.5 Haiku was released.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下 Opus、Sonnet 和 Haiku 之间的区别吗？我们该如何理解这些不同的版本？
cues.en: Can you explain the difference between Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, and how we should think about the different versions?

cues.zh: 好，那我们回到三月份，当时我们首次发布了这三款模型。
cues.en: Yeah, so let’s go back to March when we first released these three models.

cues.zh: 我们的想法是，不同公司会生产大模型和小模型、更好的和更差的模型。
cues.en: So our thinking was different companies produce large and small models, better and worse models.

cues.zh: 我们觉得市场有需求，既需要真正强大的模型——可能稍慢一些、价格也更高，也需要快速便宜的模型——在速度与成本的限制下尽可能聪明。
cues.en: We felt that there was demand, both for a really powerful model, and that might be a little bit slower that you’d have to pay more for, and also for fast cheap models that are as smart as they can be for how fast and cheap.

cues.zh: 每当你需要做某种困难的分析，比如写代码、头脑风暴想法，或者进行创意写作，我就想要那个真正强大的模型。
cues.en: Whenever you want to do some kind of difficult analysis, like if I want to write code for instance, or I want to brainstorm ideas or I want to do creative writing, I want the really powerful model.

cues.zh: 但商业场景里有很多实际应用，比如我在跟网站交互、报税，或者跟法律顾问沟通、想分析一份合同。
cues.en: But then there’s a lot of practical applications in a business sense where it’s like I’m interacting with a website, I am doing my taxes, or I’m talking to a legal advisor and I want to analyze a contract.

cues.zh: 或者很多公司就是想在 IDE 里做自动补全之类的。
cues.en: Or we have plenty of companies that are just like, I want to do auto-complete on my IDE or something.

cues.zh: 所有这些场景，你都希望响应快，并且能广泛地使用模型。
cues.en: And for all of those things, you want to act fast and you want to use the model very broadly.

cues.zh: 所以我们想覆盖这整个需求谱系。
cues.en: So we wanted to serve that whole spectrum of needs.

cues.zh: 于是我们最终用了这种诗歌主题。
cues.en: So we ended up with this kind of poetry theme.

cues.zh: 那什么诗最短呢？
cues.en: And so what’s a really short poem?

cues.zh: 是俳句。
cues.en: It’s a haiku.

cues.zh: Haiku 是那个小而快、便宜的模型，在当时，考虑到它那么快那么便宜，它的智能程度真的令人惊讶。
cues.en: Haiku is the small, fast, cheap model that was at the time, was really surprisingly intelligent for how fast and cheap it was.

cues.zh: Sonnet 是中等长度的诗，写几段。
cues.en: Sonnet is a medium-sized poem, write a couple paragraphs.

cues.zh: 所以 Sonnet 是中间档的模型。
cues.en: And so Sonnet was the middle model.

cues.zh: 它更聪明，但也稍慢一点，稍贵一点。
cues.en: It is smarter but also a little bit slower, a little bit more expensive.

cues.zh: 而 Opus，就像 Magnum Opus 意为“大作”一样，Opus 是当时最大、最聪明的模型。
cues.en: And Opus, like a Magnum Opus is a large work, Opus was the largest, smartest model at the time.

cues.zh: 这就是最初的思路。
cues.en: So that was the original kind of thinking behind it.

cues.zh: 我们当时的想法是：“每一代新模型都应该推动这条权衡曲线前移。”所以当我们发布 Sonnet 3.5 时，它的成本和速度与 Sonnet 3 大致相同，但智能提升到了比最初的 Opus 3 还聪明的程度。
cues.en: And our thinking then was, “Well, each new generation of models should shift that trade- off curve.” So when we released Sonnet 3.5, it has roughly the same cost and speed as the Sonnet 3 model, but it increased its intelligence to the point where it was smarter than the original Opus 3 model.

cues.zh: 尤其在代码方面，但总体上也如此。
cues.en: Especially for code, but also just in general.

cues.zh: 现在我们已经展示了 Haiku 3.5 的结果。
cues.en: And so now we’ve shown results for Haiku 3.5.

cues.zh: 我相信 Haiku 3.5——最小的新模型——大约和 Opus 3——最大的旧模型——一样好。
cues.en: And I believe Haiku 3.5, the smallest new model, is about as good as Opus 3, the largest old model.

cues.zh: 所以基本上，这里的目标是让曲线发生偏移，然后到某个时间点会出现 Opus 3.5。
cues.en: So basically the aim here is to shift the curve and then at some point there’s going to be an Opus 3.5.

cues.zh: 现在每一代新模型都有自己的特点。
cues.en: Now every new generation of models has its own thing.

cues.zh: 它们使用新数据，个性会以我们试图引导但无法完全引导的方式发生变化。
cues.en: They use new data, their personality changes in ways that we try to steer but are not fully able to steer.

cues.zh: 所以从来不存在那种完全对等的情况，即唯一改变的东西是智能。
cues.en: And so there’s never quite that exact equivalence, where the only thing you’re changing is intelligence.

cues.zh: 我们总是试图改进其他方面，而有些东西会在我们不知情或无法衡量的情况下发生变化。
cues.en: We always try and improve other things and some things change without us knowing or measuring.

cues.zh: 所以这非常像是一门不精确的科学。
cues.en: So it’s very much an inexact science.

cues.zh: 在很多方面，这些模型的行为方式和个性更像是一门艺术，而不是科学。
cues.en: In many ways, the manner and personality of these models is more an art than it is a science.

cues.zh: 那么，比如 Claude Opus 3.0 和 3.5 之间那段间隔时间的原因是什么？
cues.en: So what is the reason for the span of time between say, Claude Opus 3.0 and 3.5?

cues.zh: 如果能谈谈的话，那段时间花在了什么上？
cues.en: What takes that time, if you can speak to it?

cues.zh: 对，所以有不同的流程。
cues.en: Yeah, so there’s different processes.

cues.zh: 有预训练，就是常规的语言模型训练。
cues.en: There’s pre-training, which is just kind of the normal language model training.

cues.zh: 这需要很长时间。
cues.en: And that takes a very long time.

cues.zh: 如今要用数万甚至好几万个GPU或TPU来训练，或者用不同平台，但都是加速芯片，往往要训练好几个月。
cues.en: That uses, these days, tens of thousands, sometimes many tens of thousands of GPUs or TPUs or training them, or we use different platforms, but accelerator chips, often training for months.

cues.zh: 然后有一个后训练阶段，我们做基于人类反馈的强化学习，以及其他类型的强化学习。
cues.en: There’s then a kind of post-training phase where we do reinforcement learning from human feedback as well as other kinds of reinforcement learning.

cues.zh: 这个阶段现在越来越大，而且往往不那么精确。
cues.en: That phase is getting larger and larger now, and often that’s less of an exact science.

cues.zh: 通常需要花功夫才能做好。
cues.en: It often takes effort to get it right.

cues.zh: 然后模型会和我们的一些早期合作伙伴一起测试，看看效果如何，之后会在内部和外部进行安全测试，尤其是灾难性风险和自主性风险。
cues.en: Models are then tested with some of our early partners to see how good they are, and they’re then tested, both internally and externally, for their safety, particularly for catastrophic and autonomy risks.

cues.zh: 我们按照负责任扩展政策进行内部测试，这一点我可以再详细讲讲。
cues.en: So we do internal testing according to our responsible scaling policy, which I could talk more about that in detail.

cues.zh: 然后我们与美国和英国人工智能安全研究所达成协议，还与特定领域的其他第三方测试者合作，测试模型是否存在所谓的CBRN风险，即化学、生物、放射和核风险。
cues.en: And then we have an agreement with the US and the UK AI Safety Institute, as well as other third-party testers in specific domains, to test the models for what are called CBRN risks, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear.

cues.zh: 我们认为模型目前尚未构成这些严重风险，但每推出一个新模型，我们都想评估一下，看是否开始接近某些更危险的能力。
cues.en: We don’t think that models pose these risks seriously yet, but every new model we want to evaluate to see if we’re starting to get close to some of these more dangerous capabilities.

cues.zh: 这些就是各个阶段，之后还需要一些时间让模型在推理方面正常工作，并在API中上线。
cues.en: So those are the phases, and then it just takes some time to get the model working in terms of inference and launching it in the API.

cues.zh: 所以要让一个模型真正跑起来，确实有很多步骤。
cues.en: So there’s just a lot of steps to actually making a model work.

cues.zh: 当然，我们一直努力让流程尽可能精简。
cues.en: And of course, we’re always trying to make the processes as streamlined as possible.

cues.zh: 我们希望安全测试严谨，但同时也要严谨且自动化，尽可能快速地完成，而不牺牲严谨性。
cues.en: We want our safety testing to be rigorous, but we want it to be rigorous and to be automatic, to happen as fast as it can, without compromising on rigor.

cues.zh: 预训练和后续训练流程也是如此。
cues.en: Same with our pre-training process and our post-training process.

cues.zh: 所以这就像构建其他任何东西一样。
cues.en: So it’s just building anything else.

cues.zh: 就像制造飞机一样。
cues.en: It’s just like building airplanes.

cues.zh: 你要确保它们安全，但也要让流程精简。
cues.en: You want to make them safe, but you want to make the process streamlined.

cues.zh: 我认为这两者之间的创造性张力，是让模型奏效的关键。
cues.en: And I think the creative tension between those is an important thing in making the models work.

cues.zh: 对，街上传言，我忘了是谁说的，Anthropic 的工具真的很好。
cues.en: Yeah, rumor on the street, I forget who was saying that, Anthropic has really good tooling.

cues.zh: 所以这里的很多挑战可能在于软件工程方面，即构建工具，以便与基础设施进行高效、低摩擦的交互。
cues.en: So probably a lot of the challenge here is, on the software engineering side, is to build the tooling to have a efficient, low-friction interaction with the infrastructure.

cues.zh: 你会惊讶地发现，构建这些模型的挑战有多少其实归结于软件工程、性能工程。
cues.en: You would be surprised how much of the challenges of building these models comes down to software engineering, performance engineering.

cues.zh: 从外面看，你可能会想：“天哪，我们有了这个灵光一现的突破。”就像电影里的科学那样。
cues.en: From the outside, you might think, “Oh man, we had this Eureka breakthrough.” You know, this movie with the science.

cues.zh: “我们发现了它，我们搞懂了它。”但我觉得所有事情，甚至是不可思议的发现，几乎总是归结于细节。
cues.en: “We discovered it, we figured it out.” But I think all things, even incredible discoveries, they almost always come down to the details.

cues.zh: 而且往往是超级、超级无聊的细节。
cues.en: And often super, super boring details.

cues.zh: 我无法断言我们的工具是否比其他公司更好。
cues.en: I can’t speak to whether we have better tooling than other companies.

cues.zh: 我是说，我没在那些其他公司待过，至少最近没有，但这确实是我们非常关注的事情。
cues.en: I mean, haven’t been at those other companies, at least not recently, but it’s certainly something we give a lot of attention to.

cues.zh: 我不知道你能不能讲，但从 Claude 3 到 Claude 3.5，有没有进行额外的预训练，还是主要聚焦于后训练？
cues.en: I don’t know if you can say, but from Claude 3 to Claude 3.5, is there any extra pre-training going on, or is it mostly focused on the post-training?

cues.zh: 性能提升是跨越式的。
cues.en: There’s been leaps in performance.

cues.zh: 是的，我认为在任何阶段，我们都专注于同时改进所有方面。
cues.en: Yeah, I think at any given stage, we’re focused on improving everything at once.

cues.zh: 很自然。
cues.en: Just naturally.

cues.zh: 比如，有不同的团队。
cues.en: Like, there are different teams.

cues.zh: 每个团队在特定领域取得进展，让他们在接力赛中负责的那一段跑得更好。
cues.en: Each team makes progress in a particular area, in making their particular segment of the relay race better.

cues.zh: 很自然，当我们做新模型时，会把这些东西一次性全放进去。
cues.en: And it’s just natural that when we make a new model, we put all of these things in at once.

cues.zh: 那么你拥有的数据，从RLHF获得的偏好数据，有没有办法在训练新模型时应用上去？
cues.en: So the data you have, the preference data you get from RLHF, is there ways to apply it to newer models as it get trained up?

cues.zh: 有的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 旧模型的偏好数据有时会用于新模型，当然在新模型上训练效果会更好一些。
cues.en: Preference data from old models sometimes gets used for new models, although of course it performs somewhat better when it’s trained on the new models.

cues.zh: 注意我们有这种宪法AI方法，我们不仅使用偏好数据，还有一个后训练过程，让模型与自身对抗训练。
cues.en: Note that we have this constitutional AI method such that we don’t only use preference data, there’s also a post-training process where we train the model against itself.

cues.zh: 现在每天都会用到一些新的、让模型自我对抗的后训练方法。
cues.en: And there’s new types of post-training the model against itself that are used every day.

cues.zh: 所以不只是 RLHF，还有很多其他方法。
cues.en: So it’s not just RLHF, a bunch of other methods as well.

cues.zh: 我觉得后训练正变得越来越精细复杂。
cues.en: Post-training, I think, is becoming more and more sophisticated.

cues.zh: 那是什么造就了新版 Sonnet 3.5 性能的大幅跃升呢，至少从编程方面来说？
cues.en: Well, what explains the big leap in performance for the new Sonnet 3.5, I mean, at least in the programming side?

cues.zh: 也许这里正适合谈谈基准测试。
cues.en: And maybe this is a good place to talk about benchmarks.

cues.zh: 只是数字上升了，但我写代码，而且我也热爱编程，我用 Cursor 里的 Claude 3.5 来辅助编程。
cues.en: Just the number went up, but I program, but I also love programming, and I Claude 3.5 through Cursor is what I use to assist me in programming.

cues.zh: 至少从经验和传闻来看，它编程确实变聪明了。
cues.en: And there was, at least experientially, anecdotally, it’s gotten smarter at programming.

cues.zh: 我们——
cues.en: We-

cues.zh: 那要让模型变得更聪明，需要怎么做？
cues.en: So what does it take to get it smarter?

cues.zh: 我们也观察到了这一点。
cues.en: We observe that as well.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，Anthropic 这里有几位非常厉害的工程师，之前所有的代码模型，无论是我们做的还是其他公司做的，对他们来说都不太有用。
cues.en: By the way, there were a couple very strong engineers here at Anthropic, who all previous code models, both produced by us and produced by all the other companies, hadn’t really been useful to them.

cues.zh: 他们说：“也许这对初学者有用。
cues.en: They said, “Maybe this is useful to a beginner.

cues.zh: 但对我没用。”但 Sonnet 3.5，最初那个版本，第一次有人说：“天哪，这帮我搞定了一件本来要花好几个小时的事。
cues.en: It’s not useful to me.” But Sonnet 3.5, the original one for the first time, they said, “Oh, my God, this helped me with something that it would’ve taken me hours to do.

cues.zh: 这是第一个真正帮我省下时间的模型。”
cues.en: This is the first model that’s actually saved me time.”

cues.zh: 所以，水位线又在上升了。
cues.en: So again, the water line is rising.

cues.zh: 然后我觉得新的 Sonnet 还要更好。
cues.en: And then I think the new Sonnet has been even better.

cues.zh: 至于它需要什么，我只能说这是全方位的。
cues.en: In terms of what it takes, I’ll just say it’s been across the board.

cues.zh: 它在预训练里，在后训练里，也在我们做的各种评估里。
cues.en: It’s in the pre-training, it’s in the post-training, it’s in various evaluations that we do.

cues.zh: 我们也观察到了这一点。
cues.en: We’ve observed this as well.

cues.zh: 如果我们深入看基准测试的细节，SWE-bench 基本上……既然你是程序员，你会熟悉 pull request，就是 pull request，它们像是一种原子工作单元。
cues.en: And if we go into the details of the benchmark, so SWE-bench is basically… Since you’re a programmer, you’ll be familiar with pull requests, and just pull requests, they’re like a sort of atomic unit of work.

cues.zh: 你可以说我在实现一件事。
cues.en: You could say I’m implementing one thing.

cues.zh: SWE-bench 其实给你一个真实世界的场景：代码库处于当前状态，而我要实现用自然语言描述的东西。
cues.en: So SWE-bench actually gives you a real world situation where the code base is in a current state and I’m trying to implement something that’s described in language.

cues.zh: 我们有内部基准测试来衡量同样的事情，你说：“就让模型自由发挥，运行任何东西，编辑任何东西。
cues.en: We have internal benchmarks where we measure the same thing and you say, “Just give the model free rein to do anything, run anything, edit anything.

cues.zh: 它能多好地完成这些任务？”正是这个基准测试从“它能做到3%的时候”变成了“它能做到大约50%的时候”。
cues.en: How well is it able to complete these tasks?” And it’s that benchmark that’s gone from “it can do it 3% of the time” to “it can do it about 50% of the time.”

cues.zh: 所以我确实相信你可以获得基准测试的提升，但我认为如果我们能以不过度训练或针对那个特定基准测试作弊的方式达到100%，那可能代表着编程能力真实而显著的提升。
cues.en: So I actually do believe that you can gain benchmarks, but I think if we get to 100% on that benchmark in a way that isn’t over-trained or game for that particular benchmark, probably represents a real and serious increase in programming ability.

cues.zh: 我猜想，如果能达到90%、95%，那就意味着它能自主完成相当一部分软件工程任务。
cues.en: And I would suspect that if we can get to 90, 95% that it will represent ability to autonomously do a significant fraction of software engineering tasks.

cues.zh: 好，这是个荒谬的时间线问题。
cues.en: Well, ridiculous timeline question.

cues.zh: Claude Opus 3.5什么时候出？
cues.en: When is Claude Opus 3.5 coming up?

cues.zh: 不给确切日期，但据我们所知，计划仍然是有Claude 3.5 Opus。
cues.en: Not giving you an exact date, but as far as we know, the plan is still to have a Claude 3.5 Opus.

cues.zh: 我们会在GTA 6之前拿到它吗，还是不会？
cues.en: Are we going to get it before GTA 6 or no?

cues.zh: 像《永远的毁灭公爵》那样？
cues.en: Like Duke Nukem Forever?

cues.zh: 毁灭公爵。
cues.en: Duke Nukem.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 那是什么游戏来着？
cues.en: What was that game?

cues.zh: 有个游戏跳票了15年。
cues.en: There was some game that was delayed 15 years.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: That’s right.

cues.zh: 是《永远的毁灭公爵》吗？
cues.en: Was that Duke Nukem Forever?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得GTA现在才刚开始发预告片。
cues.en: And I think GTA is now just releasing trailers.

cues.zh: 我们发布第一代Sonnet才过了三个月。
cues.en: It’s only been three months since we released the first Sonnet.

cues.zh: 是啊，这发布节奏太惊人了。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s the incredible pace of release.

cues.zh: 这就说明了节奏，以及人们对发布时间的预期。
cues.en: It just tells you about the pace, the expectations for when things are going to come out.
So what about 4.0?

cues.zh: 那么，随着这些模型越来越大，你怎么看待版本管理，以及一般的版本命名方式？为什么 Sonnet 3.5 要加上日期更新？
cues.en: So how do you think, as these models get bigger and bigger, about versioning and also just versioning in general, why Sonnet 3.5 updated with the date?

cues.zh: 为什么不叫 Sonnet 3.6？很多人都是这么叫的。
cues.en: Why not Sonnet 3.6, which a lot of people are calling it?

cues.zh: 命名其实是个挺有意思的挑战，对吧？
cues.en: Naming is actually an interesting challenge here, right?

cues.zh: 因为我觉得一年前，模型的大部分工作还是预训练。
cues.en: Because I think a year ago, most of the model was pre-training.

cues.zh: 所以你可以从头开始，直接说：“好，我们要做不同规模的模型。
cues.en: And so you could start from the beginning and just say, “Okay, we’re going to have models of different sizes.

cues.zh: 我们会把它们一起训练，建立一套命名体系，然后给它们加点新东西，就有了下一代。”
cues.en: We’re going to train them all together and we’ll have a family of naming schemes and then we’ll put some new magic into them and then we’ll have the next generation.”

cues.zh: 麻烦在于，有些模型训练时间比其他模型长得多。
cues.en: The trouble starts already when some of them take a lot longer than others to train.

cues.zh: 这就已经有点打乱你的时间安排了。
cues.en: That already messes up your time a little bit.

cues.zh: 但随着你在预训练上取得巨大进步，你会突然发现：“哦，我能做出更好的预训练模型了。”而且这不需要花很长时间，但显然它和之前模型的规模和形态是一样的。
cues.en: But as you make big improvement in pre-training, then you suddenly notice, “Oh, I can make better pre-train model.” And that doesn’t take very long to do, but clearly it has the same size and shape of previous models.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这两者加在一起，再加上时机问题。
cues.en: So I think those two together as well as the timing issues.

cues.zh: 不管你想出什么样的方案，现实往往会让这个方案受挫，对吧？
cues.en: Any kind of scheme you come up with, the reality tends to frustrate that scheme, right?

cues.zh: 它往往会突破这个方案的框架。
cues.en: It tends to break out of the scheme.

cues.zh: 它不像软件那样，你可以说：“哦，这是3.7，这是3.8。”不是的，你的模型有不同的权衡取舍。
cues.en: It’s not like software where you can say, “Oh, this is 3.7, this is 3.8.” No, you have models with different trade-offs.

cues.zh: 你可以改变模型中的一些东西，也可以改变另一些东西。
cues.en: You can change some things in your models, you can change other things.

cues.zh: 有些在推理时更快，有些更慢。
cues.en: Some are faster and slower at inference.

cues.zh: 有些成本更高，有些成本更低。
cues.en: Some have to be more expensive, some have to be less expensive.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得所有公司都在这个问题上挣扎过。
cues.en: And so I think all the companies have struggled with this.

cues.zh: 我觉得在命名方面我们当时处境不错，有 Haiku、Sonnet 和 Opus。
cues.en: I think we were in a good position in terms of naming when we had Haiku, Sonnet and Opus.

cues.zh: 那是个非常好的开端。
cues.en: It was great, great start.

cues.zh: 我们努力维持它，但并不完美，所以会试着回归简洁。
cues.en: We’re trying to maintain it, but it’s not perfect, so we’ll try and get back to the simplicity.

cues.zh: 但就这个领域的本质而言，我觉得没人搞定了命名这件事。
cues.en: But just the nature of the field, I feel like no one’s figured out naming.

cues.zh: 它某种程度上和普通软件是不同的范式，所以没有哪家公司在这方面做到完美。
cues.en: It’s somehow a different paradigm from normal software and so none of the companies have been perfect at it.

cues.zh: 这件事我们挣扎的程度出奇地大，相比训练模型这门宏大科学来说它本该微不足道。
cues.en: It’s something we struggle with surprisingly much relative to how trivial it is for the grand science of training the models.

cues.zh: 所以从用户角度看，更新版 Sonnet 3.5 的用户体验就是和之前 2024 年 6 月的 Sonnet 3.5 不一样。
cues.en: So from the user side, the user experience of the updated Sonnet 3.5 is just different than the previous June 2024 Sonnet 3.5.

cues.zh: 要是能想出某种标签体系来体现这一点就好了。
cues.en: It would be nice to come up with some kind of labeling that embodies that.

cues.zh: 因为大家都在说 Sonnet 3.5，但现在又出了个不一样的版本。
cues.en: Because people talk about Sonnet 3.5, but now there’s a different one.

cues.zh: 那当新旧版本有明显提升时，你怎么区分指代旧版和新版呢？
cues.en: And so how do you refer to the previous one and the new one when there’s a distinct improvement?

cues.zh: 这让相关讨论变得很困难。
cues.en: It just makes conversation about it just challenging.

cues.zh: 是啊，是啊。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 我确实认为，模型的很多特性并没有体现在基准测试里。
cues.en: I definitely think this question of there are lots of properties of the models that are not reflected in the benchmarks.

cues.zh: 我觉得这肯定是事实，大家也都认同。
cues.en: I think that’s definitely the case and everyone agrees.

cues.zh: 而且并非所有特性都是能力层面的。
cues.en: And not all of them are capabilities.

cues.zh: 模型可以礼貌也可以唐突，可以很主动回应也可以反问你问题。
cues.en: Models can be polite or brusque, they can be very reactive or they can ask you questions.

cues.zh: 它们可以有让人觉得温暖的个性，也可以有冷漠的个性。
cues.en: They can have what feels like a warm personality or a cold personality.

cues.zh: 它们可以很无聊，也可以像 Golden Gate Claude 那样非常有辨识度。
cues.en: They can be boring or they can be very distinctive like Golden Gate Claude was.

cues.zh: 我们有一整个团队专门负责，我想我们称之为Claude character。
cues.en: And we have a whole team focused on, I think we call it Claude character.

cues.zh: Amanda领导那个团队，我们会跟你聊这个，但这仍然是一门非常不精确的科学，我们经常发现模型有一些我们不知道的特性。
cues.en: Amanda leads that team and we’ll talk to you about that, but it’s still a very inexact science and often we find that models have properties that we’re not aware of.

cues.zh: 事实是，你可以和一个模型交谈一万次，但有些行为你可能就是看不到，就像和人一样，对吧？
cues.en: The fact of the matter is that you can talk to a model 10,000 times and there are some behaviors you might not see just like with a human, right?

cues.zh: 我可能认识一个人几个月，却不知道他们有某种技能，或者不知道他们有某一面。
cues.en: I can know someone for a few months and not know that they have a certain skill or not know that there’s a certain side to them.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得我们只能习惯这个想法。
cues.en: And so I think we just have to get used to this idea.

cues.zh: 我们一直在寻找更好的方法来测试我们的模型，以展示这些能力，也决定我们希望模型拥有哪些个性特征，哪些不希望拥有。
cues.en: And we’re always looking for better ways of testing our models to demonstrate these capabilities and also to decide which are the personality properties we want models to have and which we don’t want to have.

cues.zh: 规范性问题本身也非常有意思。
cues.en: That itself, the normative question, is also super interesting.

cues.zh: 我得问你一个来自 Reddit 的问题。
cues.en: I got to ask you a question from Reddit.

cues.zh: 来自 Reddit？
cues.en: From Reddit?

cues.zh: 哦，天哪。
cues.en: Oh, boy.

cues.zh: 至少对我来说，这是一种非常迷人的心理社会现象，人们反映 Claude 随着时间推移对他们来说变笨了。
cues.en: There’s just this fascinating, to me at least, it’s a psychological social phenomenon where people report that Claude has gotten dumber for them over time.

cues.zh: 所以问题是，用户对 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 变笨的抱怨到底有没有道理？
cues.en: And so the question is, does the user complaint about the dumbing down of Claude 3.5 Sonnet hold any water?

cues.zh: 那么这些轶事性的报告是一种社会现象，还是说确实存在 Claude 会变笨的情况？
cues.en: So are these anecdotal reports a kind of social phenomena or is there any cases where Claude would get dumber?

cues.zh: 所以这其实并不适用。
cues.en: So this actually doesn’t apply.

cues.zh: 这不只是关于 Claude。
cues.en: This isn’t just about Claude.

cues.zh: 我相信每一家大型公司生产的每个基础模型都有过这类抱怨。
cues.en: I believe I’ve seen these complaints for every foundation model produced by a major company.

cues.zh: 人们这样说过 GPT-4，也这样说过 GPT-4 Turbo。
cues.en: People said this about GPT-4, they said it about GPT-4 Turbo.

cues.zh: 所以有几点。
cues.en: So a couple things.

cues.zh: 第一，模型的实际权重，也就是模型真正的大脑，除非我们推出新模型，否则是不会变的。
cues.en: One, the actual weights of the model, the actual brain of the model, that does not change unless we introduce a new model.

cues.zh: 有很多原因说明，随机替换成新版本的模型在实际操作中根本说不通。
cues.en: There are just a number of reasons why it would not make sense practically to be randomly substituting in new versions of the model.

cues.zh: 从推理的角度来说这很难，而且实际上很难控制改变模型权重带来的所有后果。
cues.en: It’s difficult from an inference perspective and it’s actually hard to control all the consequences of changing the weights of the model.

cues.zh: 比如说你想微调模型，让它少说“certainly”，旧版 Sonnet 以前就爱这么说。
cues.en: Let’s say you wanted to fine-tune the model, I don’t know, to say “certainly” less, which an old version of Sonnet used to do.

cues.zh: 结果你实际上会连带改变一百样东西。
cues.en: You actually end up changing 100 things as well.

cues.zh: 所以我们有一整套流程，也有一整套修改模型的流程。
cues.en: So we have a whole process for it and we have a whole process for modifying the model.

cues.zh: 我们会做大量测试。
cues.en: We do a bunch of testing on it.

cues.zh: 我们会在早期客户中做大量用户测试。
cues.en: We do a bunch of user testing in early customers.

cues.zh: 所以我们俩都从未在未告知任何人的情况下更改过模型的权重。
cues.en: So we both have never changed the weights of the model without telling anyone.

cues.zh: 当然，在目前的设置下，那样做也没有意义。
cues.en: And certainly, in the current setup, it would not make sense to do that.

cues.zh: 不过，有几件事我们偶尔会做。
cues.en: Now, there are a couple things that we do occasionally do.

cues.zh: 一是有时我们会进行 A/B 测试，但通常是在模型即将发布时，而且只持续很短的时间。
cues.en: One is sometimes we run A/B tests, but those are typically very close to when a model is being released and for a very small fraction of time.

cues.zh: 所以在新 Sonnet 3.5 发布前一天，我同意我们本该取个更好的名字。
cues.en: So the day before the new Sonnet 3.5, I agree we should have had a better name.

cues.zh: 用这个名字说起来很拗口。
cues.en: It’s clunky to refer to it.

cues.zh: 有些人评论说它变得好多了，那是因为在那一天或两天里，有一部分人接触到了 A/B 测试。
cues.en: There were some comments from people that it’s gotten a lot better and that’s because a fraction we’re exposed to an A/B test for those one or two days.

cues.zh: 另一件事是，系统提示偶尔会发生变化。
cues.en: The other is that occasionally the system prompt will change.

cues.zh: 系统提示词确实可能产生一些影响，虽然不太可能让模型变笨，但也不太可能让它们变得更笨。
cues.en: The system prompt can have some effects, although it’s unlikely to dumb down models, it’s unlikely to make them dumber.

cues.zh: 我们观察到，虽然我列出的这两件事——为了全面起见——发生得相当少，但对我们和其他模型公司关于模型变化的抱怨却很多：模型不擅长这个、模型审查变多了、模型被降智了。
cues.en: And we’ve seen that while these two things, which I’m listing to be very complete, happened quite infrequently, the complaints for us and for other model companies about the model change, the model isn’t good at this, the model got more censored, the model was dumbed down.

cues.zh: 这些抱怨一直存在，所以我不想说人们在凭空想象之类的，但大多数情况下，模型并没有在变。
cues.en: Those complaints are constant and so I don’t want to say people are imagining it or anything, but the models are, for the most part, not changing.

cues.zh: 如果要提出一个理论，我觉得这其实和我之前说过的一点有关，那就是模型非常复杂，有很多方面。
cues.en: If I were to offer a theory, I think it actually relates to one of the things I said before, which is that models are very complex and have many aspects to them.

cues.zh: 所以经常出现的情况是，如果我问模型一个问题，比如我说“做任务X”和“你能做任务X吗？”，模型的回答方式可能不一样。
cues.en: And so often, if I ask the model a question, if I’m like, “Do task X” versus, “Can you do task X?” the model might respond in different ways.

cues.zh: 所以，你和模型交互的方式中有各种微妙之处，稍作改变就可能带来截然不同的结果。
cues.en: And so there are all kinds of subtle things that you can change about the way you interact with the model that can give you very different results.

cues.zh: 说白了，模型常常对措辞的细微变化很敏感，这本身是我们和其他模型提供商的失败之处。
cues.en: To be clear, this itself is like a failing by us and by the other model providers that the models are just often sensitive to small changes in wording.

cues.zh: 这也是又一个例子，说明关于这些模型如何运作的科学还非常不成熟。
cues.en: It’s yet another way in which the science of how these models work is very poorly developed.

cues.zh: 所以，如果我某天晚上睡觉前用某种方式和模型对话，然后稍微改变了跟模型说话的措辞，就可能得到不同的结果。
cues.en: And so if I go to sleep one night and I was talking to the model in a certain way and I slightly changed the phrasing of how I talk to the model, I could get different results.

cues.zh: 所以这是一种可能的方式。
cues.en: So that’s one possible way.

cues.zh: 另一件事是，天哪，这些东西真的很难量化。
cues.en: The other thing is, man, it’s just hard to quantify this stuff.

cues.zh: 这些东西很难量化。
cues.en: It’s hard to quantify this stuff.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们在新模型发布时非常兴奋，但随着时间推移，他们会越来越清楚地意识到这些模型的局限性。
cues.en: I think people are very excited by new models when they come out and then as time goes on, they become very aware of their limitations.

cues.zh: 所以那可能是另一种效应，但啰嗦了半天，我想说的主要是：除了少数很窄的例外，模型基本没变。
cues.en: So that may be another effect, but that’s all a very long-winded way of saying for the most part, with some fairly narrow exceptions, the models are not changing.

cues.zh: 我觉得有一种心理效应。
cues.en: I think there is a psychological effect.

cues.zh: 你慢慢就习惯了，基准线被抬高了。
cues.en: You just start getting used to it, the baseline raises.

cues.zh: 人们第一次在飞机上用上 Wi-Fi 时，觉得太神奇了，简直是魔法。
cues.en: When people who have first gotten Wi-Fi on airplanes, it’s amazing, magic.

cues.zh: 太神奇了。
cues.en: It’s amazing.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 然后你就开始——
cues.en: And then you start-

cues.zh: 现在我却想：“这玩意儿怎么都用不了。
cues.en: And now I’m like, “I can’t get this thing to work.

cues.zh: 真是垃圾。”
cues.en: This is such a piece of crap.”

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Exactly.

cues.zh: 所以很容易产生阴谋论：“他们让 Wi-Fi 越来越慢。”这大概是我要跟 Amanda 多聊的话题，但 Reddit 上还有个问题：“Claude 什么时候才能不再像个纯粹的触手祖母，把它的道德世界观强加给我这个付费用户？”
cues.en: So it’s easy to have the conspiracy theory of, “They’re making Wi-Fi slower and slower.” This is probably something I’ll talk to Amanda much more about, but another Reddit question, “When will Claude stop trying to be my pure tentacle grandmother imposing its moral worldview on me as a paying customer?

cues.zh: 还有，让 Claude 过度道歉背后的心理机制是什么？这从另一个角度反映了那种挫败感。
cues.en: And also, what is the psychology behind making Claude overly apologetic?” So this reports about the experience, a different angle on the frustration.

cues.zh: 这和角色设定有关 [听不清 00:47:06]。
cues.en: It has to do with the character [inaudible 00:47:06].

cues.zh: 好，关于这点先说几点。
cues.en: Yeah, so a couple points on this first.

cues.zh: 第一，人们在 Reddit、Twitter 或 X 等平台上说的话，其实和用户真正在统计意义上关心的、促使他们使用模型的东西之间，存在巨大的分布差异。
cues.en: One is things that people say on Reddit and Twitter or X or whatever it is, there’s actually a huge distribution shift between the stuff that people complain loudly about on social media and what actually statistically users care about and that drives people to use the models.

cues.zh: 人们会为模型没写出全部代码、或者代码能力没达到本可以达到的水平而沮丧，尽管它已经是世界上代码能力最强的模型了。
cues.en: People are frustrated with things like the model not writing out all the code or the model just not being as good at code as it could be, even though it’s the best model in the world on code.

cues.zh: 我觉得大部分问题都跟这个有关，但确实有一小部分人提出了这些担忧，他们对模型拒绝本不该拒绝的事情感到沮丧，或者模型道歉太多，或者只是有这些烦人的口头禅。
cues.en: I think the majority of things are about that, but certainly a vocal minority raise these concerns, are frustrated by the model refusing things that it shouldn’t refuse or apologizing too much or just having these annoying verbal tics.

cues.zh: 第二个注意事项，我想说得非常清楚，因为我觉得有些人不知道这一点，另一些人知道但忘了。
cues.en: The second caveat, and I just want to say this super clearly because I think some people don’t know it, others know it, but forget it.

cues.zh: 要全面控制模型的行为是非常困难的。
cues.en: It is very difficult to control across the board how the models behave.

cues.zh: 你不能直接伸手进去说：“哦，我想让模型少道歉。”你可以这么做。
cues.en: You cannot just reach in there and say, “Oh, I want the model to apologize less.” You can do that.

cues.zh: 你可以加入训练数据说：“哦，模型应该少道歉。”但然后在其他情况下，它们最终会变得超级粗鲁或过度自信，从而误导人们。
cues.en: You can include training data that says, “Oh, the model should apologize less.” But then in some other situation, they end up being super rude or overconfident in a way that’s misleading people.

cues.zh: 所以这些都是权衡取舍。
cues.en: So there are all these trade-offs.

cues.zh: 比如，另一件事是，曾经有一段时间，模型——我们的模型，我想其他家的也是——太啰嗦了，会重复自己，说太多。
cues.en: For example, another thing is if there was a period during which models, ours and I think others as well, were too verbose, they would repeat themselves, they would say too much.

cues.zh: 你可以通过惩罚模型说话太长来减少啰嗦。
cues.en: You can cut down on the verbosity by penalizing the models for just talking for too long.

cues.zh: 这样做的时候，如果做得粗糙，模型在写代码时有时会说：“剩下的代码放这里”，对吧？
cues.en: What happens when you do that, if you do it in a crude way, is when the models are coding, sometimes they’ll say, “Rest of the code goes here,” right?

cues.zh: 因为它们学会了这是节省的方式，而且它们看到了这一点。
cues.en: Because they’ve learned that that’s the way to economize and that they see it.

cues.zh: 于是这就导致模型在写代码时所谓的“偷懒”，它们就像：“啊，剩下的你可以自己补完。”这不是因为我们想省算力，也不是因为模型在寒假偷懒，或者任何其他冒出来的阴谋论。
cues.en: And then so that leads the model to be so-called lazy in coding where they’re just like, “Ah, you can finish the rest of it.” It’s not because we want to save on compute or because the models are lazy during winter break or any of the other conspiracy theories that have come up.

cues.zh: 其实，要控制模型的行为非常困难，要同时在所有情况下引导模型的行为更是难上加难。
cues.en: Actually, it’s just very hard to control the behavior of the model, to steer the behavior of the model in all circumstances at once.

cues.zh: 这就像打地鼠一样，你压住一个地方，其他地方就开始动，而你甚至可能没有注意到或测量到。
cues.en: There’s this whack- a-mole aspect where you push on one thing and these other things start to move as well that you may not even notice or measure.

cues.zh: 所以我如此关心未来这些AI系统的宏大对齐问题，其中一个原因其实是，这些系统实际上相当不可预测。
cues.en: And so one of the reasons that I care so much about grand alignment of these AI systems in the future is actually, these systems are actually quite unpredictable.

cues.zh: 它们实际上很难被引导和控制。
cues.en: They’re actually quite hard to steer and control.

cues.zh: 而我们现在看到的这个版本——你让一件事变好，另一件事就变糟——我认为这就是未来AI系统控制问题在当下的类比，我们可以从今天就开始研究它。
cues.en: And this version we’re seeing today of you make one thing better, it makes another thing worse, I think that’s like a present day analog of future control problems in AI systems that we can start to study today.

cues.zh: 我觉得难点在于引导行为，确保当我们把 AI 系统往一个方向推时，它不会在其他方面往我们不想要的方向偏。
cues.en: I think that difficulty in steering the behavior and making sure that if we push an AI system in one direction, it doesn’t push it in another direction in some other ways that we didn’t want.

cues.zh: 我觉得这是未来的早期信号。如果我们能很好地解决这个问题——你让模型制造和传播天花，它说不，但它愿意帮你上研究生病毒学课程——我们怎么同时做到这两点？
cues.en: I think that’s an early sign of things to come, and if we can do a good job of solving this problem of you ask the model to make and distribute smallpox and it says no, but it’s willing to help you in your graduate level virology class, how do we get both of those things at once?

cues.zh: 这很难。
cues.en: It’s hard.

cues.zh: 很容易偏向一边或另一边，而这是一个多维问题。
cues.en: It’s very easy to go to one side or the other and it’s a multidimensional problem.

cues.zh: 所以我认为塑造模型个性这些问题非常难。
cues.en: And so I think these questions of shaping the model’s personality, I think they’re very hard.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们在这方面做得并不完美。
cues.en: I think we haven’t done perfectly on them.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们实际上比所有 AI 公司都做得好，但离完美还很远。
cues.en: I think we’ve actually done the best of all the AI companies, but still so far from perfect.

cues.zh: 我认为，如果我们能把这件事做对，如果能在当下这个高度受控的环境中控制好误报和漏报，那么未来我们就会做得更好，因为那时我们担心的是：模型会不会变得超级自主？
cues.en: And I think if we can get this right, if we can control the false positives and false negatives in this very controlled present day environment, we’ll be much better at doing it for the future when our worry is: will the models be super autonomous?

cues.zh: 它们会不会做出非常危险的事情？
cues.en: Will they be able to make very dangerous things?

cues.zh: 它们能不能自主建立整个公司，而这些公司是否对齐？
cues.en: Will they be able to autonomously build whole companies and are those companies aligned?

cues.zh: 所以我觉得当前这项任务既令人头疼，也是为未来做的好练习。
cues.en: So I think of this present task as both vexing but also good practice for the future.

cues.zh: 目前收集用户反馈的最佳方式是什么？
cues.en: What’s the current best way of gathering user feedback?

cues.zh: 不是轶事数据，而是关于痛点或反面——积极方面等的大规模数据？
cues.en: Not anecdotal data, but just large-scale data about pain points or the opposite of pain points, positive things, so on?

cues.zh: 是内部测试吗？
cues.en: Is it internal testing?

cues.zh: 是特定群体测试、A/B 测试吗？
cues.en: Is it a specific group testing, A/B testing?

cues.zh: 哪些做法有效？
cues.en: What works?

cues.zh: 通常，我们会进行内部模型测试，Anthropic 全体员工……Anthropic 有近 1000 人。
cues.en: So typically, we’ll have internal model bashings where all of Anthropic… Anthropic is almost 1,000 people.

cues.zh: 大家就试着攻破模型。
cues.en: People just try and break the model.

cues.zh: 他们尝试用各种方式与模型互动。
cues.en: They try and interact with it various ways.

cues.zh: 我们有一套评估标准，用来检查：“哦，模型是不是在以不该有的方式拒绝回答？”我记得甚至有个“certainly”评估，因为之前模型有个烦人的毛病，就是对各种问题都回答：“当然，我可以帮您解决。
cues.en: We have a suite of evals for, “Oh, is the model refusing in ways that it couldn’t?” I think we even had a “certainly” eval because again, at one point, the model had this problem where it had this annoying tick where it would respond to a wide range of questions by saying, “Certainly, I can help you with that.

cues.zh: 当然，我很乐意去做。
cues.en: Certainly, I would be happy to do that.

cues.zh: 当然，这是正确的。”
cues.en: Certainly, this is correct.”

cues.zh: 于是我们做了个“certainly”评估，就是看模型多久会说一次“certainly”？
cues.en: And so we had a “certainly” eval, which is: how often does the model say certainly?

cues.zh: 但你看，这就像打地鼠游戏。
cues.en: But look, this is just a whack-a-mole.

cues.zh: 如果它从“certainly”换成“definitely”怎么办？
cues.en: What if it switches from “certainly” to “definitely”?

cues.zh: 所以每次我们新增一个评估，同时还要一直针对所有旧项目做评估，这类评估有几百个，但我们发现，没有什么能替代真人亲自与模型互动。
cues.en: So every time we add a new eval and we’re always evaluating for all the old things, we have hundreds of these evaluations, but we find that there’s no substitute for a human interacting with it.

cues.zh: 所以这非常像普通的产品开发流程。
cues.en: And so it’s very much like the ordinary product development process.

cues.zh: Anthropic 内部有几百人反复测试这个模型。
cues.en: We have hundreds of people within Anthropic bash the model.

cues.zh: 然后我们做外部 A/B 测试。
cues.en: Then we do external A/B tests.

cues.zh: 有时我们会和外包人员一起跑测试。
cues.en: Sometimes we’ll run tests with contractors.

cues.zh: 我们付钱给外包人员，让他们与模型互动。
cues.en: We pay contractors to interact with the model.

cues.zh: 把这些都加在一起，仍然不完美。
cues.en: So you put all of these things together and it’s still not perfect.

cues.zh: 你还是会看到一些你不太想看到的行为。
cues.en: You still see behaviors that you don’t quite want to see.

cues.zh: 你还是会看到模型拒绝一些根本没道理拒绝的东西。
cues.en: You still see the model refusing things that it just doesn’t make sense to refuse.

cues.zh: 但我认为，努力解决这个挑战，努力阻止模型去做那些大家都认同它不该做的真正恶劣的事，大家都认同模型不该谈论，比如说，儿童虐待材料。
cues.en: But I think trying to solve this challenge, trying to stop the model from doing genuinely bad things that everyone agrees it shouldn’t do, everyone agrees that the model shouldn’t talk about, I don’t know, child abuse material.

cues.zh: 大家都同意模型不该那么做，但同时也不该用那些愚蠢笨拙的方式拒绝。
cues.en: Everyone agrees the model shouldn’t do that, but at the same time, that it doesn’t refuse in these dumb and stupid ways.

cues.zh: 我觉得尽可能精细地划出那条线、趋近完美，仍然是挑战，我们每天都在进步，但还有很多问题要解决。
cues.en: I think drawing that line as finely as possible, approaching perfectly, is still a challenge and we’re getting better at it every day, but there’s a lot to be solved.

cues.zh: 还是那句话，我把这看作一个信号：在驾驭更强大模型方面，前面还有挑战。
cues.en: And again, I would point to that as an indicator of a challenge ahead in terms of steering much more powerful models.

cues.zh: 你觉得 Claude 4.0 还会出吗？
cues.en: Do you think Claude 4.0 is ever coming out?

cues.zh: 我不想敲定任何命名方案，因为如果我在这儿说“明年我们会推出 Claude 4”，然后我们又决定因为出现了新类型的模型应该从头开始，我不想把话说死。
cues.en: I don’t want to commit to any naming scheme because if I say here, “We’re going to have Claude 4 next year,” and then we decide that we should start over because there’s a new type of model, I don’t want to commit to it.

cues.zh: 按正常的业务节奏，我预期 Claude 4 会在 Claude 3 之后推出。
cues.en: I would expect in a normal course of business that Claude 4 would come after Claude 3.

cues.zh: 5，但在这个古怪的领域里，你永远说不准。
cues.en: 5, but you never know in this wacky field.

cues.zh: 但这种扩展的理念还在继续。
cues.en: But this idea of scaling is continuing.

cues.zh: 扩展还在继续。
cues.en: Scaling is continuing.

cues.zh: 我们一定会推出比现有模型更强大的模型。
cues.en: There will definitely be more powerful models coming from us than the models that exist today.

cues.zh: 这是肯定的。
cues.en: That is certain.

cues.zh: 如果没有，那我们作为一家公司就彻底失败了。
cues.en: Or if there aren’t, we’ve deeply failed as a company.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下负责任扩展政策和AI安全等级标准，也就是ASL等级吗？
cues.en: Can you explain the responsible scaling policy and the AI safety level standards, ASL levels?

cues.zh: 尽管我对这些模型的好处感到兴奋——如果我们谈到《慈爱的机器》，我们会聊到这一点——但我担心风险，并且我一直担心风险。
cues.en: As much as I am excited about the benefits of these models, and we’ll talk about that if we talk about Machines of Loving Grace, I’m worried about the risks and I continue to be worried about the risks.

cues.zh: 任何人都不应该认为《慈爱的机器》是我在说我不再担心这些模型的风险了。
cues.en: No one should think that Machines of Loving Grace was me saying I’m no longer worried about the risks of these models.

cues.zh: 我认为它们是同一枚硬币的两面。
cues.en: I think they’re two sides of the same coin.

cues.zh: 模型的能力，以及它们解决生物学、神经科学、经济发展、治理与和平、经济大部分领域所有这些问题的能力，也伴随着风险，对吧？
cues.en: The power of the models and their ability to solve all these problems in biology, neuroscience, economic development, governance and peace, large parts of the economy, those come with risks as well, right?

cues.zh: 能力越大，责任越大。
cues.en: With great power comes great responsibility.

cues.zh: 这两者是相伴而生的。
cues.en: The two are paired.

cues.zh: 强大的东西既能做好事，也能做坏事。
cues.en: Things that are powerful can do good things and they can do bad things.

cues.zh: 我认为这些风险可以分为几个不同的类别，也许我考虑最多的两个最大风险。
cues.en: I think of those risks as being in several different categories, perhaps the two biggest risks that I think about.

cues.zh: 这并不是说今天没有重要的风险，但当我想到真正会在最大规模上发生的事情时，一个是我所说的灾难性滥用。
cues.en: And that’s not to say that there aren’t risks today that are important, but when I think of really the things that would happen on the grandest scale, one is what I call catastrophic misuse.

cues.zh: 这些是模型在网络、生物、放射、核等领域被滥用，如果真的出了大问题，可能伤害甚至杀死数千人，甚至数百万人。
cues.en: These are misuse of the models in domains like cyber, bio, radiological, nuclear, things that could harm or even kill thousands, even millions of people if they really, really go wrong.

cues.zh: 这些是首要防止的事项。
cues.en: These are the number one priority to prevent.

cues.zh: 这里我只想做一个简单的观察：如果看看当今世界上做过真正坏事的人，我认为人类实际上一直受到保护，因为真正聪明、受过良好教育的人与想干极其可怕事情的人之间的重叠通常很小。
cues.en: And here I would just make a simple observation, which is that the models, if I look today at people who have done really bad things in the world, I think actually humanity has been protected by the fact that the overlap between really smart, well-educated people and people who want to do really horrific things has generally been small.

cues.zh: 假设我是这个领域的博士，有一份高薪工作。
cues.en: Let’s say I’m someone who I have a PhD in this field, I have a well-paying job.

cues.zh: 有太多东西可以失去。
cues.en: There’s so much to lose.

cues.zh: 即使假设我完全邪恶——而大多数人并非如此——这样的人为什么要冒着生命危险、冒着毁掉遗产和声誉的风险，去做真正、真正邪恶的事情？
cues.en: Even assuming I’m completely evil, which most people are not, why would such a person risk their life, risk their legacy, their reputation to do something truly, truly evil?

cues.zh: 如果我们有更多这样的人，世界会变得更加危险。
