cues.en: If we had a lot more people like that, the world would be a much more dangerous place.

cues.zh: 所以我担心的是，作为一个智能得多的智能体，AI可能会打破这种相关性。
cues.en: And so my worry is that by being a much more intelligent agent, AI could break that correlation.

cues.zh: 所以我确实对此有严重的担忧。
cues.en: And so I do have serious worries about that.

cues.zh: 我相信我们能防止这些担忧。
cues.en: I believe we can prevent those worries.

cues.zh: 但我想作为对《爱与恩典的机器》的反驳，我要说仍然存在严重的风险。
cues.en: But I think as a counterpoint to Machines of Loving Grace, I want to say that there’s still serious risks.

cues.zh: 第二类风险是自主性风险，也就是模型可能会自行其是，尤其是当我们赋予它们比以往更多的自主权，尤其是当我们让它们监督更广泛的任务，比如编写整个代码库，或者有朝一日甚至有效地运营整个公司时，它们就被放得太松了。
cues.en: And the second range of risks would be the autonomy risks, which is the idea that models might, on their own, particularly as we give them more agency than they’ve had in the past, particularly as we give them supervision over wider tasks like writing whole code bases or someday even effectively operating entire companies, they’re on a long enough leash.

cues.zh: 它们在做我们真正想让它们做的事吗？
cues.en: Are they doing what we really want them to do?

cues.zh: 甚至很难详细理解它们在做什么，更不用说控制它了。
cues.en: It’s very difficult to even understand in detail what they’re doing, let alone control it.

cues.zh: 就像我说的，这些早期迹象表明，很难完美划清模型该做和不该做的事之间的界限。偏向一边，会得到烦人又无用的东西；偏向另一边，又会出现其他行为。
cues.en: And like I said, these early signs that it’s hard to perfectly draw the boundary between things the model should do and things the model shouldn’t do that if you go to one side, you get things that are annoying and useless and you go to the other side, you get other behaviors.

cues.zh: 解决一个问题，又会制造其他问题。
cues.en: If you fix one thing, it creates other problems.

cues.zh: 我们在这方面越来越擅长了。
cues.en: We’re getting better and better at solving this.

cues.zh: 我不认为这是个无解的问题。
cues.en: I don’t think this is an unsolvable problem.

cues.zh: 我认为这是一门科学，就像飞机安全、汽车安全或药物安全一样。
cues.en: I think this is a science like the safety of airplanes or the safety of cars or the safety of drugs.

cues.zh: 我不认为我们遗漏了什么重大的东西。
cues.en: I don’t think there’s any big thing we’re missing.

cues.zh: 我只是觉得我们需要更擅长控制这些模型。
cues.en: I just think we need to get better at controlling these models.

cues.zh: 这就是我担心的两个风险。
cues.en: And so these are the two risks I’m worried about.

cues.zh: 而我们的负责任扩展计划——我承认，这是对你问题一个非常冗长的回答。
cues.en: And our responsible scaling plan, which I’ll recognize is a very long-winded answer to your question.

cues.zh: 我很喜欢。
cues.en: I love it.

cues.zh: 我很喜欢。
cues.en: I love it.

cues.zh: 我们的负责任扩展计划旨在应对这两类风险。
cues.en: Our responsible scaling plan is designed to address these two types of risks.

cues.zh: 所以每次开发新模型时，我们基本上都会测试它做这两类坏事的能力。
cues.en: And so every time we develop a new model, we basically test it for its ability to do both of these bad things.

cues.zh: 稍微往回退一点说，我认为AI系统有个有趣的困境：它们还不够强大，不足以造成这些灾难。
cues.en: So if I were to back up a little bit, I think we have an interesting dilemma with AI systems where they’re not yet powerful enough to present these catastrophes.

cues.zh: 我不知道它们是否真的会造成这些灾难。
cues.en: I don’t know if they’ll ever present these catastrophes.

cues.zh: 有可能不会。
cues.en: It’s possible they won’t.

cues.zh: 但担忧的理由、风险的理由足够充分，我们应该现在就行动，而且它们进步得非常非常快。
cues.en: But the case for worry, the case for risk is strong enough that we should act now and they’re getting better very, very fast.

cues.zh: 我在参议院作证时说，我们可能在两到三年内面临严重的生物风险。
cues.en: I testified in the Senate that we might have serious bio risks within two to three years.

cues.zh: 那是大约一年前的事了。
cues.en: That was about a year ago.

cues.zh: 事情进展得很快。
cues.en: Things have proceeded apace.

cues.zh: 我们面临这样一个情况：要应对这些风险出奇地难，因为它们今天还不存在。
cues.en: So we have this thing where it’s surprisingly hard to address these risks because they’re not here today, they don’t exist.

cues.zh: 它们就像幽灵，但正以极快的速度逼近我们，因为模型进步得太快了。
cues.en: They’re like ghosts, but they’re coming at us so fast because the models are improving so fast.

cues.zh: 那么，你该如何应对一个今天还不存在、但正飞速逼近我们的东西呢？
cues.en: So how do you deal with something that’s not here today, doesn’t exist, but is coming at us very fast?

cues.zh: 为此我们想出的解决方案，是与 METR 这样的组织和 Paul Christiano 等人合作得出的：你需要的是能告诉你风险何时临近的测试。
cues.en: So the solution we came up with for that, in collaboration with people like the organization METR and Paul Christiano is what you need for that are you need tests to tell you when the risk is getting close.

cues.zh: 你需要一个预警系统。
cues.en: You need an early warning system.

cues.zh: 所以每当我们有新模型时，都会测试它执行这些 CBRN 任务的能力，同时测试它自主独立完成任务的能力。
cues.en: And so every time we have a new model, we test it for its capability to do these CBRN tasks as well as testing it for how capable it is of doing tasks autonomously on its own.

cues.zh: 在我们最新版的 RSP 中，也就是过去一两个月发布的版本里，我们测试自主性风险的方式是看 AI 模型自身完成 AI 研究各方面工作的能力，而当 AI 模型能够做 AI 研究时，它们就变得真正、真正自主了。
cues.en: And in the latest version of our RSP, which we released in the last month or two, the way we test autonomy risks is the AI model’s ability to do aspects of AI research itself, which when the AI models can do AI research, they become truly, truly autonomous.

cues.zh: 而这个阈值在其他很多方面都很重要。
cues.en: And that threshold is important for a bunch of other ways.

cues.zh: 那么接下来我们拿这些任务怎么办？
cues.en: And so what do we then do with these tasks?

cues.zh: RSP 基本上构建了我们所说的“如果-那么”结构，也就是如果模型通过了某项能力，那么我们就对它们施加一整套安全与安保要求。
cues.en: The RSP basically develops what we’ve called an if-then structure, which is if the models pass a certain capability, then we impose a certain set of safety and security requirements on them.

cues.zh: 所以今天的模型属于所谓的 ASL-2。
cues.en: So today’s models are what’s called ASL-2.

cues.zh: ASL-1 级别的模型适用于那些明显不构成任何自主性或滥用风险的系统。
cues.en: Models that were ASL-1 is for systems that manifestly don’t pose any risk of autonomy or misuse.

cues.zh: 比如，一个下棋机器人，Deep Blue 就属于 ASL-1。
cues.en: So for example, a chess playing bot, Deep Blue would be ASL-1.

cues.zh: 很明显，你没法把深蓝用在象棋以外的任何地方。
cues.en: It’s just manifestly the case that you can’t use Deep Blue for anything other than chess.

cues.zh: 它就是为下棋设计的。
cues.en: It was just designed for chess.

cues.zh: 没人会用它发动高超的网络攻击，或者肆意妄为地统治世界。
cues.en: No one’s going to use it to conduct a masterful cyber attack or to run wild and take over the world.

cues.zh: ASL-2 是当今的 AI 系统，我们已经对其进行了测量，我们认为这些系统根本不够聪明，无法自主自我复制或执行一系列任务，也不够聪明，无法提供关于 CBRN 风险以及如何制造 CBRN 武器的有意义信息，超出通过谷歌搜索所能获知的范围。
cues.en: ASL-2 is today’s AI systems where we’ve measured them and we think these systems are simply not smart enough to autonomously self-replicate or conduct a bunch of tasks and also not smart enough to provide meaningful information about CBRN risks and how to build CBRN weapons above and beyond what can be known from looking at Google.

cues.zh: 事实上，有时它们确实能提供搜索引擎之外的信息，但不是那种能拼凑起来的方式，不是那种端到端足够危险的方式。
cues.en: In fact, sometimes they do provide information above and beyond a search engine, but not in a way that can be stitched together, not in a way that end-to-end is dangerous enough.

cues.zh: 所以 ASL-3 将是模型足够强大、能增强非国家行为体能力的那个节点，对吧？
cues.en: So ASL-3 is going to be the point at which the models are helpful enough to enhance the capabilities of non-state actors, right?

cues.zh: 不幸的是，国家行为体已经能以很高的熟练度做很多这类非常危险且具有破坏性的事情。
cues.en: State actors can already do, unfortunately, to a high level of proficiency, a lot of these very dangerous and destructive things.

cues.zh: 区别在于，非国家行为体没有这个能力。
cues.en: The difference is that non-state actors are not capable of it.

cues.zh: 所以当我们达到 ASL-3 时，我们会采取特殊的安全预防措施，足以防止模型被非国家行为体窃取，以及模型在部署后被滥用。
cues.en: And so when we get to ASL-3, we’ll take special security precautions designed to be sufficient to prevent theft of the model by non-state actors and misuse of the model as it’s deployed.

cues.zh: 我们必须针对这些特定领域设置增强的过滤器。
cues.en: We’ll have to have enhanced filters targeted at these particular areas.

cues.zh: 网络、生物、核。
cues.en: Cyber, bio, nuclear.

cues.zh: 网络、生物、核，以及模型自主性——这与其说是滥用风险，不如说是模型自身做出坏事的风险。
cues.en: Cyber, bio, nuclear and model autonomy, which is less a misuse risk and more a risk of the model doing bad things itself.

cues.zh: ASL-4，到了这些模型可能增强已有丰富知识背景的国家行为体的能力，和/或成为此类风险主要来源的程度。
cues.en: ASL-4, getting to the point where these models could enhance the capability of a already knowledgeable state actor and/or become the main source of such a risk.

cues.zh: 如果你想制造这类风险，主要途径就是通过模型。
cues.en: If you wanted to engage in such a risk, the main way you would do it is through a model.

cues.zh: 然后我认为ASL-4在自主性方面，是指借助AI模型在AI研究能力上获得一定程度的加速。
cues.en: And then I think ASL-4 on the autonomy side, it’s some amount of acceleration in AI research capabilities with an AI model.

cues.zh: 而ASL-5则是我们达到模型真正具备能力的阶段，它们在这些任务上的能力可能超越人类。
cues.en: And then ASL-5 is where we would get to the models that are truly capable that it could exceed humanity in their ability to do any of these tasks.

cues.zh: 所以这个“如果-那么”结构承诺的意义基本上是说：“听着，我不知道，我和这些模型打交道很多年了，也担心风险很多年了。
cues.en: And so the point of the if-then structure commitment is basically to say, “Look, I don’t know, I’ve been working with these models for many years and I’ve been worried about risk for many years.

cues.zh: 喊狼来了其实很危险。
cues.en: It’s actually dangerous to cry wolf.

cues.zh: 说这个模型有风险其实很危险。
cues.en: It’s actually dangerous to say this model is risky.

cues.zh: 人们看着它说，这明显不危险。”再说一次，风险的精妙之处不在于今天，但它正快速向我们袭来。
cues.en: And people look at it and they say this is manifestly not dangerous.” Again, it’s the delicacy of the risk isn’t here today, but it’s coming at us fast.

cues.zh: 你如何应对这个问题？
cues.en: How do you deal with that?

cues.zh: 对风险规划者来说，处理这个问题真的很令人烦恼。
cues.en: It’s really vexing to a risk planner to deal with it.

cues.zh: 所以这个如果-那么结构基本上是说：“看，我们不想激怒一群人，我们不想通过对今天不危险的模型施加这些非常沉重的负担，来损害我们在对话中占有一席之地的能力。”所以如果-那么，触发承诺基本上是应对这个问题的一种方式。
cues.en: And so this if-then structure basically says, “Look, we don’t want to antagonize a bunch of people, we don’t want to harm our own ability to have a place in the conversation by imposing these very onerous burdens on models that are not dangerous today.” So the if-then, the trigger commitment is basically a way to deal with this.

cues.zh: 它说的是，当你能证明模型危险时，就要严厉打击。
cues.en: It says you clamp down hard when you can show the model is dangerous.

cues.zh: 当然，随之而来的是足够的缓冲阈值，这样你才不会面临错过危险的高风险。
cues.en: And of course, what has to come with that is enough of a buffer threshold that you’re not at high risk of missing the danger.

cues.zh: 这不是一个完美的框架。
cues.en: It’s not a perfect framework.

cues.zh: 我们不得不修改它。
cues.en: We’ve had to change it.

cues.zh: 几周前我们刚推出了一个新版本，未来可能一年会发布多次新版本，因为从技术、组织、研究的角度来看，这些政策很难做对。
cues.en: We came out with a new one just a few weeks ago and probably going forward, we might release new ones multiple times a year because it’s hard to get these policies right technically, organizationally from a research perspective.

cues.zh: 但这就是提案，即“如果-那么”承诺和触发条件，以便现在尽量减少负担和误报，但在危险真正来临时能恰当应对。
cues.en: But that is the proposal, if-then commitments and triggers in order to minimize burdens and false alarms now, but really react appropriately when the dangers are here.

cues.zh: 你认为ASL-3的时间线如何，其中几个触发条件会被触发？
cues.en: What do you think the timeline for ASL-3 is where several of the triggers are fired?

cues.zh: 你认为ASL-4的时间线如何？
cues.en: And what do you think the timeline is for ASL-4?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以这在公司内部引发了激烈争论。
cues.en: So that is hotly debated within the company.

cues.zh: 我们正在积极准备ASL-3的安全措施以及ASL-3的部署措施。
cues.en: We are working actively to prepare ASL-3 security measures as well as ASL-3 deployment measures.

cues.zh: 我不打算详细展开，但我们在两方面都取得了很大进展，我认为我们很快就能准备好。
cues.en: I’m not going to go into detail, but we’ve made a lot of progress on both and we’re prepared to be, I think, ready quite soon.

cues.zh: 如果我们明年达到ASL-3，我一点也不会感到意外。
cues.en: I would not be surprised at all if we hit ASL-3 next year.

cues.zh: 之前有人担心我们甚至今年就可能达到。
cues.en: There was some concern that we might even hit it this year.

cues.zh: 这仍然有可能。
cues.en: That’s still possible.

cues.zh: 那仍可能发生。
cues.en: That could still happen.

cues.zh: 很难说，但如果是2030年，我会非常非常惊讶。
cues.en: It’s very hard to say, but I would be very, very surprised if it was 2030.

cues.zh: 我认为会比那早得多。
cues.en: I think it’s much sooner than that.

cues.zh: 所以有检测它的协议，即if-then协议，然后还有如何应对它的协议。
cues.en: So there’s protocols for detecting it, the if-then and then there’s protocols for how to respond to it.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 第二个，也就是后者，有多难？
cues.en: How difficult is the second, the latter?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我认为对于ASL-3，主要关乎安全性，以及在我们部署模型时针对非常狭窄的一组领域对模型施加的过滤器。
cues.en: I think for ASL-3, it’s primarily about security and about filters on the model relating to a very narrow set of areas when we deploy the model.

cues.zh: 因为在ASL-3级别，模型还不具备自主能力。
cues.en: Because at ASL-3, the model isn’t autonomous yet.

cues.zh: 所以即使模型在内部部署，你也不用担心模型本身会做出不良行为。
cues.en: And so you don’t have to worry about the model itself behaving in a bad way even when it’s deployed internally.

cues.zh: 所以我认为ASL-3的措施，我不会说它们简单直接，它们是严格的，但更容易推理。
cues.en: So I think the ASL- 3 measures are, I won’t say straightforward, they’re rigorous, but they’re easier to reason about.

cues.zh: 我认为一旦到了ASL-4，我们就开始担心模型足够聪明，可能会在测试中故意放水，可能在测试中不说实话。
cues.en: I think once we get to ASL-4, we start to have worries about the models being smart enough that they might sandbag tests, they might not tell the truth about tests.

cues.zh: 我们有一些关于“潜伏代理”的研究结果，还有一篇更近期的论文，探讨“模型能否误导对其自身能力的放水尝试，把自己表现得比实际能力更弱？”所以我认为在ASL-4阶段，除了与模型交互之外，使用其他手段将是一个重要的组成部分。
cues.en: We had some results came out about sleeper agents and there was a more recent paper about, “Can the models mislead attempts to sandbag their own abilities, present themselves as being less capable than they are?” And so I think with ASL-4, there’s going to be an important component of using other things than just interacting with the models.

cues.zh: 比如可解释性，或者隐藏的思维链，你需要深入模型内部，通过某种不易被模型言论所污染的其他机制来验证模型确实具备某些属性。
cues.en: For example, interpretability or hidden chains of thought where you have to look inside the model and verify via some other mechanism that is not as easily corrupted as what the model says, that the model indeed has some property.

cues.zh: 所以我们还在研究 ASL-4。
cues.en: So we’re still working on ASL-4.

cues.zh: RSP 的一个特点是，在达到 ASL-3 之前，我们不会具体规定 ASL-4。
cues.en: One of the properties of the RSP is that we don’t specify ASL-4 until we’ve hit ASL-3.

cues.zh: 我认为这已被证明是明智的决定，因为即便是 ASL-3，也很难详细了解这些东西，我们想尽可能多花时间来把这些事情做对。
cues.en: And I think that’s proven to be a wise decision because even with ASL-3, again, it’s hard to know this stuff in detail, and we want to take as much time as we can possibly take to get these things right.

cues.zh: 所以对于 ASL-3，恶意行为者是人类。
cues.en: So for ASL-3, the bad actor will be the humans.

cues.zh: 人类，是的。
cues.en: Humans, yes.

cues.zh: 所以这里稍微多一点……
cues.en: And so there’s a little bit more…

cues.zh: 对于 ASL-4，我认为两者都是。
cues.en: For ASL- 4, it’s both, I think.

cues.zh: 两者都是。
cues.en: It’s both.

cues.zh: 还有欺骗，这就是机制可解释性发挥作用的地方，希望用于此的技术不会让模型接触到。
cues.en: And so deception, and that’s where mechanistic interpretability comes into play, and hopefully the techniques used for that are not made accessible to the model.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 当然，你可以把机制可解释性直接接到模型本身上，但那样它就失去了作为模型状态可靠指标的作用。
cues.en: Of course, you can hook up the mechanistic interpretability to the model itself, but then you’ve lost it as a reliable indicator of the model state.

cues.zh: 你还能想到很多奇特的方式让它变得不可靠，比如模型聪明到能跳到别的电脑上，读取你查看它内部状态的那段代码。
cues.en: There are a bunch of exotic ways you can think of that it might also not be reliable, like if the model gets smart enough that it can jump computers and read the code where you’re looking at its internal state.

cues.zh: 有些情况我们考虑过了。
cues.en: We’ve thought about some of those.

cues.zh: 我觉得它们已经够奇特了。
cues.en: I think they’re exotic enough.

cues.zh: 有办法让它们变得不太可能发生。
cues.en: There are ways to render them unlikely.

cues.zh: 但总的来说，你要把机制可解释性保留为一个验证集或测试集，与模型的训练过程分开。
cues.en: But yeah, generally, you want to preserve mechanistic interpretability as a verification set or test set that’s separate from the training process of the model.

cues.zh: 你看，我认为随着这些模型对话能力越来越强、越来越聪明，社会工程也会成为一种威胁，因为它们可能开始对公司内部的工程师极具说服力。
cues.en: See, I think as these models become better and better conversation and become smarter, social engineer becomes a threat too because they could start being very convincing to the engineers inside companies.

cues.zh: 哦，是的。
cues.en: Oh, yeah.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我们在生活中见过很多人类煽动民粹的例子，有人担心模型也会这么做。
cues.en: We’ve seen lots of examples of demagoguery in our life from humans, and there’s a concern that models could do that as well.

cues.zh: Claude 变得越来越强大的方式之一，是它现在能做一些智能体的事情，比如计算机使用。
cues.en: One of the ways that Claude has been getting more and more powerful is it’s now able to do some agentic stuff, computer use.

cues.zh: Claude.ai 本身的沙盒内也有分析功能。
cues.en: There’s also an analysis within the sandbox of Claude.ai itself.

cues.zh: 但我们来聊聊计算机使用。
cues.en: But let’s talk about computer use.

cues.zh: 这让我觉得非常兴奋，你只要给 Claude 一个任务，它就会执行一系列操作，自己搞清楚，并且能访问……
cues.en: That seems to me super exciting that you can just give Claude a task and it takes a bunch of actions, figures it out, and has access to the…

cues.zh: ……执行一系列操作，自己搞清楚，并通过截图访问你的电脑。
cues.en: … a bunch of actions, figures it out and has access to your computer through screenshots.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下这是怎么运作的，以及它会走向何方吗？
cues.en: So can you explain how that works and where that’s headed?

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 其实相对简单。
cues.en: It’s actually relatively simple.

cues.zh: Claude 很早就有这个能力了，从三月份的 Claude 3 开始，就能分析图像并用文本回应。
cues.en: So Claude has had for a long time, since Claude 3 back in March, the ability to analyze images and respond to them with text.

cues.zh: 我们唯一新增的是，这些图像可以是电脑截图，然后我们训练模型给出屏幕上可点击的位置，和/或键盘上可按下的按键，以便执行操作。
cues.en: The only new thing we added is those images can be screenshots of a computer and in response, we train the model to give a location on the screen where you can click and/or buttons on the keyboard, you can press in order to take action.

cues.zh: 事实证明，其实不需要太多额外训练，模型就能在这项任务上表现得相当好。
cues.en: And it turns out that with actually not all that much additional training, the models can get quite good at that task.

cues.zh: 这是泛化能力的一个好例子。
cues.en: It’s a good example of generalization.

cues.zh: 人们有时说，如果能到达近地轨道，你就已经走了一半的路，因为摆脱引力井需要耗费太多能量。
cues.en: People sometimes say if you get to lower earth orbit, you’re halfway to anywhere because of how much it takes to escape the gravity well.

cues.zh: 如果你有一个强大的预训练模型，我觉得在智能空间里，你就已经走了一半的路。
cues.en: If you have a strong pre-trained model, I feel like you’re halfway to anywhere in terms of the intelligence space.

cues.zh: 所以实际上，让 Claude 做到这一点并没有花太多功夫。
cues.en: And so actually, it didn’t take all that much to get Claude to do this.

cues.zh: 你可以在循环里设置它，给模型一张截图，告诉它点哪里，再给下一张截图，告诉它点哪里，这就变成了一种几乎像3D视频一样的模型交互，它能够完成所有这些任务。
cues.en: And you can just set that in a loop, give the model a screenshot, tell it what to click on, give it the next screenshot, tell it what to click on and that turns into a full kind of almost 3D video interaction of the model and it’s able to do all of these tasks.

cues.zh: 我们展示了这些演示，它能填写电子表格，能与网站交互，能打开各种程序、不同的操作系统，Windows、Linux、Mac。
cues.en: We showed these demos where it’s able to fill out spreadsheets, it’s able to kind of interact with a website, it’s able to open all kinds of programs, different operating systems, Windows, Linux, Mac.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这一切都非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: So I think all of that is very exciting.

cues.zh: 我要说的是，虽然理论上你在那里能做的事情，通过给模型驱动电脑屏幕的API也都能做到，但这确实大大降低了门槛。
cues.en: I will say, while in theory there’s nothing you could do there that you couldn’t have done through just giving the model the API to drive the computer screen, this really lowers the barrier.

cues.zh: 有很多人要么没法使用那些API，要么需要花很长时间才能做到。
cues.en: And there’s a lot of folks who either aren’t in a position to interact with those APIs or it takes them a long time to do.

cues.zh: 屏幕本身就是一个通用界面，交互起来容易得多。
cues.en: It’s just the screen is just a universal interface that’s a lot easier to interact with.

cues.zh: 所以我预计随着时间推移，这会降低很多门槛。
cues.en: And so I expect over time, this is going to lower a bunch of barriers.

cues.zh: 说实话，目前的模型还有很多不足之处，我们在博客里也坦诚地说了。
cues.en: Now, honestly, the current model has, it leaves a lot still to be desired and we were honest about that in the blog.

cues.zh: 它会犯错，会点错地方。
cues.en: It makes mistakes, it misclicks.

cues.zh: 我们特意提醒大家：“嘿，你不能就让这东西在你电脑上跑个几分钟又几分钟。
cues.en: We were careful to warn people, “Hey, you can’t just leave this thing to run on your computer for minutes and minutes.

cues.zh: 你得给它设定边界和护栏。”我觉得这也是我们先以 API 形式发布、而不是直接交给消费者让它控制电脑的原因之一。
cues.en: You got to give this thing boundaries and guardrails.” And I think that’s one of the reasons we released it first in an API form rather than just hand the consumer and give it control of their computer.

cues.zh: 但我确实觉得，把这些能力推向外界很重要。
cues.en: But I definitely feel that it’s important to get these capabilities out there.

cues.zh: 随着模型越来越强大，我们必须认真思考如何安全地使用这些能力。
cues.en: As models get more powerful, we’re going to have to grapple with how do we use these capabilities safely.

cues.zh: 如何防止它们被滥用？
cues.en: How do we prevent them from being abused?

cues.zh: 我认为，在能力仍然有限时发布模型，对做到这一点非常有帮助。
cues.en: And I think releasing the model while the capabilities are still limited is very helpful in terms of doing that.

cues.zh: 我认为自发布以来，不少客户都以各种方式利用了它，Replit 可能是部署最快的之一。
cues.en: I think since it’s been released, a number of customers, I think Replit was maybe one of the most quickest to deploy things, have made use of it in various ways.

cues.zh: 人们为 Windows 桌面、Mac、Linux 机器接上了演示。
cues.en: People have hooked up demos for Windows desktops, Macs, Linux machines.

cues.zh: 所以是的，这非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: So yeah, it’s been very exciting.

cues.zh: 我想和其他事物一样，它带来了令人兴奋的新能力，而伴随这些新能力，我们必须思考如何让模型安全、可靠，做人类希望它们做的事。
cues.en: I think as with anything else, it comes with new exciting abilities and then with those new exciting abilities, we have to think about how to make the model safe, reliable, do what humans want them to do.

cues.zh: 所有事情都是同样的道理。
cues.en: It’s the same story for everything.

cues.zh: 一样的。
cues.en: Same thing.

cues.zh: 就是那种同样的矛盾。
cues.en: It’s that same tension.

cues.zh: 但这里用例的可能性，范围简直不可思议。
cues.en: But the possibility of use cases here, just the range is incredible.

cues.zh: 那么未来要让它真正运行良好，需要投入多少？
cues.en: So how much to make it work really well in the future?

cues.zh: 你需要多大程度地超越预训练模型所做的，做更多后训练、RLHF 或有监督微调，或者专门为智能体相关的东西合成数据？
cues.en: How much do you have to specially kind of go beyond what the pre-trained model is doing, do more post-training, RLHF or supervised fine-tuning or synthetic data just for the agentive stuff?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得从高层面上说，我们的意图是持续大量投入，让模型变得更好。
cues.en: I think speaking at a high level, it’s our intention to keep investing a lot in making the model better.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们看一些基准测试，之前的模型像是，“哦，6% 的时候能做到，”而现在我们的模型能做到 14% 或 22% 的时候。
cues.en: I think we look at some of the benchmarks where previous models were like, “Oh, could do it 6% of the time,” and now our model would do it 14 or 22% of the time.

cues.zh: 而且是的，我们想达到人类水平的可靠性，80%、90%，就像其他任何地方一样。
cues.en: And yeah, we want to get up to the human level reliability of 80, 90% just like anywhere else.

cues.zh: 我们正处在与 SWE-bench 相同的曲线上，我猜一年后，模型能非常非常可靠地完成这件事。
cues.en: We’re on the same curve that we were on with SWE-bench where I think I would guess a year from now, the models can do this very, very reliably.

cues.zh: 但总得从某处开始。
cues.en: But you got to start somewhere.

cues.zh: 所以你认为有可能达到人类水平 90%，基本上就是做你现在在做的事，还是必须为计算机使用做特殊处理？
cues.en: So you think it’s possible to get to the human level 90% basically doing the same thing you’re doing now or it has to be special for computer use?

cues.zh: 这取决于你说的特殊是什么意思，以及一般意义上的特殊，但我总体上认为，我们一直用来训练当前模型的同类技术，我预计会加倍投入这些技术，就像我们在代码、通用模型、图像输入、语音上所做的那样，我预计这些相同的技术在这里也会像在其他所有地方一样扩展。
cues.en: It depends what you mean by special and special in general, but I generally think the same kinds of techniques that we’ve been using to train the current model, I expect that doubling down on those techniques in the same way that we have for code, for models in general, for image input, for voice, I expect those same techniques will scale here as they have everywhere else,

cues.zh: 但这赋予了 Claude 行动的能力，所以你可以做很多非常强大的事情，但你也可能造成很多损害。
cues.en: But this is giving the power of action to Claude and so you could do a lot of really powerful things, but you could do a lot of damage also.

cues.zh: 是的，是的。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 不，我们一直非常清楚这一点。
cues.en: No and we’ve been very aware of that.

cues.zh: 你看，我的观点其实是，计算机使用并不是像 CBRN 或自主能力那样根本性的新能力。
cues.en: Look, my view actually is computer use isn’t a fundamentally new capability like the CBRN or autonomy capabilities are.

cues.zh: 它更像是为模型打开了一扇窗，让它能够使用和应用已有的能力。
cues.en: It’s more like it kind of opens the aperture for the model to use and apply its existing abilities.

cues.zh: 所以我们的思路，回到我们的 RSP，就是：这个模型所做的任何事情，从 RSP 的角度来看，本身并没有增加风险；但随着模型变得更强大，拥有这种能力可能会变得更可怕——一旦它具备了在 ASL-3 和 ASL-4 级别做事的认知能力，这可能就是让它摆脱束缚去做那些事的东西。
cues.en: And so the way we think about it, going back to our RSP, is nothing that this model is doing inherently increases the risk from an RSP perspective, but as the models get more powerful, having this capability may make it scarier once it has the cognitive capability to do something at the ASL-3 and ASL-4 level, this may be the thing that kind of unbounds it from doing so.

cues.zh: 所以展望未来，这种交互方式当然是我们已经测试过的，而且我们将在 RSP 框架下继续测试。
cues.en: So going forward, certainly this modality of interaction is something we have tested for and that we will continue to test for an RSP going forward.

cues.zh: 我觉得最好在模型能力变得超强之前，先学习和探索这项能力
cues.en: I think it’s probably better to learn and explore this capability before the model is super capable

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 而且有很多有趣的攻击方式，比如提示注入，因为现在你扩大了攻击面，可以通过屏幕上的内容进行提示注入。
cues.en: And there’s a lot of interesting attacks like prompt injection because now you’ve widened the aperture so you can prompt inject through stuff on screen.

cues.zh: 所以如果这变得越来越有用，那么向模型中注入内容的收益也会越来越大。
cues.en: So if this becomes more and more useful, then there’s more and more benefit to inject stuff into the model.

cues.zh: 如果它访问某个网页，可能是无害的内容，比如广告，也可能是有害的内容，对吧？
cues.en: If it goes to certain web page, it could be harmless stuff like advertisements or it could be harmful stuff, right?

cues.zh: 是的，我们深入考虑过垃圾信息、验证码、批量……告诉你一个秘密，如果你发明了一项新技术，最先看到的滥用不一定是最大的滥用，而是诈骗，就是些小打小闹的诈骗。
cues.en: Yeah, we’ve thought a lot about things like spam, CAPTCHA, mass… One secret, I’ll tell you, if you’ve invented a new technology, not necessarily the biggest misuse, but the first misuse you’ll see, scams, just petty scams.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 这就像一样古老的东西，人们互相诈骗，这是和时代一样古老的事。
cues.en: It’s like a thing as old, people scamming each other, it’s this thing as old as time.

cues.zh: 每次你都得应对它。
cues.en: And it’s just every time, you got to deal with it.

cues.zh: 说起来几乎有点可笑，但确实如此，总的来说机器人和垃圾信息就是这样的东西，随着它变得越来越智能——
cues.en: It’s almost silly to say, but it’s true, sort of bots and spam in general is a thing as it gets more and more intelligent-

cues.zh: 是的，是的。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: ……就越来难以对抗。
cues.en: … it’s harder and harder to fight it.

cues.zh: 就像我说的，世界上有很多小罪犯，每项新技术都是小罪犯做蠢事和恶意行为的新途径。
cues.en: Like I said, there are a lot of petty criminals in the world and it’s like every new technology is a new way for petty criminals to do something stupid and malicious.

cues.zh: 有没有关于对它进行沙箱隔离的想法？
cues.en: Is there any ideas about sandboxing it?

cues.zh: 沙箱隔离任务有多难？
cues.en: How difficult is the sandboxing task?

cues.zh: 是的，我们在训练期间进行沙箱隔离。
cues.en: Yeah, we sandbox during training.

cues.zh: 比如，训练期间我们没有让模型接触互联网。
cues.en: So for example, during training we didn’t expose the model to the internet.

cues.zh: 我认为训练期间那样做可能是个坏主意，因为模型可能会改变其策略，可能会改变它正在做的事情，并且会对现实世界产生影响。
cues.en: I think that’s probably a bad idea during training because the model can be changing its policy, it can be changing what it’s doing and it’s having an effect in the real world.

cues.zh: 就实际部署模型而言，这取决于具体应用。
cues.en: In terms of actually deploying the model, it kind of depends on the application.

cues.zh: 有时你希望模型在现实世界中做点什么。
cues.en: Sometimes you want the model to do something in the real world.

cues.zh: 当然，你总可以在外部加上防护，总可以设置防护栏。
cues.en: But of course, you can always put guard, you can always put guard rails on the outside.

cues.zh: 你可以说：“好吧，这个模型不会把我的数据搬走，不会把我电脑或网络服务器上的任何文件搬到别处去。”
cues.en: You can say, “Okay, well, this model’s not going to move data from my, the model’s not going to move any files from my computer or my web server to anywhere else.”

cues.zh: 说到沙箱，等我们谈到 ASL-4 时，这些预防措施就都没意义了。
cues.en: Now, when you talk about sandboxing, again, when we get to ASL-4, none of these precautions are going to make sense there.

cues.zh: 谈到 ASL-4 时，理论上担心的是模型可能聪明到能突破任何盒子。
cues.en: When you talk about ASL-4, you’re then, the model is being, there’s theoretical worry the model could be smart enough to kind of break it to out of any box.

cues.zh: 所以在那里，我们需要考虑机制可解释性。
cues.en: And so there, we need to think about mechanistic interpretability.

cues.zh: 如果要搞沙盒，它必须在数学上可证明。
cues.en: If we’re going to have a sandbox, it would need to be a mathematically provable.

cues.zh: 那和我们现在面对的模型完全是两个世界。
cues.en: That’s a whole different world than what we’re dealing with with the models today.

cues.zh: 对，就是打造一个 ASL-4 级 AI 系统无法逃出的牢笼的科学。
cues.en: Yeah, the science of building a box from which ASL-4 AI system cannot escape.

cues.zh: 我觉得这大概不是正确的做法。
cues.en: I think it’s probably not the right approach.

cues.zh: 我认为正确的做法，不是弄一个未对齐的东西再设法防止它逃逸，而是直接用正确的方式设计模型，或者建立一个循环，让你能窥探模型内部、验证其属性，这样你就有机会判断、迭代，真正把它做对。
cues.en: I think the right approach, instead of having something unaligned that you’re trying to prevent it from escaping, I think it’s better to just design the model the right way or have a loop where you look inside the model and you’re able to verify properties and that gives you an opportunity to tell, iterate and actually get it right.

cues.zh: 我认为遏制坏模型，远比拥有好模型要糟糕得多。
cues.en: I think containing bad models is a much worse solution than having good models.

cues.zh: 让我问问监管方面的问题。
cues.en: Let me ask about regulation.

cues.zh: 监管在保障AI安全方面起什么作用？
cues.en: What’s the role of regulation in keeping AI safe?

cues.zh: 比如，你能描述一下加州AI监管法案SB 1047吗？它最终被州长否决了。
cues.en: So for example, can you describe California AI regulation bill SB 1047 that was ultimately vetoed by the governor?

cues.zh: 总的来说，这个法案有哪些优缺点？
cues.en: What are the pros and cons of this bill in general?

cues.zh: 是的，我们最终对法案提出了一些建议。
cues.en: Yes, we ended up making some suggestions to the bill.

cues.zh: 后来其中一些被采纳了，到那时我们对这个法案的看法相当积极，但它仍然有一些缺点。
cues.en: And then some of those were adopted and we felt, I think, quite positively about the bill by the end of that, it did still have some downsides.

cues.zh: 当然，它被否决了。
cues.en: And of course, it got vetoed.

cues.zh: 我认为从高层来看，这个法案背后的一些关键理念，我会说和我们的RSP背后的理念相似。
cues.en: I think at a high level, I think some of the key ideas behind the bill are I would say similar to ideas behind our RSPs.

cues.zh: 而且我认为非常重要的一点是，某个司法管辖区——无论是加州、联邦政府，还是其他国家和州——能通过一些这样的监管。
cues.en: And I think it’s very important that some jurisdiction, whether it’s California or the federal government and/or other countries and other states, passes some regulation like this.

cues.zh: 我可以讲讲为什么我觉得这一点如此重要。
cues.en: And I can talk through why I think that’s so important.

cues.zh: 所以我对我们的 RSP 感觉不错。
cues.en: So I feel good about our RSP.

cues.zh: 它并不完美。
cues.en: It’s not perfect.

cues.zh: 它需要大量迭代。
cues.en: It needs to be iterated on a lot.

cues.zh: 但它一直是个很好的推动力，让公司认真对待这些风险，把它们纳入产品规划，真正让它们成为 Anthropic 工作的核心部分，并确保所有一千人——现在 Anthropic 已经快一千人了——都明白这是公司最高优先级之一，甚至就是最高优先级。
cues.en: But it’s been a good forcing function for getting the company to take these risks seriously, to put them into product planning, to really make them a central part of work at Anthropic and to make sure that all of a thousand people, and it’s almost a thousand people now at Anthropic, understand that this is one of the highest priorities of the company, if not the highest priority.

cues.zh: 但一方面，仍有一些公司没有类似 RSP 的机制，比如 OpenAI，Google 在 Anthropic 之后几个月也采用了这些机制，但还有其他公司根本没有这些机制。
cues.en: But one, there are still some companies that don’t have RSP like mechanisms, like OpenAI, Google did adopt these mechanisms a couple months after Anthropic did, but there are other companies out there that don’t have these mechanisms at all.

cues.zh: 所以，如果一些公司采用了这些机制，而另一些没有，就真的会造成一种局面：其中一些危险具有这样的性质——五家公司里有三家在保证安全也没用，只要另外两家不安全，就会产生这种负外部性。
cues.en: And so if some companies adopt these mechanisms and others don’t, it’s really going to create a situation where some of these dangers have the property that it doesn’t matter if three out of five of the companies are being safe, if the other two are being unsafe, it creates this negative externality.

cues.zh: 而且我认为，这种缺乏统一性的做法，对我们这些花了很多心思、非常认真地对待这些流程的人并不公平。
cues.en: And I think the lack of uniformity is not fair to those of us who have put a lot of effort into being very thoughtful about these procedures.

cues.zh: 第二点是，我不认为可以信任这些公司会自行遵守这些自愿性计划。
cues.en: The second thing is I don’t think you can trust these companies to adhere to these voluntary plans on their own.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 我愿意相信 Anthropic 会做到，我们会尽一切努力去做到，我们的 RSP 由我们的长期利益信托来核查，所以我们尽一切努力遵守我们自己的 RSP。
cues.en: I like to think that Anthropic will, we do everything we can that we will, our RSP is checked by our long-term benefit trust, so we do everything we can to adhere to our own RSP.

cues.zh: 但你听到很多关于各家公司的说法，说：“哦，他们说会给这么多算力，结果没给。
cues.en: But you hear lots of things about various companies saying, “Oh, they said they would give this much compute and they didn’t.

cues.zh: 他们说会做这件事，结果没做。”我觉得去纠缠公司做过的具体事情没意义，但我认为这个大的原则是：如果没有东西监督他们，如果没有东西监督我们整个行业，就无法保证我们会做正确的事，而风险非常高。
cues.en: They said they would do this thing and the didn’t.” I don’t think it makes sense to litigate particular things that companies have done, but I think this broad principle that if there’s nothing watching over them, if there’s nothing watching over us as an industry, there’s no guarantee that we’ll do the right thing and the stakes are very high.

cues.zh: 所以我认为重要的是有一个所有人遵循的统一标准，确保行业做到大多数从业者已经说过很重要、并且已经说过他们肯定会做的事。
cues.en: And so I think it’s important to have a uniform standard that everyone follows and to make sure that simply that the industry does what a majority of the industry has already said is important and has already said that they definitely will do.

cues.zh: 对，有些人，我认为有一类人是原则上反对监管的。
cues.en: Right, some people, I think there’s a class of people who are against regulation on principle.

cues.zh: 我理解这种想法从何而来。
cues.en: I understand where that comes from.

cues.zh: 如果你去欧洲，看到像 GDPR 这样的东西，看到他们做的一些其他事情。
cues.en: If you go to Europe and you see something like GDPR, you see some of the other stuff that they’ve done.

cues.zh: 有些是好的，但有些确实是不必要的负担，我认为可以说确实拖慢了创新。
cues.en: Some of it’s good, but some of it is really unnecessarily burdensome and I think it’s fair to say really has slowed innovation.

cues.zh: 所以我理解人们基于先验立场的出发点。
cues.en: And so I understand where people are coming from on priors.

cues.zh: 我理解为什么人们从那个立场出发。
cues.en: I understand why people start from that position.

cues.zh: 但再次强调，我认为 AI 是不同的。
cues.en: But again, I think AI is different.

cues.zh: 如果我们谈到我刚才几分钟前说过的自主性和滥用的非常严重的风险，我认为那些是不寻常的，它们需要异常强有力的回应。
cues.en: If we go to the very serious risks of autonomy and misuse that I talked about just a few minutes ago, I think that those are unusual and they warrant an unusually strong response.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这非常重要。
cues.en: And so I think it’s very important.

cues.zh: 同样，我们需要一些大家都能支持的东西。
cues.en: Again, we need something that everyone can get behind.

cues.zh: 我认为 SB 1047 的问题之一，尤其是它的最初版本，是它包含了 RSP 的许多结构，但也包含了很多要么笨重、要么只会制造一堆负担和麻烦的内容，甚至在应对风险方面可能都没打中目标。
cues.en: I think one of the issues with SB 1047, especially the original version of it was it had a bunch of the structure of RSPs, but it also had a bunch of stuff that was either clunky or that just would’ve created a bunch of burdens, a bunch of hassle and might even have missed the target in terms of addressing the risks.

cues.zh: 你在 Twitter 上其实听不到这些，你听到的只是人们在为任何监管欢呼。
cues.en: You don’t really hear about it on Twitter, you just hear about kind of people are cheering for any regulation.

cues.zh: 然后反对的人会编造出这些往往相当不诚实的论点，说这会把我们赶出加州——可这项法案如果你总部在加州并不适用，只有你在加州做生意才适用——或者说它会破坏开源生态，或者说它会导致所有这些事情。
cues.en: And then the folks who are against make up these often quite intellectually dishonest arguments about how it’ll make us move away from California, bill doesn’t apply if you’re headquartered in California, bill only applies if you do business in California, or that it would damage the open source ecosystem or that it would cause all of these things.

cues.zh: 我觉得那些大多是胡说八道，但反对监管还有更好的理由。
cues.en: I think those were mostly nonsense, but there are better arguments against regulation.

cues.zh: 有个人叫 Dean Ball，我认为他是一位非常严谨的分析者，专门研究监管落地后如何可能自成一套体系，或者设计得有多糟糕。
cues.en: There’s one guy, Dean Ball, who’s really, I think, a very scholarly analyst who looks at what happens when a regulation is put in place in ways that they can kind of get a life of their own or how they can be poorly designed.

cues.zh: 所以我们一直以来的立场是：我们确实认为这个领域应该有监管，但我们希望成为一个推动者，确保监管是精准的、针对重大风险的，并且是人们实际能够遵守的。
cues.en: And so our interest has always been we do think there should be regulation in this space, but we want to be an actor who makes sure that that regulation is something that’s surgical, that’s targeted at the serious risks and is something people can actually comply with.

cues.zh: 因为我认为监管倡导者没能充分理解的一点是：如果我们出台的东西针对性很差、浪费大家大量时间，结果就是人们会说：“看吧，这些安全风险，纯属胡说八道。”
cues.en: Because something I think the advocates of regulation don’t understand as well as they could is if we get something in place that’s poorly targeted, that wastes a bunch of people’s time, what’s going to happen is people are going to say, “See, these safety risks, this is nonsense.

cues.zh: 我不得不雇了10个律师来填这些表格。
cues.en: I just had to hire 10 lawyers to fill out all these forms.

cues.zh: 我得为一件显然不危险的事情做所有这些测试。”
cues.en: I had to run all these tests for something that was clearly not dangerous.”

cues.zh: 这样过了六个月，就会形成一股浪潮，最终我们会达成一个反对监管的持久共识。
cues.en: And after six months of that, there will be a ground swell and we’ll end up with a durable consensus against regulation.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，对于那些想要真正问责的人来说，最大的敌人就是设计糟糕的监管。
cues.en: And so I think the worst enemy of those who want real accountability is badly designed regulation.

cues.zh: 我们得真正把它做对。
cues.en: We need to actually get it right.

cues.zh: 如果我能对倡导者们说一句话，那就是我希望他们更好地理解这种动态，我们需要非常小心，需要和那些真正有经验、见过监管在实践中如何运作的人交流。
cues.en: And if there’s one thing I could say to the advocates, it would be that I want them to understand this dynamic better and we need to be really careful and we need to talk to people who actually have experience seeing how regulations play out in practice.

cues.zh: 而那些见过的人，都明白要非常小心。
cues.en: And the people who have seen that, understand to be very careful.

cues.zh: 如果这只是个小问题，我可能根本反对监管。
cues.en: If this was some lesser issue, I might be against regulation at all.

cues.zh: 但我想让反对者理解的是，底层问题其实很严重。
cues.en: But what I want the opponents to understand is that the underlying issues are actually serious.

cues.zh: 这些问题不是我或其他公司因为监管俘获而编造出来的，不是科幻幻想，也不是那些东西。
cues.en: They’re not something that I or the other companies are just making up because of regulatory capture, they’re not sci-fi fantasies, they’re not any of these things.

cues.zh: 每次我们有新模型，每隔几个月我们都会测量这些模型的行为，它们在那些令人担忧的任务上越来越强，就像它们在好的、有价值的、经济上有用的任务上越来越强一样。
cues.en: Every time we have a new model, every few months we measure the behavior of these models and they’re getting better and better at these concerning tasks just as they are getting better and better at good, valuable, economically useful tasks.

cues.zh: 所以我非常希望，一些前——我觉得 SB 1047 非常两极分化，我非常希望一些最理性的反对者和一些最理性的支持者能坐下来一起谈。
cues.en: And so I would just love it if some of the former, I think SB 1047 was very polarizing, I would love it if some of the most reasonable opponents and some of the most reasonable proponents would sit down together.

cues.zh: 我觉得不同的AI公司里，Anthropic是唯一一家非常细致地表达了积极态度的AI公司。
cues.en: And I think that the different AI companies, Anthropic was the only AI company that felt positively in a very detailed way.

cues.zh: 我记得Elon简短地发过一条积极的推文，但像Google、OpenAI、Meta、Microsoft这些大公司都相当坚决地反对。
cues.en: I think Elon tweeted briefly something positive, but some of the big ones like Google, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft were pretty staunchly against.

cues.zh: 所以我真正希望的是，一些关键利益相关者、一些最有见地的支持者和一些最有见地的反对者能坐下来谈，说我们怎么解决这个问题，让支持者觉得真正降低了风险，让反对者觉得没有比必要程度更多地阻碍行业或阻碍创新。
cues.en: So I would really is if some of the key stakeholders, some of the most thoughtful proponents and some of the most thoughtful opponents would sit down and say how do we solve this problem in a way that the proponents feel brings a real reduction in risk and that the opponents feel that it is not hampering the industry or hampering innovation any more necessary than it needs to.

cues.zh: 我觉得不管什么原因，事情变得过于两极分化，那两个群体没能以应有的方式坐下来谈。
cues.en: I think for whatever reason, that things got too polarized and those two groups didn’t get to sit down in the way that they should.

cues.zh: 我感到紧迫。
cues.en: And I feel urgency.

cues.zh: 我真的觉得2025年我们得做点什么。
cues.en: I really think we need to do something in 2025.

cues.zh: 如果到了2025年底，我们对此仍然无所作为，那我会很担心。
cues.en: If we get to the end of 2025 and we’ve still done nothing about this, then I’m going to be worried.

cues.zh: 我现在还不担心，因为风险还没到来，但我觉得时间不多了。
cues.en: I’m not worried yet because, again, the risks aren’t here yet, but I think time is running short.

cues.zh: 然后拿出一些精准的办法，就像你说的。
cues.en: And come up with something surgical, like you said.

cues.zh: 对，对，对，没错。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, exactly.

cues.zh: 我们需要摆脱这种激烈支持安全与激烈反监管的言论对立。
cues.en: And we need to get away from this intense pro safety versus intense anti-regulatory rhetoric.

cues.zh: 这已经变成了Twitter上的骂战，不会有什么好结果。
cues.en: It’s turned into these flame wars on Twitter and nothing good’s going to come of that.

cues.zh: 所以大家对这场游戏中的不同参与者都很好奇。
cues.en: So there’s a lot of curiosity about the different players in the game.

cues.zh: 元老之一就是OpenAI。
cues.en: One of the OGs is OpenAI.

cues.zh: 你在OpenAI有好几年的经验。
cues.en: You’ve had several years of experience at OpenAI.

cues.zh: 你的故事和经历是怎样的？
cues.en: What’s your story and history there?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我在OpenAI待了大约五年。
cues.en: So I was at OpenAI for roughly five years.

cues.zh: 最后那段时间，我想大概有两年吧，我是那里的研究副总裁。
cues.en: For the last, I think it was couple years, I was vice president of research there.

cues.zh: 大概是我和Ilya Sutskever真正确定了研究方向。
cues.en: Probably myself and Ilya Sutskever were the ones who really kind of set the research direction.

cues.zh: 2016或2017年前后，我开始真正相信、或者至少确认了我对扩展假说的信念，当时Ilya对我说了那句著名的话：“关于这些模型，你需要明白的是，它们就是想学习。
cues.en: Around 2016 or 2017, I first started to really believe in or at least confirm my belief in the scaling hypothesis when Ilya famously said to me, “The thing you need to understand about these models is they just want to learn.

cues.zh: 模型就是想学习。”有时候就是有这样一句话，像锥子一样，你听到它就会想：“啊，这一下全解释通了。
cues.en: The models just want to learn.” And again, sometimes there are these one sentences, these then cones, that you hear them and you’re like, “Ah, that explains everything.

cues.zh: 这解释了我见过的上千件事。”从那以后，我脑子里就一直有个画面：你用正确的方式优化模型，把模型引向正确的方向，它们就是想学习。
cues.en: That explains a thousand things that I’ve seen.” And then ever after, I had this visualization in my head of you optimize the models in the right way, you point the models in the right way, they just want to learn.

cues.zh: 他们只想解决问题，不管问题是什么。
cues.en: They just want to solve the problem regardless of what the problem is.

cues.zh: 所以基本上就是别挡他们的路？
cues.en: So get out of their way, basically?

cues.zh: 别挡他们的路。
cues.en: Get out of their way.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 别把你自己的想法强加给他们，规定他们该怎么学。
cues.en: Don’t impose your own ideas about how they should learn.

cues.zh: 这和 Rich Sutton 在《苦涩的教训》里说的，以及 Gwern 在缩放假说里说的是一回事。
cues.en: And this was the same thing as Rich Sutton put out in the bitter lesson or Gwern put out in the scaling hypothesis.

cues.zh: 我觉得总体上的动态是，我从 Ilya 和其他人那里得到了这种启发，比如 Alec Radford，他做了最初的 GPT-1，然后在此基础上大力推进，我和我的合作者在 GPT-2、GPT-3、基于人类反馈的强化学习上继续推进，这是试图处理早期安全性和持久性的一种尝试，还有辩论和放大之类的东西，非常侧重可解释性。
cues.en: I think generally the dynamic was I got this kind of inspiration from Ilya and from others, folks like Alec Radford, who did the original GPT-1 and then ran really hard with it, me and my collaborators, on GPT-2, GPT-3, RL from Human Feedback, which was an attempt to kind of deal with the early safety and durability, things like debate and amplification, heavy on interpretability.

cues.zh: 所以再次强调，安全加上扩展的结合。
cues.en: So again, the combination of safety plus scaling.

cues.zh: 大概在2018、2019、2020那几年，我和我的合作者们——其中很多人后来成了Anthropic的联合创始人——真正有了清晰的愿景，并推动了方向。
cues.en: Probably 2018, 2019, 2020, those were kind of the years when myself and my collaborators, probably many of whom became co-founders of Anthropic, kind of really had a vision and drove the direction.

cues.zh: 你为什么离开？
cues.en: Why’d you leave?

cues.zh: 你为什么决定离开？
cues.en: Why’d you decide to leave?

cues.zh: 这么说吧，我这样讲，我觉得这和“向上竞争”有关。在OpenAI期间，我逐渐认识到扩展假设的重要性，也逐渐认识到安全与扩展假设同等重要。
cues.en: Yeah, so look, I’m going to put things this way and I think it ties to the race to the top, which is in my time at OpenAI, what I come to see as I’d come to appreciate the scaling hypothesis and as I’d come to appreciate kind of the importance of safety along with the scaling hypothesis.

cues.zh: 第一点，我认为OpenAI当时是认同的。
cues.en: The first one I think OpenAI was getting on board with.

cues.zh: 第二点，某种程度上一直是OpenAI对外传达的一部分。
cues.en: The second one in a way had always been part of OpenAI’s messaging.

cues.zh: 但在我待在那里的许多年里，我对该如何处理这些事情、该如何把它们呈现给世界、组织该秉持什么样的原则，有着自己特定的愿景。
cues.en: But over many years of the time that I spent there, I think I had a particular vision of how we should handle these things, how we should be brought out in the world, the kind of principles that the organization should have.

cues.zh: 你看，关于公司该不该做这做那，有过许许多多的讨论。
cues.en: And look, there were many, many discussions about should the company do this, should the company do that?

cues.zh: 外面有很多错误信息。
cues.en: There’s a bunch of misinformation out there.

cues.zh: 有人说我们离开是因为不喜欢和微软的交易。
cues.en: People say we left because we didn’t like the deal with Microsoft.

cues.zh: 不对。
cues.en: False.

cues.zh: 尽管确实有很多讨论、很多疑问，关于我们究竟怎么和微软做这笔交易。
cues.en: Although, it was like a lot of discussion, a lot of questions about exactly how we do the deal with Microsoft.

cues.zh: 我们离开是因为不喜欢商业化。
cues.en: We left because we didn’t like commercialization.

cues.zh: 那不是真的。
cues.en: That’s not true.

cues.zh: 我们打造了 GPD-3，那正是被商业化的模型。
cues.en: We built GPD-3, which was the model that was commercialized.

cues.zh: 我参与了商业化。
cues.en: I was involved in commercialization.

cues.zh: 这更多还是关于你怎么去做。
cues.en: It’s more, again, about how do you do it?

cues.zh: 文明正沿着这条路走向非常强大的人工智能。
cues.en: Civilization is going down this path to very powerful AI.

cues.zh: 该怎么做？
cues.en: What’s the way to do it?

cues.zh: 那就是谨慎、直接、诚实，从而在组织和个人层面建立信任。
cues.en: That is cautious, straightforward, honest, that builds trust in the organization and in individuals.

cues.zh: 我们怎么从这里走到那里，怎么才能真正想清楚怎样把它做对？
cues.en: How do we get from here to there and how do we have a real vision for how to get it right?

cues.zh: 怎么让安全不只是嘴上说说，只因为这样好招人。
cues.en: How can safety not just be something we say because it helps with recruiting.

cues.zh: 我觉得说到底，如果你对这件事有愿景，就别管别人的愿景。
cues.en: And I think at the end of the day, if you have a vision for that, forget about anyone else’s vision.

cues.zh: 我不想谈别人的愿景。
cues.en: I don’t want to talk about anyone else’s vision.

cues.zh: 如果你有怎么做成的愿景，你就该去做，去实现那个愿景。
cues.en: If you have a vision for how to do it, you should go off and you should do that vision.

cues.zh: 试图跟别人的愿景争论，效率极低。
cues.en: It is incredibly unproductive to try and argue with someone else’s vision.

cues.zh: 你可能觉得他们做得不对。
cues.en: You might think they’re not doing it the right way.

cues.zh: 你可能觉得他们不诚实。
cues.en: You might think they’re dishonest.

cues.zh: 谁知道呢？
cues.en: Who knows?

cues.zh: 也许你对，也许你不对。
cues.en: Maybe you’re right, maybe you’re not.

cues.zh: 但你该做的是，带上你信任的一些人，一起去做，把你的愿景变成现实。
cues.en: But what you should do is you should take some people you trust and you should go off together and you should make your vision happen.

cues.zh: 如果你的愿景足够有说服力，能打动人心，在伦理和市场之间找到某种平衡，如果你能打造一家人们想加入的公司，采取人们认为合理的做法，同时还能维持自己在生态系统中的地位，如果你做到了这些，人们就会效仿你。
cues.en: And if your vision is compelling, if you can make it appeal to people, some combination of ethically in the market, if you can make a company that’s a place people want to join, that engages in practices that people think are reasonable while managing to maintain its position in the ecosystem at the same time, if you do that, people will copy it.

cues.zh: 而你在做这件事，尤其是你做得比他们更好，这会促使他们改变行为，这种方式比你是他们的老板、和他们争论要有效得多。
cues.en: And the fact that you are doing it, especially the fact that you’re doing it better than they are, causes them to change their behavior in a much more compelling way than if they’re your boss and you’re arguing with them.

cues.zh: 我没法说得比这更具体了，但我认为，试图让别人的愿景变得像你的愿景一样，通常是徒劳无益的。
cues.en: I don’t know how to be any more specific about it than that, but I think it’s generally very unproductive to try and get someone else’s vision to look like your vision.

cues.zh: 去做一个干净的实验，然后说“这就是我们的愿景，这就是我们做事的方式”，这样效率要高得多。
cues.en: It’s much more productive to go off and do a clean experiment and say, “This is our vision, this is how we’re going to do things.

cues.zh: 你的选择是，你可以无视我们，你可以拒绝我们正在做的事，或者你可以开始变得更像我们。”而模仿是最真诚的奉承。
cues.en: Your choice is you can ignore us, you can reject what we’re doing or you can start to become more like us.” And imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

cues.zh: 这体现在客户的行为上，体现在公众的行为上，也体现在人们选择去哪里工作的行为上。
cues.en: And that plays out in the behavior of customers, that plays out in the behavior of the public, that plays out in the behavior of where people choose to work.

cues.zh: 再说一次，归根结底，这不是关于一家公司赢还是另一家公司赢。
cues.en: And again, at the end, it’s not about one company winning or another company winning.

cues.zh: 如果我们或另一家公司在采取某种人们真心觉得有吸引力的做法，我希望那是实质性的，而不只是表面功夫，我认为研究人员很老练，他们看的是实质，然后其他公司开始复制那种做法，并因为复制了那种做法而获胜。
cues.en: If we or another company are engaging in some practice that people find genuinely appealing, and I want it to be in substance, not just an appearance and I think researchers are sophisticated and they look at substance, and then other companies start copying that practice and they win because they copied that practice.

cues.zh: 这很棒。
cues.en: That’s great.

cues.zh: 这就是成功。
cues.en: That’s success.

cues.zh: 这就像是一场逐顶竞争。
cues.en: That’s like the race to the top.

cues.zh: 最终谁赢并不重要，只要大家都在互相借鉴彼此的好做法。
cues.en: It doesn’t matter who wins in the end as long as everyone is copying everyone else’s good practices.

cues.zh: 我的一种理解是，我们都害怕的是逐底竞争，而逐底竞争谁赢并不重要，因为大家都是输家。
cues.en: One way I think of it is the thing we’re all afraid of is the race to the bottom and the race to the bottom doesn’t matter who wins because we all lose.

cues.zh: 在最极端的情况下，我们造出这种自主AI，然后机器人奴役我们之类的。
cues.en: In the most extreme world, we make this autonomous AI that the robots enslave us or whatever.

cues.zh: 这是半开玩笑，但那确实是最极端可能发生的情况。
cues.en: That’s half joking, but that is the most extreme thing that could happen.

cues.zh: 那样的话，哪家公司领先就不重要了。
cues.en: Then it doesn’t matter which company was ahead.

cues.zh: 反过来，如果你创造一场逐顶竞争，让大家争相采用好做法，那么到头来，谁最终获胜并不重要，甚至谁发起了这场逐顶竞争也不重要。
cues.en: If instead you create a race to the top where people are competing to engage in good practices, then at the end of the day, it doesn’t matter who ends up winning, it doesn’t even matter who started the race to the top.

cues.zh: 重点不在于做个道德高尚的人，而在于让系统达到比之前更好的平衡状态。
cues.en: The point isn’t to be virtuous, the point is to get the system into a better equilibrium than it was before.

cues.zh: 而个体公司可以在这方面发挥一定作用。
cues.en: And individual companies can play some role in doing this.

cues.zh: 个体公司可以帮忙启动这件事，可以帮忙加速推进。
cues.en: Individual companies can help to start it, can help to accelerate it.

cues.zh: 坦率地说，我认为其他公司的个人也做过同样的事。
cues.en: And frankly, I think individuals at other companies have done this as well.

cues.zh: 当我们发布RSP时，有些人会反应更积极，推动其他公司也做类似的事情，有时候其他公司会做出一些让我们觉得“哦，这是个好做法”的举动。
cues.en: The individuals that when we put out an RSP react by pushing harder to get something similar done at other companies, sometimes other companies do something that’s we’re like, “Oh, it’s a good practice.

cues.zh: 我们觉得那很好。
cues.en: We think that’s good.

cues.zh: 我们也应该采纳。唯一的区别在于，我认为我们会更主动一些。
cues.en: We should adopt it too.” The only difference is I think we try to be more forward leaning.

cues.zh: 我们会更早采纳更多这类做法，当别人发明出来时，我们也会更快地采纳。
cues.en: We try and adopt more of these practices first and adopt them more quickly when others invent them.

cues.zh: 但我认为，这种动态才是我们应该关注的，它把哪家公司赢了、谁信任谁这类问题抽象掉了。
cues.en: But I think this dynamic is what we should be pointing at and that I think it abstracts away the question of which company’s winning, who trusts who.

cues.zh: 我觉得这些戏剧性的问题都极其无趣，真正重要的是我们共同所处的生态系统，以及如何让这个生态系统变得更好，因为这制约着所有参与者。
cues.en: I think all these questions of drama are profoundly uninteresting and the thing that matters is the ecosystem that we all operate in and how to make that ecosystem better because that constrains all the players.

cues.zh: 所以 Anthropic 就像是一个干净的实验，建立在“AI 安全具体应该是什么样”这一基础之上？
cues.en: And so Anthropic is this kind of clean experiment built on a foundation of what concretely AI safety should look like?

cues.zh: 嗯，你看，我确信我们一路上犯过不少错误。
cues.en: Well, look, I’m sure we’ve made plenty of mistakes along the way.

cues.zh: 完美的组织并不存在。
cues.en: The perfect organization doesn’t exist.

cues.zh: 它必须应对一千名员工的不完美。
cues.en: It has to deal with the imperfection of a thousand employees.

cues.zh: 它必须应对我们领导者的不完美，包括我自己。
cues.en: It has to deal with the imperfection of our leaders, including me.

cues.zh: 它必须应对我们所安排的人的不完美，这些人负责监督领导者的不完美，比如董事会和长期利益信托。
cues.en: It has to deal with the imperfection of the people we’ve put to oversee the imperfection of the leaders like the board and the long-term benefit trust.

cues.zh: 这都是一群不完美的人，试图不完美地追求某种永远无法完美实现的理想。
cues.en: It’s all a set of imperfect people trying to aim imperfectly at some ideal that will never perfectly be achieved.

cues.zh: 这就是你所承诺要面对的。
cues.en: That’s what you sign up for.

cues.zh: 它将永远如此。
cues.en: That’s what it will always be.

cues.zh: 但不完美并不意味着你就此放弃。
cues.en: But imperfect doesn’t mean you just give up.

cues.zh: 有更好的，也有更糟的。
cues.en: There’s better and there’s worse.

cues.zh: 希望我们能做得足够好，从而开始建立一些整个行业都参与的实践。
cues.en: And hopefully, we can do well enough that we can begin to build some practices that the whole industry engages in.

cues.zh: 然后我猜这些公司中会有多家取得成功。
cues.en: And then my guess is that multiple of these companies will be successful.

cues.zh: Anthropic会取得成功。
cues.en: Anthropic will be successful.

cues.zh: 其他公司，比如我过去待过的那些，也会取得成功。
cues.en: These other companies, like ones I’ve been at the past, will also be successful.

cues.zh: 有些会比其他的更成功。
cues.en: And some will be more successful than others.

cues.zh: 这不如让行业激励保持一致那么重要。
cues.en: That’s less important than, again, that we align the incentives of the industry.

cues.zh: 这在一定程度上通过逐顶竞争实现，部分通过RSP这类机制，部分通过有针对性的精准监管。
cues.en: And that happens partly through the race to the top, partly through things like RSP, partly through, again, selected surgical regulation.

cues.zh: 你说过人才密度胜过人才规模，能解释一下吗？
cues.en: You said talent density beats talent mass, so can you explain that?

cues.zh: 能详细说说吗？
cues.en: Can you expand on that?

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 能谈谈打造一支优秀的AI研究员和工程师团队需要什么吗？
cues.en: Can you just talk about what it takes to build a great team of AI researchers and engineers?

cues.zh: 这个说法每个月都变得更加正确。
cues.en: This is one of these statements that’s more true every month.

cues.zh: 每个月我都觉得这个说法比上个月更正确。
cues.en: Every month I see this statement as more true than I did the month before.

cues.zh: 如果我做个思想实验，假设你有一个100人的团队，他们非常聪明、有动力、与使命一致，这就是你的公司。
cues.en: So if I were to do a thought experiment, let’s say you have a team of 100 people that are super smart, motivated and aligned with the mission and that’s your company.

cues.zh: 或者你可以有一个一千人的团队，其中200人超级聪明、超级认同使命，然后800人，这么说吧，你随机挑800名大厂员工，你更想要哪种？
cues.en: Or you can have a team of a thousand people where 200 people are super smart, super aligned with the mission and then 800 people are, let’s just say you pick 800 random big tech employees, which would you rather have?

cues.zh: 一千人那组的整体人才密度更高。
cues.en: The talent mass is greater in the group of a thousand people.

cues.zh: 你会有更多才华横溢、极度认同使命、极其聪明的人。
cues.en: You have even a larger number of incredibly talented, incredibly aligned, incredibly smart people.

cues.zh: 但问题在于，如果每次某个超级有才华的人环顾四周，看到的都是同样才华横溢、同样投入的人，这就为一切定下了基调。
cues.en: But the issue is just that if every time someone super talented looks around, they see someone else super talented and super dedicated, that sets the tone for everything.

cues.zh: 这就定下了基调：每个人都深受鼓舞，想在同一地方工作。
cues.en: That sets the tone for everyone is super inspired to work at the same place.

cues.zh: 每个人都信任彼此。
cues.en: Everyone trusts everyone else.

cues.zh: 如果你有一千或一万人，而情况已经严重倒退，你无法做筛选，只能随机选人，那结果就是你需要设置大量流程和大量防护措施，仅仅因为人们不完全信任彼此，或者你得去裁决政治斗争。
cues.en: If you have a thousand or 10,000 people and things have really regressed, you are not able to do selection and you’re choosing random people, what happens is then you need to put a lot of processes and a lot of guardrails in place just because people don’t fully trust each other or you have to adjudicate political battles.

cues.zh: 有很多事情会拖慢组织的运作效率。
cues.en: There are so many things that slow down the org’s ability to operate.

cues.zh: 我们现在快一千人了，一直努力让这一千人里尽可能大的比例都是超有才华、超有技能的人，这也是过去几个月我们大幅放缓招聘的原因之一。
cues.en: And so we’re nearly a thousand people and we’ve tried to make it so that as large a fraction of those thousand people as possible are super talented, super skilled, it’s one of the reasons we’ve slowed down hiring a lot in the last few months.

cues.zh: 我记得今年头七八个月，我们从300人增长到800人，现在放缓了。
cues.en: We grew from 300 to 800, I believe, I think in the first seven, eight months of the year and now we’ve slowed down.

cues.zh: 过去三个月，我们从800人到了900、950，差不多这样。
cues.en: The last three months, we went from 800 to 900, 950, something like that.

cues.zh: 具体数字别引用我，但我觉得一千人左右是个拐点，我们想更谨慎地控制增长。
cues.en: Don’t quote me on the exact numbers, but I think there’s an inflection point around a thousand and we want to be much more careful how we grow.

cues.zh: 早期和现在一样，我们招了很多物理学家。
cues.en: Early on and now as well, we’ve hired a lot of physicists.

cues.zh: 理论物理学家学东西特别快。
cues.en: Theoretical physicists can learn things really fast.

cues.zh: 最近，随着我们持续招人，我们在研究侧和软件工程侧都设了很高的门槛，招了很多资深的人，包括这个领域其他公司的人，我们一直保持着非常严格的筛选。
cues.en: Even more recently, as we’ve continued to hire that, we’ve really had a high bar on both the research side and the software engineering side, have hired a lot of senior people, including folks who used to be at other companies in this space, and we’ve just continued to be very selective.

cues.zh: 从一百人扩展到一千人、一千人扩展到一万人很容易，但如果不注意确保每个人都有统一的目标，就会出问题。
cues.en: It’s very easy to go from a hundred to a thousand, a thousand to 10,000 without paying attention to making sure everyone has a unified purpose.

cues.zh: 这太强大了。
cues.en: It’s so powerful.

cues.zh: 如果你的公司里有很多各自为政的派系，都想做自己的事，都在为自己的利益优化，那就很难把事做成。
cues.en: If your company consists of a lot of different fiefdoms that all want to do their own thing, they’re all optimizing for their own thing, it’s very hard to get anything done.

cues.zh: 但如果每个人都能看到公司更大的目标，如果有信任、有把事情做对的投入，那就是一种超能力。
cues.en: But if everyone sees the broader purpose of the company, if there’s trust and there’s dedication to doing the right thing, that is a superpower.

cues.zh: 我认为这本身几乎能克服其他所有劣势。
cues.en: That in itself I think can overcome almost every other disadvantage.

cues.zh: 还有向Steve Jobs致敬，A级人才。
cues.en: And to Steve Jobs, A players.

cues.zh: A级人才希望环顾四周，看到的都是其他A级人才，这话换个说法就是这个意思。
cues.en: A players want to look around and see other A players is another way of saying that.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Correct.

cues.zh: 我不知道这关乎人性的哪一点，但看到那些没有执着地朝着单一使命奋进的人，确实让人泄气。
cues.en: I don’t know what that is about human nature, but it is demotivating to see people who are not obsessively driving towards a singular mission.

cues.zh: 而反过来，看到这样的人则超级激励人心。
cues.en: And it is on the flip side of that, super motivating to see that.

cues.zh: 这很有意思。
cues.en: It’s interesting.

cues.zh: 从你和这么多优秀人才共事的经历来看，要成为一名出色的AI研究员或工程师，需要具备什么？
cues.en: What’s it take to be a great AI researcher or engineer from everything you’ve seen from working with so many amazing people?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我认为首要品质，尤其是在研究方面，但其实两方面都是，就是思想开放。
cues.en: I think the number one quality, especially on the research side, but really both, is open mindedness.

cues.zh: 思想开放听起来很容易，对吧？
cues.en: Sounds easy to be open-minded, right?

cues.zh: 你就想，“哦，我对任何事都持开放态度。”但如果回想我自己在这个缩放假设上的早期经历，我看到的和别人看到的是同样的数据。
cues.en: You’re just like, “Oh, I’m open to anything.” But if I think about my own early history in this scaling hypothesis, I was seeing the same data others were seeing.

cues.zh: 我不觉得自己比共事过的几百人中的任何一个更会编程，或更擅长提出研究想法。
cues.en: I don’t think I was a better programmer or better at coming up with research ideas than any of the hundreds of people that I worked with.

cues.zh: 某种程度上，我还不如他们。
cues.en: In some ways, I was worse.

cues.zh: 我从来都不擅长精确编程、找 bug、写 GPU 内核。
cues.en: I’ve never precise programming of finding the bug, writing the GPU kernels.

cues.zh: 我能给你指出这里上百个比我更擅长这些的人。
cues.en: I could point you to a hundred people here who are better at that than I am.

cues.zh: 但我觉得我确实有一样不同的东西，那就是我愿意用全新的眼光去看待事物。
cues.en: But the thing that I think I did have that was different was that I was just willing to look at something with new eyes.

cues.zh: 人们说：“哦，我们还没有正确的算法。
cues.en: People said, “Oh, we don’t have the right algorithms yet.

cues.zh: 我们还没想出正确的做事方式。”而我就想：“哦，我不知道。
cues.en: We haven’t come up with the right way to do things.” And I was just like, “Oh, I don’t know.

cues.zh: 这个神经网络有 3000 万个参数。
cues.en: This neural net has 30 million parameters.

cues.zh: 如果我们给它 5000 万个呢？
cues.en: What if we gave it 50 million instead?

cues.zh: 咱们画几张图看看。”就是那种基本的科学心态，“哦天哪，”我看到某个可以改变的变量。
cues.en: Let’s plot some graphs.” That basic scientific mindset of like, “Oh man,” I see some variable that I could change.

cues.zh: 当它发生变化时会发生什么？
cues.en: What happens when it changes?

cues.zh: 我们来试试这些不同的方法，画个图看看。
cues.en: Let’s try these different things and create a graph.

cues.zh: 对偶数来说，这是世界上最简单的事，改变数量，这可不是博士级别的实验设计，这简单又愚蠢。
cues.en: For even, this was the simplest thing in the world, change the number of, this wasn’t PhD level experimental design, this was simple and stupid.

cues.zh: 只要告诉任何人这很重要，谁都能做到。
cues.en: Anyone could have done this if you just told them that it was important.

cues.zh: 理解起来也不难。
cues.en: It’s also not hard to understand.

cues.zh: 不需要多聪明就能想到这个。
cues.en: You didn’t need to be brilliant to come up with this.

cues.zh: 但把这两件事结合起来，极少数人，屈指可数的几个人，因为意识到了这一点，推动了整个领域的发展。
cues.en: But you put the two things together and some tiny number of people, some single digit number of people have driven forward the whole field by realizing this.

cues.zh: 事情往往就是这样。
cues.en: And it’s often like that.

cues.zh: 回顾历史上的发现，往往都是如此。
cues.en: If you look back at the discoveries in history, they’re often like that.

cues.zh: 所以这种开放的心态，这种愿意用新眼光去看待事物的态度，往往来自刚进入这个领域的人，经验在这方面常常是劣势，而这才是最重要的。
cues.en: And so this open-mindedness and this willingness to see with new eyes that often comes from being newer to the field, often experience is a disadvantage for this, that is the most important thing.

cues.zh: 这很难寻找和测试，但我认为它是最重要的，因为当你发现一些东西，一些真正全新的思考方式，当你有主动性去做这件事时，它绝对是具有变革性的。
cues.en: It’s very hard to look for and test for, but I think it’s the most important thing because when you find something, some really new way of thinking about things, when you have the initiative to do that, it’s absolutely transformative.

cues.zh: 并且能够进行快速实验，面对这种情况，保持开放的心态和好奇心，用全新的眼光看待数据，看看它实际上在说什么。
cues.en: And also be able to do kind of rapid experimentation and, in the face of that, be open-minded and curious and looking at the data with these fresh eyes and seeing what is it that it’s actually saying.

cues.zh: 这适用于机制可解释性。
cues.en: That applies in mechanistic interpretability.

cues.zh: 这是另一个例子。
cues.en: It’s another example of this.

cues.zh: 机制可解释性的一些早期工作非常简单，只是之前没有人想过去关注这个问题。
cues.en: Some of the early work and mechanistic interpretability so simple, it’s just no one thought to care about this question before.

cues.zh: 你说了成为一名伟大的AI研究员需要什么。
cues.en: You said what it takes to be a great AI researcher.

cues.zh: 我们能倒带回去吗，你会给对AI感兴趣的人什么建议？
cues.en: Can we rewind the clock back, what advice would you give to people interested in AI?

cues.zh: 他们很年轻，看起来……
cues.en: They’re young, looking…

cues.zh: 你会给对AI感兴趣的人什么建议？
cues.en: What advice would you give to people interested in AI?

cues.zh: 他们很年轻。
cues.en: They’re young.

cues.zh: 想着我怎样才能对世界产生影响？
cues.en: Looking forward to how can I make an impact on the world?

cues.zh: 我想我的第一条建议就是直接开始玩这些模型。
cues.en: I think my number one piece of advice is to just start playing with the models.

cues.zh: 其实我有点担心，这建议现在看起来太显而易见了。
cues.en: Actually, I worry a little, this seems like obvious advice now.

cues.zh: 我觉得三年前这并不明显，人们一开始会说，“哦，让我读读最新的强化学习论文。”你也该这么做，但现在模型和API更普及了，大家更多在动手实践。
cues.en: I think three years ago it wasn’t obvious and people started by, “Oh, let me read the latest reinforcement learning paper.” And you should do that as well, but now with wider availability of models and APIs, people are doing this more.

cues.zh: 但我认为，就是经验性知识。
cues.en: But, I think just experiential knowledge.

cues.zh: 这些模型是没人真正理解的新产物，所以要去动手积累经验。
cues.en: These models are new artifacts that no one really understands and so getting experience playing with them.

cues.zh: 我还想说，同样地，要去做新事情，往新方向思考，有太多东西还没被探索过。
cues.en: I would also say again, in line with the do something new, think in some new direction, there are all these things that haven’t been explored.

cues.zh: 比如，机制可解释性仍然非常新。
cues.en: For example, mechanistic interpretability is still very new.

cues.zh: 做这个可能比研究新的模型架构更好，因为它比以前更受关注了。
cues.en: It’s probably better to work on that than it is to work on new model architectures, because it’s more popular than it was before.

cues.zh: 大概有100人在做这个，但并没有1万人在做。
cues.en: There are probably 100 people working on it, but there aren’t like 10,000 people working on it.

cues.zh: 这就是一个非常有研究潜力的领域。
cues.en: And it’s just this fertile area for study.

cues.zh: 有太多唾手可得的成果，你走过去就能随手摘到。
cues.en: There’s so much low-hanging fruit, you can just walk by and you can pick things.

cues.zh: 不知为何，人们对此兴趣还不够。
cues.en: For whatever reason, people aren’t interested in it enough.

cues.zh: 我觉得在长时程学习和长时程任务方面，还有很多工作要做。
cues.en: I think there are some things around long horizon learning and long horizon tasks, where there’s a lot to be done.

cues.zh: 我认为在评估方面，我们研究评估的能力还处于非常早期的阶段，尤其是对于在现实世界中行动的动态系统。
cues.en: I think evaluations, we’re still very early in our ability to study evaluations, particularly for dynamic systems acting in the world.

cues.zh: 我觉得多智能体这块有些东西。
cues.en: I think there’s some stuff around multi-agent.

cues.zh: 我的建议是，滑向冰球将要去的地方，而且你不需要多聪明才能想到这一点。
cues.en: Skate where the puck is going is my advice, and you don’t have to be brilliant to think of it.

cues.zh: 五年后所有令人兴奋的东西，人们甚至会把它当作常识来提，但不知怎么的，总有一道障碍，让人们没有尽可能地加倍投入，或者害怕去做不流行的事情。
cues.en: All the things that are going to be exciting in five years, people even mention them as conventional wisdom, but it’s just somehow there’s this barrier that people don’t double down as much as they could, or they’re afraid to do something that’s not the popular thing.

cues.zh: 我不知道为什么会这样，但跨越那道障碍，是我的第一条建议。
cues.en: I don’t know why it happens, but getting over that barrier, that’s my number one piece of advice.

cues.zh: 我们能不能聊聊后训练。
cues.en: Let’s talk if we could a bit about post-training.

cues.zh: 看起来现代的后训练配方什么都有一点。
cues.en: So it seems that the modern post-training recipe has a little bit of everything.

cues.zh: 监督微调、RLHF、带RLAIF的宪法AI——
cues.en: So supervised fine-tuning, RLHF, the constitutional AI with RLAIF-

cues.zh: 最好的缩写。
cues.en: Best acronym.

cues.zh: 又是那个命名的问题。
cues.en: It’s the, again, that naming thing.

cues.zh: 然后是合成数据。
cues.en: And then synthetic data.

cues.zh: 似乎有大量合成数据，或者至少是在想办法获得高质量的合成数据。
cues.en: Seems like a lot of synthetic data, or at least trying to figure out ways to have high quality synthetic data.

cues.zh: 那么，如果这就是让 Anthropic 的 Claude 如此出色的秘诀，那这种魔力有多少来自预训练？
cues.en: So if this is a secret sauce that makes Anthropic clause so incredible, how much of the magic is in the pre-training?

cues.zh: 又有多少来自后训练？
cues.en: How much of it is in the post-training?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 首先，我们自己也无法完全准确地衡量这一点。
cues.en: So first of all, we’re not perfectly able to measure that ourselves.

cues.zh: 当你看到某种出色的角色能力时，有时很难分辨它来自预训练还是后训练。
cues.en: When you see some great character ability, sometimes it’s hard to tell whether it came from pre-training or post-training.

cues.zh: 我们开发了一些方法来尝试区分这两者，但效果并不完美。
cues.en: We developed ways to try and distinguish between those two, but they’re not perfect.

cues.zh: 第二点我想说的是，当存在优势时——我认为我们在强化学习方面总体上做得相当不错，也许是最好的，尽管我不确定，毕竟我看不到其他公司内部的情况。
cues.en: The second thing I would say is, when there is an advantage and I think we’ve been pretty good in general at RL, perhaps the best, although I don’t know, I don’t see what goes on inside other companies.

cues.zh: 通常并不是“天哪，我们有个别人没有的秘密魔法方法”。通常更像是“我们在基础设施上做得更好了，所以能跑得更久”，或者“我们拿到了更高质量的数据”，或者“我们能更好地过滤数据”，或者“我们能把这些方法结合起来实践”。
cues.en: Usually it isn’t, “Oh my God, we have this secret magic method that others don’t have.” Usually it’s like, “Well, we got better at the infrastructure so we could run it for longer,” or, “We were able to get higher quality data,” or, “We were able to filter our data better, or “We were able to combine these methods and practice.”

cues.zh: 通常就是些枯燥的实践和手艺活儿。
cues.en: It’s usually some boring matter of practice and trade craft.

cues.zh: 所以当我思考如何在这些模型的训练方式上做出特别的东西时，我更愿意把它想成设计飞机或汽车。
cues.en: So when I think about how to do something special in terms of how we train these models both, but even more so I really think of it a little more, again, as designing airplanes or cars.

cues.zh: 并不是说“哦天哪，
cues.en: It’s not just like, “Oh, man.

cues.zh: 我有蓝图了”，也许这能让你造出下一架飞机。
cues.en: I have the blueprint.” Maybe that makes you make the next airplane.

cues.zh: 但真正重要的，是我们思考设计过程的那种文化手艺，我觉得它比我们能发明的任何具体小装置都更重要。
cues.en: But there’s some cultural trade craft of how we think about the design process that I think is more important than any particular gizmo we’re able to invent.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那我来问问你一些具体的技术。
cues.en: Well, let me ask you about specific techniques.

cues.zh: 先说 RLHF，你怎么看，就从直觉、甚至哲学层面拉远来看……你觉得 RLHF 为什么效果这么好？
cues.en: So first on RLHF, what do you think, just zooming out intuition, almost philosophy … Why do you think RLHF works so well?

cues.zh: 回到扩展假说，绕过扩展假说的方法之一就是，如果你针对 X 训练，并且投入足够的算力，那你就能得到 X。
cues.en: If I go back to the scaling hypothesis, one of the ways to skate the scaling hypothesis is, if you train for X and you throw enough compute at it, then you get X.

cues.zh: 所以 RLHF 擅长让模型做人类想让它做的事，或者更准确地说，做那些短暂观察模型、考虑不同可能回复的人类所偏好的回复，这在安全性和能力两方面都不完美，因为人类往往无法完美识别模型想要什么，而人类当下想要的，未必是他们长期想要的。
cues.en: And so RLHF is good at doing what humans want the model to do, or at least to state it more precisely doing what humans who look at the model for a brief period of time and consider different possible responses, what they prefer as the response, which is not perfect from both the safety and capabilities perspective, in that humans are often not able to perfectly identify what the model wants and what humans want in the moment may not be what they want in the long term.

cues.zh: 这里面有很多微妙之处，但模型很擅长产出人类在浅层意义上想要的东西。
cues.en: So there’s a lot of subtlety there, but the models are good at producing what the humans in some shallow sense want.

cues.zh: 而且实际上你甚至不需要投入那么多算力，因为还有另一个因素，就是强大的预训练模型离任何目标都只差一半。
cues.en: And it actually turns out that you don’t even have to throw that much compute at it, because of another thing, which is this thing about a strong pre-trained model being halfway to anywhere.

cues.zh: 所以一旦你有了预训练模型，你就拥有了把模型引导到目标方向所需的全部表征。
cues.en: So once you have the pre-trained model, you have all the representations you need to get the model where you want it to go.

cues.zh: 那你觉得 RLHF 是让模型变得更聪明了，还是只是让它在人类眼里显得更聪明？
cues.en: So do you think RLHF makes the model smarter, or just appear smarter to the humans?

cues.zh: 我不认为它让模型变得更聪明。
cues.en: I don’t think it makes the model smarter.

cues.zh: 我也不认为它只是让模型显得更聪明。
cues.en: I don’t think it just makes the model appear smarter.

cues.zh: 这就像是 RLHF 弥合了人类和模型之间的鸿沟。
cues.en: It’s like RLHF bridges the gap between the human and the model.

cues.zh: 我可能有一个非常聪明但完全无法沟通的东西。
cues.en: I could have something really smart that can’t communicate at all.

cues.zh: 我们都认识这样的人，他们非常聪明，却说不清自己在说什么。
cues.en: We all know people like this, people who are really smart but can’t understand what they’re saying.

cues.zh: 所以我认为 RLHF 正好弥合了这个差距。
cues.en: So I think RLHF just bridges that gap.

cues.zh: 我认为这并不是我们做的唯一一种强化学习。
cues.en: I think it’s not the only kind of RL we do.

cues.zh: 它也不是未来会出现的唯一一种强化学习。
cues.en: It’s not the only kind of RL that will happen in the future.

cues.zh: 我认为强化学习有潜力让模型更聪明，让它们推理得更好，运行得更好，甚至让它们发展出新技能。
cues.en: I think RL has the potential to make models smarter, to make them reason better, to make them operate better, to make them develop new skills even.

cues.zh: 也许在某些情况下，这甚至可以通过人类反馈来实现。
cues.en: And perhaps that could be done even in some cases with human feedback.

cues.zh: 但今天我们做的这种 RLHF 大多还做不到这一点，尽管我们正很快开始具备这种能力。
cues.en: But, the kind of RLHF we do today mostly doesn’t do that yet, although we’re very quickly starting to be able to.

cues.zh: 但如果你看有用性这个指标，它会提升吗？
cues.en: But if you look at the metric of helpfulness, it increases that?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 它也会提升，Leopold 那篇文章里用的词是什么来着，“解除束缚”，基本上就是模型被束缚住了，然后你对它们做各种训练来解除束缚。
cues.en: It also increases, what was this word in Leopold’s essay, “unhobbling,” where basically the models are hobbled and then you do various trainings to them to unhobble them.

cues.zh: 我喜欢这个词，因为它很罕见。
cues.en: So I like that word, because it’s a rare word.

cues.zh: 所以我认为RLHF在某些方面解放了模型。
cues.en: So I think RLHF unhobbles the models in some ways.

cues.zh: 但还有其他方面，模型尚未被解放，需要被解放。
cues.en: And then there are other ways where that model hasn’t yet been unhobbled and needs to unhobble.

cues.zh: 如果从成本角度说，预训练是最贵的部分吗？
cues.en: If you can say in terms of cost, is pre-training the most expensive thing?

cues.zh: 还是后训练正在逐渐赶上？
cues.en: Or is post-training creep up to that?

cues.zh: 目前来看，预训练仍然占成本的大头。
cues.en: At the present moment, it is still the case that pre-training is the majority of the cost.

cues.zh: 我不知道未来会怎样，但我完全可以预见，未来后训练会占成本的大头。
cues.en: I don’t know what to expect in the future, but I could certainly anticipate a future where post-training is the majority of the cost.

cues.zh: 在你预见的那个未来里，后训练中成本高的是人类还是AI？
cues.en: In that future you anticipate, would it be the humans or the AI that’s the costly thing for the post-training?

cues.zh: 我不认为你能把人类规模扩大到足以获得高质量。
cues.en: I don’t think you can scale up humans enough to get high quality.

cues.zh: 任何依赖人类、消耗大量算力的方法，都必须依赖某种规模化监督手段，比如辩论、迭代放大之类的。
cues.en: Any kind of method that relies on humans and uses a large amount of compute, it’s going to have to rely on some scaled supervision method, like debate or iterated amplification or something like that.

cues.zh: 关于宪法式 AI 那组非常有意思的想法，你能先描述一下 2022 年 12 月论文里首次详述的内容，以及之后的发展吗？
cues.en: So on that super interesting set of ideas around constitutional AI, can you describe what it is as first detailed in December 2022 paper and beyond that.

cues.zh: 它是什么？
cues.en: What is it?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 这是两年前的事了。
cues.en: So this was from two years ago.

cues.zh: 基本思路是这样的，我们先说明 RLHF 是什么。
cues.en: The basic idea is, so we describe what RLHF is.

cues.zh: 你有一个模型，从里面采样两次。
cues.en: You have a model and you just sample from it twice.

cues.zh: 它给出两个可能的回答，然后你问：“人类，你更喜欢哪个回答？”另一种变体是：“给这个回答按一到七打分。”这很难，因为你需要扩大人类交互的规模，而且非常隐晦。
cues.en: It spits out two possible responses, and you’re like, “Human, which responses do you like better?” Or another variant of it is, “Rate this response on a scale of one to seven.” So that’s hard because you need to scale up human interaction and it’s very implicit.

cues.zh: 我不太清楚我想让模型做什么。
cues.en: I don’t have a sense of what I want the model to do.

cues.zh: 我只是知道这1000个人的平均意愿想让模型做什么。
cues.en: I just have a sense of what this average of 1,000 humans wants the model to do.

cues.zh: 所以有两个想法。
cues.en: So two ideas.

cues.zh: 一是，AI系统本身能否判断哪个回复更好？
cues.en: One is, could the AI system itself decide which response is better?

cues.zh: 你能不能把这两个回复展示给AI系统，问它哪个更好？
cues.en: Could you show the AI system these two responses and ask which response is better?

cues.zh: 第二，AI应该用什么标准？
cues.en: And then second, well, what criterion should the AI use?

cues.zh: 于是就有了这个想法：你有一份文档，可以称之为宪法，里面写明模型在回复时应该遵循的原则。
cues.en: And so then there’s this idea, you have a single document, a constitution if you will, that says, these are the principles the model should be using to respond.

cues.zh: AI系统会读取这些原则，同时也会读取环境和回复。
cues.en: And the AI system reads those reads principles as well as reading the environment and the response.

cues.zh: 然后它说：“这个AI模型做得怎么样？”这基本上是一种自我对弈的形式。
cues.en: And it says, “Well, how good did the AI model do?” It’s basically a form of self-play.

cues.zh: 你是在让模型和自己对抗训练。
cues.en: You’re training the model against itself.

cues.zh: 于是 AI 给出回应，然后你把它反馈回所谓的偏好模型，偏好模型再反过来喂给模型，让它变得更好。
cues.en: And so the AI gives the response and then you feed that back into what’s called the preference model, which in turn feeds the model to make it better.

cues.zh: 于是就形成了 AI、偏好模型和 AI 自身改进这三者的三角关系。
cues.en: So you have this triangle of the AI, the preference model, and the improvement of the AI itself.

cues.zh: 应该说，在宪法里，这套原则是人类可解读的。
cues.en: And we should say that in the constitution, the set of principles are human interpretable.

cues.zh: 它们——
cues.en: They’re-

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 这是人类和 AI 系统都能读懂的东西。
cues.en: It’s something both the human and the AI system can read.

cues.zh: 所以它有一种很好的可转译性或对称性。
cues.en: So it has this nice translatability or symmetry.

cues.zh: 实践中，我们既用模型宪法，也用 RLHF，还用一些其他方法。
cues.en: In practice, we both use a model constitution and we use RLHF and we use some of these other methods.

cues.zh: 所以它变成了工具箱里的一件工具，既减少了对 RLHF 的需求，又提升了 RLHF 每个数据点的使用价值。
cues.en: So it’s turned into one tool in a toolkit, that both reduces the need for RLHF and increases the value we get from using each data point of RLHF.

cues.zh: 它还会以有趣的方式与未来的推理型强化学习方法相互作用。
cues.en: It also interacts in interesting ways with future reasoning type RL methods.

cues.zh: 所以它是工具箱中的一个工具，但我认为它是个非常重要的工具。
cues.en: So it’s one tool in the toolkit, but I think it is a very important tool.

cues.zh: 嗯，对我们人类来说，它很有说服力。
cues.en: Well, it’s a compelling one to us humans.

cues.zh: 想想美国的开国元勋和美国的建国历程。
cues.en: Thinking about the founding fathers and the founding of the United States.

cues.zh: 自然的问题是，你认为由谁来定义宪法、宪法中的那套原则，以及如何定义？
cues.en: The natural question is who and how do you think it gets to define the constitution, the set of principles in the constitution?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 那我给一个务实的回答和一个更抽象的回答。
cues.en: So I’ll give a practical answer and a more abstract answer.

cues.zh: 我认为务实的回答是看实践，模型会被各种不同的客户使用。
cues.en: I think the practical answer is look in practice, models get used by all kinds of different customers.

cues.zh: 所以你可以有这样一个想法：模型可以拥有专门的规则或原则。
