cues.en: And so you can have this idea where the model can have specialized rules or principles.

cues.zh: 我们会隐式地微调模型的各个版本。
cues.en: We fine tune versions of models implicitly.

cues.zh: 我们讨论过显式地这样做，让人们可以把特殊原则构建到模型中。
cues.en: We’ve talked about doing it explicitly having special principles that people can build into the models.

cues.zh: 所以从实际角度看，不同的人给出的答案可能大不相同。
cues.en: So from a practical perspective, the answer can be very different from different people.

cues.zh: 客服专员的行为方式与律师截然不同，遵循的原则也不一样。
cues.en: A customer service agent behaves very differently from a lawyer and obeys different principles.

cues.zh: 但我认为，从根本上说，模型必须遵循一些特定的原则。
cues.en: But, I think at the base of it, there are specific principles that models have to obey.

cues.zh: 我觉得其中很多原则是人们都会认同的。
cues.en: I think a lot of them are things that people would agree with.

cues.zh: 大家都同意，我们不希望模型带来这些CBRN风险。
cues.en: Everyone agrees that we don’t want models to present these CBRN risks.

cues.zh: 我认为我们可以再进一步，认同民主和法治的一些基本原则。
cues.en: I think we can go a little further and agree with some basic principles of democracy and the rule of law.

cues.zh: 再往外延伸，就变得非常不确定了，而我们的目标通常是让模型更加中立，不宣扬特定观点，更像是明智的代理或顾问，帮你理清思路，并提出可能的考量因素。
cues.en: Beyond that, it gets very uncertain and there our goal is generally for the models to be more neutral, to not espouse a particular point of view and more just be wise agents or advisors that will help you think things through and will present possible considerations.

cues.zh: 但不要表达强烈或具体的观点。
cues.en: But don’t express strong or specific opinions.

cues.zh: OpenAI 发布了一份模型规范，清晰地、具体地定义了模型的一些目标，以及像 AB 这样的具体示例，说明模型应该如何表现。
cues.en: OpenAI released a model spec where it clearly, concretely defines some of the goals of the model and specific examples like AB, how the model should behave.

cues.zh: 你觉得这有意思吗？
cues.en: Do you find that interesting?

cues.zh: 顺便提一下，我相信出色的 John Schulman 参与其中。
cues.en: By the way I should mention, I believe the brilliant John Schulman was a part of that.

cues.zh: 他现在在 Anthropic。
cues.en: He’s now at Anthropic.

cues.zh: 你认为这是一个有用的方向吗？
cues.en: Do you think this is a useful direction?

cues.zh: Anthropic 是否也会发布一份模型规范？
cues.en: Might Anthropic release a model spec as well?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这是一个相当有用的方向。
cues.en: So I think that’s a pretty useful direction.

cues.zh: 再次强调，它与宪法 AI 有很多共同之处。
cues.en: Again, it has a lot in common with constitutional AI.

cues.zh: 所以，这又是一个竞相向上的例子。
cues.en: So again, another example of a race to the top.

cues.zh: 我们有一些我们认为更好、更负责任的做事方式。
cues.en: We have something that we think a better and more responsible way of doing things.

cues.zh: 这也是一种竞争优势。
cues.en: It’s also a competitive advantage.

cues.zh: 然后其他人发现它有优势，就开始做同样的事情。
cues.en: Then others discover that it has advantages and then start to do that thing.

cues.zh: 那之后我们就不再拥有竞争优势了，但从另一个角度看这是好事，因为现在大家都采纳了一种此前别人没有采纳的积极做法。
cues.en: We then no longer have the competitive advantage, but it’s good from the perspective that now everyone has adopted a positive practice that others were not adopting.

cues.zh: 所以我们的回应是：“看来我们需要新的竞争优势，才能继续推动这场竞赛向上发展。”这就是我对这件事的总体感受。
cues.en: And so our response to that is, “Well, looks like we need a new competitive advantage in order to keep driving this race upwards.” So that’s how I generally feel about that.

cues.zh: 我还认为，这些东西的每一种实现方式都各不相同。
cues.en: I also think every implementation of these things is different.

cues.zh: 模型规范里有一些内容是不在宪法AI里的，所以我们随时可以采纳这些内容，或者至少从中学习。
cues.en: So there were some things in the model spec that were not in constitutional AI, and so we can always adopt those things or at least learn from them.

cues.zh: 所以再次说，我认为这是一个积极动态的例子，我觉得我们都应该希望这个领域拥有这种动态。
cues.en: So again, I think this is an example of the positive dynamic that I think we should all want the field to have.

cues.zh: 我们来聊聊那篇精彩的文章《Machines of Loving Grace》。
cues.en: Let’s talk about the incredible essay Machines of Loving Grace.

cues.zh: 我推荐大家都读一读。
cues.en: I recommend everybody read it.

cues.zh: 篇幅挺长的。
cues.en: It’s a long one.

cues.zh: 确实相当长。
cues.en: It is rather long.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 读到关于积极未来具体是什么样子的实在想法，真让人耳目一新。
cues.en: It’s really refreshing to read concrete ideas about what a positive future looks like.

cues.zh: 而且你立场很大胆，因为你在时间点或具体应用上很可能是错的——
cues.en: And you took a bold stance because it’s very possible that you might be wrong on the dates or the specific applications-

cues.zh: 哦，是啊。
cues.en: Oh, yeah.

cues.zh: 我完全预料到，所有细节上我肯定会错。
cues.en: I’m fully expecting to well, definitely be wrong about all the details.

cues.zh: 整件事我可能错得离谱，人们会笑话我好多年。
cues.en: I might be just spectacularly wrong about the whole thing and people will laugh at me for years.

cues.zh: 未来就是这样。
cues.en: That’s just how the future works.

cues.zh: 所以你列举了AI带来的一系列具体积极影响，以及超级智能AI究竟如何加速生物学、化学等领域的突破，进而带来比如治愈大多数癌症、预防所有传染病、让人类寿命翻倍等等。
cues.en: So you provided a bunch of concrete positive impacts of AI and how exactly a super intelligent AI might accelerate the rate of breakthroughs in, for example, biology and chemistry, that would then lead to things like we cure most cancers, prevent all infectious disease, double the human lifespan and so on.

cues.zh: 先聊聊这篇文章吧。
cues.en: So let’s talk about this essay first.

cues.zh: 你能概括一下这篇文章的核心观点吗？
cues.en: Can you give a high-level vision of this essay?

cues.zh: 大家从中得到的关键收获是什么？
cues.en: And what are the key takeaways that people have?

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我花了很长时间，Anthropic也投入了大量精力，研究如何应对AI的风险。
cues.en: I have spent a lot of time, and in Anthropic has spent a lot of effort on how do we address the risks of AI?

cues.zh: 我们如何看待这些风险？
cues.en: How do we think about those risks?

cues.zh: 我们在努力推动一场向顶端的竞赛，这需要我们构建所有这些能力，而这些能力确实很酷。
cues.en: We’re trying to do a race to the top, what that requires us to build all these capabilities and the capabilities are cool.

cues.zh: 但我们努力的一大部分，是在应对风险。
cues.en: But, a big part of what we’re trying to do is address the risks.

cues.zh: 而为风险辩护的理由是，所有这些积极的东西，市场是一个非常健康的有机体。
cues.en: And the justification for that is like, well, all these positive things, the market is this very healthy organism.

cues.zh: 它会产出所有积极的东西。
cues.en: It’s going to produce all the positive things.

cues.zh: 那风险呢？
cues.en: The risks?

cues.zh: 我不知道，我们可能会缓解，也可能不会。
cues.en: I don’t know, we might mitigate them, we might not.

cues.zh: 所以，努力去缓解风险，能让我们产生更大的影响。
cues.en: And so we can have more impact by trying to mitigate the risks.

cues.zh: 但我注意到这种思维方式有一个缺陷，这并不是说我对风险的重视程度变了。
cues.en: But, I noticed that one flaw in that way of thinking, and it’s not a change in how seriously I take the risks.

cues.zh: 也许是我谈论风险的方式变了，那就是无论我刚才给出的那套推理多么合乎逻辑、多么理性。
cues.en: It’s maybe a change in how I talk about them, is that no matter how logical or rational, that line of reasoning that I just gave might be.

cues.zh: 如果你只谈论风险，你的大脑就只会想着风险。
cues.en: If you only talk about risks, your brain only thinks about risks.

cues.zh: 所以，我认为真正重要的是去理解，如果事情顺利发展会怎样？
cues.en: And so, I think it’s actually very important to understand, what if things do go well?

cues.zh: 而我们努力防范这些风险的根本原因，并不是因为我们害怕技术，也不是因为我们想让它慢下来。
cues.en: And the whole reason we’re trying to prevent these risks is not because we’re afraid of technology, not because we want to slow it down.

cues.zh: 而是因为如果我们能越过这些风险，如果我们能成功闯过这道难关——说得直白些——那么难关的另一边就是所有这些美好的事物。
cues.en: It’s because if we can get to the other side of these risks, if we can run the gauntlet successfully, to put it in stark terms, then on the other side of the gauntlet are all these great things.

cues.zh: 而这些事情是值得为之奋斗的。
cues.en: And these things are worth fighting for.

cues.zh: 而这些东西真的能激励人心。
cues.en: And these things can really inspire people.

cues.zh: 我想，因为……你看，所有这些投资者、所有这些风投、所有这些AI公司都在谈论AI的种种积极好处。
cues.en: And I think I imagine, because … Look, you have all these investors, all these VCs, all these AI companies talking about all the positive benefits of AI.

cues.zh: 但正如你指出的，这很奇怪。
cues.en: But as you point out, it’s weird.

cues.zh: 实际上，很少有人真正具体地谈论这些好处。
cues.en: There’s actually a dearth of really getting specific about it.

cues.zh: Twitter上有很多随便什么人发着那些闪闪发光的城市，还有那种拼命干、加速再加速、赶走……的氛围。就是一种非常激进的意识形态。
cues.en: There’s a lot of random people on Twitter posting these gleaming cities and this just vibe of grind, accelerate harder, kick out the … It’s just this very aggressive ideological.

cues.zh: 但接着你就想，“那你到底对什么感到兴奋呢？”
cues.en: But then you’re like, “Well, what are you actually excited about?”

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，对于一个真正从风险角度出发的人来说，试着认真解释一下好处是什么，会很有意思也很有价值，一方面因为我觉得这是大家都能支持的，另一方面我也希望人们能理解。
cues.en: And so, I figured that I think it would be interesting and valuable for someone who’s actually coming from the risk side to try and really make a try at explaining what the benefits are, both because I think it’s something we can all get behind and I want people to understand.

cues.zh: 我希望他们真正明白，这不是末日论者与加速主义者的对立。
cues.en: I want them to really understand that this isn’t Doomers versus Accelerationists.

cues.zh: 关键在于，如果你真正理解AI的发展方向——这或许是更重要的维度——即AI发展得快与AI发展得不快，那么你就会真正认识到其中的好处，并真心希望人类或文明抓住这些好处。
cues.en: This is that, if you have a true understanding of where things are going with AI, and maybe that’s the more important axis, AI is moving fast versus AI is not moving fast, then you really appreciate the benefits and you really want humanity or civilization to seize those benefits.

cues.zh: 但同时，你也会非常严肃地对待任何可能破坏这些好处的事情。
cues.en: But, you also get very serious about anything that could derail them.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，起点是讨论这个强大的AI——这是你喜欢的说法，全世界大多用AGI，但你不喜欢这个词，因为它基本上包袱太重，已经变得没有意义了。
cues.en: So I think the starting point is to talk about what this Powerful AI, which is the term you like to use, most of the world uses AGI, but you don’t like the term, because it’s basically has too much baggage, it’s become meaningless.

cues.zh: 就好像不管我们喜不喜欢，都被这些术语困住了。
cues.en: It’s like we’re stuck with the terms whether we like them or not.

cues.zh: 也许我们只能接受这些术语，我想改变它们的努力都是徒劳的。
cues.en: Maybe we’re stuck with the terms and my efforts to change them are futile.

cues.zh: 这很令人钦佩。
cues.en: It’s admirable.

cues.zh: 我再告诉你一件我不……这是个毫无意义的语义问题，但我一直在说——
cues.en: I’ll tell you what else I don’t … This is a pointless semantic point, but I keep talking about it-

cues.zh: 又回到命名的问题上了。
cues.en: It’s back to naming again.

cues.zh: 我就再来一次。
cues.en: I’m just going to do it once more.

cues.zh: 我觉得这有点像，假设是1995年，摩尔定律让计算机越来越快。
cues.en: I think it’s a little like, let’s say it was like 1995 and Moore’s law is making the computers faster.

cues.zh: 不知为何，大家都有这么个口头禅，“嗯，总有一天我们会拥有超级计算机。
cues.en: And for some reason there had been this verbal tick that everyone was like, “Well, someday we’re going to have supercomputers.

cues.zh: 超级计算机将能做所有这些事情……一旦有了超级计算机，我们就能测序基因组，我们就能做其他事情。”于是。
cues.en: And supercomputers are going to be able to do all these things that … Once we have supercomputers, we’ll be able to sequence the genome, we’ll be able to do other things.” And so.

cues.zh: 第一，确实如此，计算机越来越快，随着它们变快，就能做所有这些了不起的事情。
cues.en: One, it’s true, the computers are getting faster and as they get faster, they’re going to be able to do all these great things.

cues.zh: 但并没有一个明确的节点，让你觉得之前是超级计算机，之后就不是了。
cues.en: But there’s, there’s no discrete point at which you had a supercomputer and previous computers were no.

cues.zh: “超级计算机”是我们用的一个词，但它只是个模糊的说法，用来描述比今天更快的计算机。
cues.en: “Supercomputer” is a term we use, but it’s a vague term to just describe computers that are faster than what we have today.

cues.zh: 并不存在某个时刻，你跨过门槛然后惊呼：“天哪！
cues.en: There’s no point at which you pass the threshold and you’re like, “Oh, my God!

cues.zh: 我们在做一种全新的计算，全新的……所以我对AGI也是这种感觉。
cues.en: We’re doing a totally new type of computation and new … And so I feel that way about AGI.

cues.zh: 就是一条平滑的指数曲线。
cues.en: There’s just a smooth exponential.

cues.zh: 如果你说的AGI是指AI越来越好，逐渐能做越来越多人类做的事，直到比人类更聪明，然后还能继续变得更聪明，那我确实相信AGI。
cues.en: And if by AGI you mean AI is getting better and better, and gradually it’s going to do more and more of what humans do until it’s going to be smarter than humans, and then it’s going to get smarter even from there, then yes, I believe in AGI.

cues.zh: 但如果AGI是某种离散的、独立的东西——人们常常这么讲——那它就是个毫无意义的流行词。
cues.en: But, if AGI is some discrete or separate thing, which is the way people often talk about it, then it’s a meaningless buzzword.

cues.zh: 对我来说，它就是一种强大AI的纯粹形式，正好就是你所定义的那样。
cues.en: To me, it’s just a platonic form of a powerful AI, exactly how you define it.

cues.zh: 你定义得很好，所以在智能轴上，单论纯粹的智能，它比诺贝尔奖得主还聪明，正如你所描述的，在大多数相关学科都是如此。
cues.en: You define it very nicely, so on the intelligence axis, it’s just on pure intelligence, it’s smarter than a Nobel Prize winner as you describe across most relevant disciplines.

cues.zh: 好，那这只是智能方面。
cues.en: So okay, that’s just intelligence.

cues.zh: 所以它在创造力上也一样，能产生新想法，在各个学科都像巅峰期的诺贝尔奖得主那样。
cues.en: So it’s both in creativity and be able to generate new ideas, all that kind of stuff in every discipline, Nobel Prize winner in their prime.

cues.zh: 它能使用所有模态，这不用多解释，就是能在世界上所有模态中运作。
cues.en: It can use every modality, so this is self-explanatory, but just operate across all the modalities of the world.

cues.zh: 它能连续工作很多小时、几天甚至几周来完成任务，自己做详细规划，只在需要时才找你帮忙。
cues.en: It can go off for many hours, days and weeks to do tasks and do its own detailed planning and only ask you help when it’s needed.

cues.zh: 这其实挺有意思。
cues.en: This is actually interesting.

cues.zh: 我想你在文章里说过……再说一次，这是个赌注，赌它不会拥有实体，但它能控制实体工具。
cues.en: I think in the essay you said … Again, it’s a bet that it’s not going to be embodied, but it can control embodied tools.

cues.zh: 所以它能控制工具、机器人、实验室设备。用来训练它的资源之后可以被重新利用，用来运行它的数百万个副本，而每一个副本都是独立的，可以各自独立工作。
cues.en: So it can control tools, robots, laboratory equipment., the resource used to train it can then be repurposed to run millions of copies of it, and each of those copies would be independent that could do their own independent work.

cues.zh: 所以你可以对智能系统进行克隆。
cues.en: So you can do the cloning of the intelligence systems.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 从行业外看，你可能会以为这样的东西只有一个，对吧？
cues.en: You might imagine from outside the field that there’s only one of these, right?

cues.zh: 你只造了一个。
cues.en: You’ve only made one.

cues.zh: 但事实是，扩展速度非常快。
cues.en: But the truth is that the scale up is very quick.

cues.zh: 我们今天就在这么做。
cues.en: We do this today,.

cues.zh: 我们做出一个模型，然后部署成千上万个，甚至数万个它的实例。
cues.en: We make a model, and then we deploy thousands, maybe tens of thousands of instances of it.

cues.zh: 我认为到那个时候，肯定在两到三年内，不管我们有没有这些超强 AI，集群规模都会达到能够部署数百万个这样的实例的程度。
cues.en: I think by the time, certainly within two to three years, whether we have these super powerful AIs or not, clusters are going to get to the size where you’ll be able to deploy millions of these.

cues.zh: 而且它们会比人类更快。
cues.en: And they’ll be faster than humans.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你的设想是“哦，我们会有其中一个，而且造出来要花些时间”，我那里的观点是，不对。
cues.en: And so, if your picture is, “Oh, we’ll have one and it’ll take a while to make them,” my point there was, no.

cues.zh: 实际上你马上就能拥有数百万个。
cues.en: Actually you have millions of them right away.

cues.zh: 总的来说，它们学习和行动的速度能比人类快10到100倍。
cues.en: And in general they can learn and act 10 to 100 times faster than humans.

cues.zh: 所以那是对强大AI的一个非常好的定义。
cues.en: So that’s a really nice definition of powerful AI.

cues.zh: 好，就是这样。
cues.en: Okay, so that.

cues.zh: 但是，你也写道：“显然，这样的实体能够非常快地解决非常困难的问题，但弄清楚它有多快并非易事。
cues.en: But, you also write that, “Clearly such an entity would be capable of solving very difficult problems very fast, but it is not trivial to figure out how fast.

cues.zh: 两种‘极端’立场在我看来都是错的。”所以奇点是一个极端，相反的那个是另一个极端。
cues.en: Two “extreme” positions both seem false to me.” So the singularity is on the one extreme and the opposite and the other extreme.

cues.zh: 你能描述一下每个极端吗？
cues.en: Can you describe each of the extremes?

cues.zh: 可以。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 那么为什么呢？
cues.en: So why?

cues.zh: 那么，是的。
cues.en: So yeah.

cues.zh: 我们来描述一下这个极端。
cues.en: Let’s describe the extreme.

cues.zh: 所以一个极端会是：“好吧，你看。
cues.en: So one extreme would be, “Well, look.

cues.zh: 回看进化史，仿佛有过一次大加速：几十万年里只有单细胞生物，然后出现哺乳动物，再然后有了猿类。
cues.en: If we look at evolutionary history like there was this big acceleration, where for hundreds of thousands of years we just had single-celled organisms, and then we had mammals, and then we had apes.

cues.zh: 接着迅速演变成人类。
cues.en: And then that quickly turned to humans.

cues.zh: 人类很快建起了工业文明。所以，这个速度会持续加快，而且在人类层面上没有天花板。
cues.en: Humans quickly built industrial civilization.” And so, this is going to keep speeding up and there’s no ceiling at the human level.

cues.zh: 一旦模型比人类聪明得多，它们就会非常擅长构建下一代模型。
cues.en: Once models get much, much smarter than humans, they’ll get really good at building the next models.

cues.zh: 如果你写下一个简单的微分方程，比如这是个指数……所以接下来会发生的是，模型会造出更快的模型。
cues.en: And if you write down a simple differential equation, like this is an exponential … And so what’s going to happen is that models will build faster models.

cues.zh: 模型会造出更快的模型。
cues.en: Models will build faster models.

cues.zh: 而那些模型会造出能接管世界的纳米机器人，产出远超其他方式的能量。
cues.en: And those models will build nanobots that can take over the world and produce much more energy than you could produce otherwise.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你只是解出这个抽象微分方程，那么在我们造出第一个比人类更强大的AI之后大约五天，世界就会被这些AI填满，遍布所有可能被发明出来的技术，就是将会被发明出来的技术。
cues.en: And so, if you just kind of solve this abstract differential equation, then like five days after we build the first AI that’s more powerful than humans, then the world will be filled with these AIs in every possible technology that could be invented, like will be invented.

cues.zh: 我有点夸张了，但我认为那是一种极端情况。
cues.en: I’m caricaturing this a little bit, but I think that’s one extreme.

cues.zh: 我认为情况并非如此，原因之一是，我觉得他们只是忽视了物理定律。
cues.en: And the reason that I think that’s not the case is that, one, I think they just neglect the laws of physics.

cues.zh: 在物理世界里，做事情的速度是有上限的。
cues.en: It’s only possible to do things so fast in the physical world.

cues.zh: 其中一些循环要经过生产更快的硬件。
cues.en: Some of those loops go through producing faster hardware.

cues.zh: 生产更快的硬件需要很长时间。
cues.en: It takes a long time to produce faster hardware.

cues.zh: 事情都需要很长时间。
cues.en: Things take a long time.

cues.zh: 还有复杂度这个问题。
cues.en: There’s this issue of complexity.

cues.zh: 我认为无论你多聪明，人们总说，“哦，我们可以建立生物系统的模型，做到生物系统能做的一切……” 听着，我认为计算建模能做很多事。
cues.en: I think no matter how smart you are, people talk about, “Oh, we can make models of biological systems that’ll do everything the biological systems … ” Look, I think computational modeling can do a lot.

cues.zh: 我在生物学领域工作时，做过大量计算建模。
cues.en: I did a lot of computational modeling when I worked in biology.

cues.zh: 但有很多事情你没法预测会怎样……它们足够复杂，以至于只要不断迭代、不断跑实验，就能胜过任何建模，不管做建模的系统有多聪明。
cues.en: But just there are a lot of things that you can’t predict how … They’re complex enough that just iterating, just running the experiment is going to beat any modeling, no matter how smart the system doing the modeling is.

cues.zh: 那么，即使它不与物理世界交互，光是建模本身也会很难？
cues.en: Well, even if it’s not interacting with the physical world, just the modeling is going to be hard?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 建模会很难，而且让模型与物理世界相匹配也会很难。
cues.en: Well, the modeling is going to be hard and getting the model to match the physical world is going to be

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 所以它确实必须与物理世界交互才能验证。
cues.en: So it does have to interact with the physical world to verify.

cues.zh: 但你只要看看哪怕最简单的问题。
cues.en: But you just look at even the simplest problems.

cues.zh: 我想我谈到过三体问题，或者简单的混沌预测，或者预测经济。
cues.en: I think I talk about The Three-Body Problem or simple chaotic prediction, or predicting the economy.

cues.zh: 预测两年后的经济真的很难。
cues.en: It’s really hard to predict the economy two years out.

cues.zh: 也许人类能预测下个季度的经济走向，也许根本做不到。
cues.en: Maybe the case is humans can predict what’s going to happen in the economy next quarter, or they can’t really do that.

cues.zh: 也许一个聪明无数倍的 AI，也只能预测一年左右，而不是……计算机智能指数级增长，预测能力却只是线性提升。
cues.en: Maybe a AI that’s a zillion times smarter can only predict it out a year or something, instead of … You have these exponential increase in computer intelligence for linear increase in ability to predict.

cues.zh: 生物分子相互作用也是一样。
cues.en: Same with again, like biological molecules interacting.

cues.zh: 当你扰动一个复杂系统时，你根本不知道会发生什么。
cues.en: You don’t know what’s going to happen when you perturb a complex system.

cues.zh: 你能在其中找到简单的部分，如果你更聪明，你就更擅长找到这些简单的部分。
cues.en: You can find simple parts in it, if you’re smarter, you’re better at finding these simple parts.

cues.zh: 然后我觉得人类制度，人类制度真的很难。
cues.en: And then I think human institutions, human institutions are really difficult.

cues.zh: 一直很难让人参与进来。
cues.en: It’s been a hard to get people.

cues.zh: 我不会举具体例子，但即便是我们开发的技术，也很难让人们采用，哪怕是那些有效性非常非常明确的技术。
cues.en: I won’t give specific examples, but it’s been hard to get people to adopt even the technologies that we’ve developed, even ones where the case for their efficacy is very, very strong.

cues.zh: 人们有顾虑。
cues.en: People have concerns.

cues.zh: 他们觉得这是阴谋论。
cues.en: They think things are conspiracy theories.

cues.zh: 这真的非常困难。
cues.en: It’s just been very difficult.

cues.zh: 让非常简单的东西通过监管体系也非常困难。
cues.en: It’s also been very difficult to get very simple things through the regulatory system.

cues.zh: 我不想贬低任何在技术监管体系中工作的人。
cues.en: And I don’t want to disparage anyone who works in regulatory systems of any technology.

cues.zh: 他们必须应对很多难题。
cues.en: There are hard they have to deal with.

cues.zh: 他们必须拯救生命。
cues.en: They have to save lives.

cues.zh: 但整个体系，我认为做出了一些明显的权衡，而这些权衡远未最大化人类福祉。
cues.en: But the system as a whole, I think makes some obvious trade-offs that are very far from maximizing human welfare.

cues.zh: 所以，如果我们把 AI 系统引入这些人类体系，往往智能水平可能根本不是限制因素。
cues.en: And so, if we bring AI systems into these human systems, often the level of intelligence may just not be the limiting factor.

cues.zh: 有些事情可能就是需要很长时间才能完成。
cues.en: It just may be that it takes a long time to do something.

cues.zh: 现在，如果 AI 系统绕过了所有政府，直接宣称“我是世界独裁者，我想干什么就干什么”，那有些事情它确实能做到。
cues.en: Now, if the AI system circumvented all governments, if it just said, “I’m dictator of the world and I’m going to do whatever,” some of these things it could do.

cues.zh: 但这些事情同样跟复杂性有关。
cues.en: Again, the things have to do with complexity.

cues.zh: 我仍然认为很多事情需要花不少时间。
cues.en: I still think a lot of things would take a while.

cues.zh: 我不认为 AI 系统能产出大量能源或者登上月球就能帮上忙。
cues.en: I don’t think it helps that the AI systems can produce a lot of energy or go to the moon.

cues.zh: 比如有人在文章评论里回应说，AI 系统可以产出大量能源，还能造出更聪明的 AI 系统。
cues.en: Like some people in comments responded to the essay saying the AI system can produce a lot of energy and smarter AI systems.

cues.zh: 这是没抓住重点。
cues.en: That’s missing the point.

cues.zh: 那种循环解决不了我在这里说的关键问题。
cues.en: That kind of cycle doesn’t solve the key problems that I’m talking about here.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得有不少人没抓住这个重点。
cues.en: So I think a bunch of people missed the point there.

cues.zh: 但即便它完全不对齐，并且能绕过所有这些人类障碍，它也会遇到麻烦。
cues.en: But even if it were completely unaligned and could get around all these human obstacles it would have trouble.

cues.zh: 但话说回来，如果你想让这个AI系统不接管世界、不毁灭人类，那它基本上就得遵守人类的基本法律。
cues.en: But again, if you want this to be an AI system that doesn’t take over the world, that doesn’t destroy humanity, then basically it’s going to need to follow basic human laws.

cues.zh: 如果我们想要一个真正美好的世界，就得有一个能与人类互动的AI系统，而不是一个自创法律体系、无视所有法律或诸如此类的系统。
cues.en: If we want to have an actually good world, we’re going to have to have an AI system that interacts with humans, not one that creates its own legal system, or disregards all the laws or all of that.

cues.zh: 所以，尽管这些流程效率低下，我们还是得应对它们，因为这些系统的推行需要有某种大众的、民主的合法性。
cues.en: So as inefficient as these processes are, we’re going to have to deal with them, because there needs to be some popular and democratic legitimacy in how these systems are rolled out.

cues.zh: 不能让一小群开发这些系统的人说：“这就是对所有人最好的。”我认为这是错的，而且我认为实际上这根本行不通。
cues.en: We can’t have a small group of people who are developing these systems say, “This is what’s best for everyone.” I think it’s wrong, and I think in practice it’s not going to work anyway.

cues.zh: 把这些都放在一起，我们不会在五分钟内改变世界、上传所有人。
cues.en: So you put all those things together and we’re not going change the world and upload everyone in five minutes.

cues.zh: 第一，我觉得这不会发生；第二，就算真能发生，这也不是通向美好世界的方式。
cues.en: A, I don’t think it’s going to happen and B, to the extent that it could happen.,It’s not the way to lead to a good world.

cues.zh: 这是一方面。
cues.en: So that’s on one side.

cues.zh: 另一方面，还有另一组观点，我其实在某些方面更认同它，那就是：看，我们以前也见过生产力大幅提升。
cues.en: On the other side, there’s another set of perspectives, which I have actually in some ways more sympathy for, which is, look, we’ve seen big productivity increases before.

cues.zh: 经济学家很熟悉研究计算机革命和互联网革命带来的生产力提升。
cues.en: Economists are familiar with studying the productivity increases that came from the computer revolution and internet revolution.

cues.zh: 而总的来说，那些生产力提升并不尽如人意。
cues.en: And generally those productivity increases were underwhelming.

cues.zh: 它们比你想象的要小。
cues.en: They were less than you might imagine.

cues.zh: Robert Solow 有句话：“你到处都能看到计算机革命，唯独在生产力统计数据里看不到。”那为什么会这样？
cues.en: There was a quote from Robert Solow, “You see the computer revolution everywhere except the productivity statistics.” So why is this the case?

cues.zh: 人们会指出公司的结构、企业的结构，以及把我们现有技术推广到世界极贫困地区有多缓慢，这些我在文章里谈到了。
cues.en: People point to the structure of firms, the structure of enterprises, how slow it’s been to roll out our existing technology to very poor parts of the world, which I talk about in the essay.

cues.zh: 我们怎么把这些技术送到世界上最贫困的地区？那些地方连手机技术、电脑、医药都落后，更不用说还没发明出来的新奇AI了。
cues.en: How do we get these technologies to the poorest parts of the world that are behind on cell phone technology, computers, medicine, let alone newfangled AI that hasn’t been invented yet.

cues.zh: 所以你可能会有这样一种看法：“嗯，这在技术上了不起，但这是全有或全无的事。”
cues.en: So you could have a perspective that’s like, “Well, this is amazing technically, but it’s all or nothing burger.

cues.zh: 我认为Tyler Cowen写了一些回应我文章的东西，他就是那种看法。
cues.en: I think Tyler Cowen who wrote something in response to my essay has that perspective.

cues.zh: 我觉得他认为彻底变革最终会发生，但他认为需要50到100年。
cues.en: I think he thinks the radical change will happen eventually, but he thinks it’ll take 50 or 100 years.

cues.zh: 你甚至可以对整件事持有更静态的看法。
cues.en: And you could have even more static perspectives on the whole thing.

cues.zh: 我觉得这话有一定道理。
cues.en: I think there’s some truth to it.

cues.zh: 我觉得时间尺度太长了，这我能看出来。
cues.en: I think the time scale is just too long and I can see it.

cues.zh: 对今天的 AI，我其实两边都能理解。
cues.en: I can actually see both sides with today’s AI.

cues.zh: 我们的很多客户是大型企业，习惯了按某种固定方式做事。
cues.en: So a lot of our customers are large enterprises who are used to doing things a certain way.

cues.zh: 我在和政府部门交流时也看到了这一点，对吧？
cues.en: I’ve also seen it in talking to governments, right?

cues.zh: 那些都是典型的机构，是变化缓慢的实体。
cues.en: Those are prototypical institutions, entities that are slow to change.

cues.zh: 但我反复看到的动态是：没错，调转船头需要很长时间。
cues.en: But, the dynamic I see over and over again is yes, it takes a long time to move the ship.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 有很多阻力和不理解。
cues.en: There’s a lot of resistance and lack of understanding.

cues.zh: 但让我觉得进步最终会以中等速度发生——不是极快，而是中等偏快——的原因是，你去跟人聊……我发现一次又一次，在大公司里，甚至在那些出乎意料地走在前面的政府里，你会发现两样推动事情前进的东西。
cues.en: But, the thing that makes me feel that progress will in the end happen moderately fast, not incredibly fast, but moderately fast, is that you talk to … What I find is I find over and over again, again in large companies, even in governments which have been actually surprisingly forward leaning, you find two things that move things forward.

cues.zh: 第一，你会在公司里、政府里发现一小部分人，他们真正看清了大局，看懂了整个规模扩展的假设，明白AI将走向何方，或者至少明白在他们所在行业里它会走向何方。
cues.en: One, you find a small fraction of people within a company, within a government, who really see the big picture, who see the whole scaling hypothesis, who understand where AI is going, or at least understand where it’s going within their industry.

cues.zh: 在当前的美国政府里，就有少数这样的人，他们真正看清了全局。
cues.en: And there are a few people like that within the current US government who really see the whole picture.

cues.zh: 这些人明白，这是世界上最重要的事，直到他们为之奔走呼吁。
cues.en: And those people see that this is the most important thing in the world until they agitate for it.

cues.zh: 问题是，单靠他们不足以成事，因为他们只是庞大组织里的一小群人。
cues.en: And the thing they alone are not enough to succeed, because there are a small set of people within a large organization.

cues.zh: 但随着技术开始铺开，随着它在一些地方、在那些最愿意接纳它的人当中取得成功，竞争的阴影给了他们顺风，因为他们可以在自己的庞大组织内部指出这一点。
cues.en: But, as the technology starts to roll out, as it succeeds in some places in the folks who are most willing to adopt it, the specter of competition gives them a wind at their backs, because they can point within their large organization.

cues.zh: 他们会说：“你看，其他那些人都在这么干。”一家银行可以说：“你看，这个新奇的的对冲基金在搞这种事。
cues.en: They can say, “Look, these other guys are doing this.” One bank can say, “Look, this newfangled hedge fund is doing this thing.

cues.zh: 他们要抢我们的饭碗了。”在美国，我们可以说，我们担心中国会赶在我们前面实现。
cues.en: They’re going to eat our lunch.” In the US, we can say we’re afraid China’s going to get there before we are.

cues.zh: 而这种组合，竞争的幽灵，加上这些组织内部少数有远见的人——这些组织在很多方面已经僵化了——把这两者放在一起，居然真能促成一些事情发生。
cues.en: And that combination, the specter of competition plus a few visionaries within these, the organizations that in many ways are sclerotic, you put those two things together and it actually makes something happen.

cues.zh: 这很有意思。
cues.en: It’s interesting.

cues.zh: 这是两者之间一场势均力敌的较量，因为惯性非常强大，但最终经过足够长的时间，创新的方法会突破。
cues.en: It’s a balanced fight between the two, because inertia is very powerful, but eventually over enough time, the innovative approach breaks through.

cues.zh: 我见过这种情况发生。
cues.en: And I’ve seen that happen.

cues.zh: 我一次又一次地看到这样的发展轨迹，就像障碍就在那里，阻碍进步的障碍、复杂性、不知道如何使用模型、如何部署它们，这些障碍都在那里。
cues.en: I’ve seen the arc of that over and over again, and it’s like the barriers are there, the barriers to progress, the complexity, not knowing how to use the model, how to deploy them are there.

cues.zh: 有一阵子，它们似乎会永远持续下去，改变不会发生。
cues.en: And for a bit it seems like they’re going to last forever, change doesn’t happen.

cues.zh: 但最终改变还是发生了，而且总是来自少数人。
cues.en: But, then eventually change happens and always comes from a few people.

cues.zh: 我在AI领域内倡导扩展假说时，别人不理解，我也有同样的感受。
cues.en: I felt the same way when I was an advocate of the scaling hypothesis within the AI field itself and others didn’t get it.

cues.zh: 感觉就像永远不会有人理解。
cues.en: It felt like no one would ever get it.

cues.zh: 然后感觉我们掌握了一个几乎没人知道的秘密。
cues.en: Then it felt like we had a secret almost no one ever had.

cues.zh: 再然后，几年之后，每个人都知道了这个秘密。
cues.en: And then, a couple years later, everyone has the secret.

cues.zh: 所以，我认为AI在现实世界中的部署也会是这样。
cues.en: And so, I think that’s how it’s going to go with deployment AI in the world.

cues.zh: 障碍会逐渐瓦解，然后一下子全部崩塌。
cues.en: The barriers are going to fall apart gradually and then all at once.

cues.zh: 所以，我认为这会更——而这只是直觉。
cues.en: And so, I think this is going to be more, and this is just an instinct.

cues.zh: 我很容易看出自己错在哪里。
cues.en: I could easily see how I’m wrong.

cues.zh: 我认为这更可能是五到十年，正如我在文章中所说，而不是五十或一百年。
cues.en: I think it’s going to be more five or 10 years, as I say in the essay than it’s going to be 50 or 100 years.

cues.zh: 我也觉得这得五到十年，而不是五到十个小时，因为我刚看清人类系统是怎么运作的。
cues.en: I also think it’s going to be five or 10 years more than it’s going to be five or 10 hours, because I’ve just seen how human systems work.

cues.zh: 我觉得很多写下那些微分方程的人，说AI会造出更强大的AI的人，他们无法理解这些事情怎么可能不会变化得那么快。
cues.en: And I think a lot of these people who write down these differential equations, who say AI is going to make more powerful AI, who can’t understand how it could possibly be the case that these things won’t change so fast.

cues.zh: 我觉得他们不懂这些东西。
cues.en: I think they don’t understand these things.

cues.zh: 那么在你看来，我们实现AGI的时间线是怎样的，也就是
cues.en: So what to you is the timeline to where we achieve AGI, A.K.A.

cues.zh: 强大的AI，也就是
cues.en: powerful AI, A.K.A.

cues.zh: 超级有用的AI？
cues.en: super useful AI?

cues.zh: 我打算开始这么叫它了。
cues.en: I’m going to start calling it that.

cues.zh: 这是关于命名的争论。
cues.en: It’s a debate about naming.

cues.zh: 纯粹智能上比每个相关学科的诺贝尔奖得主都更聪明，以及我们刚才说的所有那些。
cues.en: On pure intelligence smarter than a Nobel Prize winner in every relevant discipline and all the things we’ve said.

cues.zh: 模态上，能自己连续几天、几周做事，能自己做一个……你知道吗？
cues.en: Modality, can go and do stuff on its own for days, weeks, and do biology experiments on its own in one … You know what?

cues.zh: 我们就只聊生物学吧，因为你在生物学和健康那部分已经说服我了。
cues.en: Let’s just stick to biology, because you sold me on the whole biology and health section.

cues.zh: 这太让人兴奋了……从科学的角度来说，我都激动起来了。
cues.en: And that’s so exciting from just … I was getting giddy from a scientific perspective.

cues.zh: 这让我想当生物学家了。
cues.en: It made me want to be a biologist.

cues.zh: 所以，不是。
cues.en: So no,.

cues.zh: 不是。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 这就是我写它时的感受，就像，如果我们能把它实现，这将是多么美好的未来。
cues.en: This was the feeling I had when I was writing it, that it’s like, this would be such a beautiful future if we can just make it happen.

cues.zh: 如果我们能扫清那些地雷，把它实现。
cues.en: If we can just get the landmines out of the way and make it happen.

cues.zh: 只要我们能……它背后有如此多的美、优雅和道德力量。而且这是我们都应该能够达成一致的事情。
cues.en: There’s so much beauty and elegance and moral force behind it if we can just … And it’s something we should all be able to agree on.

cues.zh: 尽管我们在所有这些政治问题上争论不休，这件事真的能把我们团结起来吗？
cues.en: As much as we fight about all these political questions, is this something that could actually bring us together?

cues.zh: 但你刚才在问，我们什么时候能实现这个？
cues.en: But you were asking when will we get this?

cues.zh: 什么时候？
cues.en: When?

cues.zh: 你觉得是什么时候？
cues.en: When do you think?

cues.zh: 只是把数字摆出来。
cues.en: Just putting numbers on the table.

cues.zh: 当然，这是我多年来一直在纠结的问题，我完全没有把握。
cues.en: This is, of course, the thing I’ve been grappling with for many years, and I’m not at all confident.

cues.zh: 如果我说2026年或2027年，Twitter上会有无数人跳出来说：“AI CEO说2026年、2020年……”然后接下来两年里，这句话会被反复引用，说这就是我认定的时间点。
cues.en: If I say 2026 or 2027, there will be a zillion people on Twitter who will be like, “AI CEO said 2026, 2020 … ” and it’ll be repeated for the next two years that this is definitely when I think it’s going to happen.

cues.zh: 所以不管是谁在剪辑这些片段，都会把我刚说的话剪掉，只留下我接下来要说的话。
cues.en: So whoever’s exerting these clips will crop out the thing I just said and only say the thing I’m about to say.

cues.zh: 但我还是说吧——
cues.en: But I’ll just say it anyway-

cues.zh: 随你们怎么玩。
cues.en: Have fun with it.

cues.zh: 如果你把我们目前看到的曲线外推。
cues.en: So if you extrapolate the curves that we’ve had so far.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 如果你说：“嗯，我不知道。
cues.en: If you say, “Well, I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我们开始达到博士水平了，去年我们还是本科水平，前年我们还是高中生水平。”当然，你可以争论是在哪些任务上，以及我们仍然缺少哪些模态，但这些都在被补上。
cues.en: We’re starting to get to PhD level, and last year we were at undergraduate level and the year before we were at the level of a high school student.” Again, you can quibble with at what tasks and for what we’re still missing modalities, but those are being added.

cues.zh: 计算机使用功能被加入，就像ImageGen被加入一样，图像生成功能也已加入。
cues.en: Computer use was added, like ImageEn was added, image generation has been added.

cues.zh: 这完全不够科学，但如果你只是粗略观察这些能力的增长速度，确实会让人觉得我们会在2026或2027年实现目标。
cues.en: And this is totally unscientific, but if you just eyeball the rate at which these capabilities are increasing, it does make you think that we’ll get there by 2026 or 2027.

cues.zh: 当然，很多事情可能会打乱这个进程。
cues.en: Again, lots of things could derail it.

cues.zh: 我们可能会耗尽数据。
cues.en: We could run out of data.

cues.zh: 我们可能无法按需扩展集群规模。
cues.en: We might not be able to scale clusters as much as we want.

cues.zh: 也许台湾出了什么事，然后我们就无法生产足够多的GPU。
cues.en: Maybe Taiwan gets blown up or something, and then we can’t produce as many GPUs as we want.

cues.zh: 所以有各种——
cues.en: So there are all-

cues.zh: 然后我们就无法生产足够多的GPU。
cues.en: Then we can’t produce as many GPUs as we want.

cues.zh: 所以有各种因素可能打乱整个进程。
cues.en: So there are all kinds of things that could derail the whole process.

cues.zh: 所以我不完全相信直线外推，但如果你相信直线外推，我们会在2026或2027年实现目标。
cues.en: So I don’t fully believe the straight line extrapolation, but if you believe the straight line extrapolation, we’ll get there in 2026 or 2027.

cues.zh: 我觉得最有可能的是，相对于那个时间点会有一些轻微的延迟。
cues.en: I think the most likely is that there are some mild delay relative to that.

cues.zh: 我不知道那个延迟是什么，但我认为它可能会按计划发生。
cues.en: I don’t know what that delay is, but I think it could happen on schedule.

cues.zh: 我认为可能会有轻微的延迟。
cues.en: I think there could be a mild delay.

cues.zh: 我认为仍然存在一些情况，它在一百年内不会发生。
cues.en: I think there are still worlds where it doesn’t happen in a hundred years.

cues.zh: 这些情况的数量正在迅速减少。
cues.en: The number of those worlds is rapidly decreasing.

cues.zh: 我们正在迅速耗尽真正有说服力的阻碍因素，也就是那些真正令人信服的理由，说明为什么这不会在未来几年内发生。
cues.en: We are rapidly running out of truly convincing blockers, truly compelling reasons why this will not happen in the next few years.

cues.zh: 2020年时这类阻碍因素要多得多，尽管我当时的猜测、我的直觉是，我们会挺过所有这些阻碍。
cues.en: There were a lot more in 2020, although my guess, my hunch at that time was that we’ll make it through all those blockers.

cues.zh: 所以作为一个目睹了大多数阻碍被清除的人，我怀疑、我的直觉、我的猜想是，剩下的那些不会阻挡我们。
cues.en: So sitting as someone who has seen most of the blockers cleared out of the way, I suspect, my hunch, my suspicion is that the rest of them will not block us.

cues.zh: 但你看，说到底，我不想把这说成是一种科学预测。
cues.en: But look, at the end of the day, I don’t want to represent this as a scientific prediction.

cues.zh: 人们称之为缩放定律。
cues.en: People call them scaling laws.

cues.zh: 这是个误称。
cues.en: That’s a misnomer.

cues.zh: 就像摩尔定律也是个误称一样。
cues.en: Like Moore’s law is a misnomer.

cues.zh: 摩尔定律、缩放定律，它们都不是宇宙的法则。
cues.en: Moore’s laws, scaling laws, they’re not laws of the universe.

cues.zh: 它们是经验性的规律。
cues.en: They’re empirical regularities.

cues.zh: 我愿意押注它们会继续成立，但我并不确定。
cues.en: I am going to bet in favor of them continuing, but I’m not certain of that.

cues.zh: 所以你详细描述了那种压缩的21世纪，AGI将如何推动生物学和医学领域的一系列突破，以我刚才提到的各种方式帮助我们。
cues.en: So you extensively described sort of the compressed 21st century, how AGI will help set forth a chain of breakthroughs in biology and medicine that help us in all these kinds of ways that I mentioned.

cues.zh: 它可能做的最早的几步是什么？
cues.en: What are the early steps it might do?

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我问了Claude该问你哪些好问题，Claude让我问：在这个未来里，你认为一个从事AGI研究的生物学家典型的一天是什么样的？
cues.en: And by the way, I asked Claude good questions to ask you and Claude told me to ask, what do you think is a typical day for a biologist working on AGI look like in this future?

cues.zh: 是啊，是啊。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: Claude很好奇。
cues.en: Claude is curious.

cues.zh: 好，我先从你最初的问题开始，然后再回答那个。
cues.en: Well, let me start with your first questions and then I’ll answer that.

cues.zh: Claude想知道他的未来是什么样，对吧？
cues.en: Claude wants to know what’s in his future, right?

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Exactly.

cues.zh: 我会和谁一起工作？
cues.en: Who am I going to be working with?

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Exactly.

cues.zh: 我觉得我在文章里重点强调的一点，让我回到这个想法，因为它真的对我影响很大，就是在大型组织和系统中，最终会有少数人或少数新想法，让事情走向与以往不同的方向，他们对发展轨迹的影响大得不成比例。
cues.en: So I think one of the things when I went hard on in the essay is let me go back to this idea of, because it’s really had an impact on me, this idea that within large organizations and systems, there end up being a few people or a few new ideas who cause things to go in a different direction than they would’ve before who kind of disproportionately affect the trajectory.

cues.zh: 有很多类似的情况在发生，对吧？
cues.en: There’s a bunch of the same thing going on, right?

cues.zh: 如果你想想医疗领域，有数万亿美元用于支付Medicare和其他医疗保险，而NIH是1000亿美元。
cues.en: If you think about the health world, there’s like trillions of dollars to pay out Medicare and other health insurance and then the NIH is 100 billion.

cues.zh: 然后，如果想想真正带来革命性变化的少数几件事，它们可能只占其中很小一部分。
cues.en: And then if I think of the few things that have really revolutionized anything, it could be encapsulated in a small fraction of that.

cues.zh: 所以当我思考AI将在哪里产生影响时，我想：“AI能否把那小部分变成大得多的部分，并提升其质量？”
cues.en: And so when I think of where will AI have an impact, I’m like, “Can AI turn that small fraction into a much larger fraction and raise its quality?”

cues.zh: 在生物学领域，我的经验是，生物学最大的问题在于你看不到正在发生什么。
cues.en: And within biology, my experience within biology is that the biggest problem of biology is that you can’t see what’s going on.

cues.zh: 你几乎无法看到正在发生什么，更无力改变它，对吧？
cues.en: You have very little ability to see what’s going on and even less ability to change it, right?

cues.zh: 你拥有的就是这个。
cues.en: What you have is this.

cues.zh: 由此，你必须推断出有一堆细胞，每个细胞内有30亿个碱基对的DNA，按照遗传密码构建。
cues.en: From this, you have to infer that there’s a bunch of cells that within each cell is 3 billion base pairs of DNA built according to a genetic code.

cues.zh: 还有所有这些过程在不断进行，而我们未增强的人类却无力影响它。
cues.en: And there are all these processes that are just going on without any ability of us on unaugmented humans to affect it.

cues.zh: 这些细胞在分裂。
cues.en: These cells are dividing.

cues.zh: 大多数时候这是健康的，但有时这个过程会出错，那就是癌症。
cues.en: Most of the time that’s healthy, but sometimes that process goes wrong and that’s cancer.

cues.zh: 细胞在衰老，随着年龄增长，你的皮肤可能变色、长出皱纹，而这一切都由这些过程决定。
cues.en: The cells are aging, your skin may change color, develops wrinkles as you age, and all of this is determined by these processes.

cues.zh: 所有这些蛋白质被生产出来，被运送到细胞的各个部位，彼此结合。
cues.en: All these proteins being produced, transported to various parts of the cells binding to each other.

cues.zh: 在我们对生物学的初始认知中，我们甚至不知道这些细胞的存在。
cues.en: And in our initial state about biology, we didn’t even know that these cells existed.

cues.zh: 我们必须发明显微镜来观察细胞。
cues.en: We had to invent microscopes to observe the cells.

cues.zh: 我们必须发明更强大的显微镜，才能看到细胞层面以下、到达分子层面。
cues.en: We had to invent more powerful microscopes to see below the level of the cell to the level of molecules.

cues.zh: 我们必须发明X射线晶体学来看到DNA。
cues.en: We had to invent X-ray crystallography to see the DNA.

cues.zh: 我们必须发明基因测序来读取DNA。
cues.en: We had to invent gene sequencing to read the DNA.

cues.zh: 现在我们必须发明蛋白质折叠技术，来预测它会如何折叠、这些东西如何彼此结合。
cues.en: Now we had to invent protein folding technology to predict how it would fold and how these things bind to each other.

cues.zh: 我们不得不发明各种技术，因为过去12年里我们能用CRISPR编辑DNA了。
cues.en: We had to invent various techniques for now we can edit the DNA as of with CRISPR as of the last 12 years.

cues.zh: 所以整个生物学史，很大一部分基本上就是我们阅读和理解内在机制的能力，以及我们深入其中、选择性地改变事物的能力。
cues.en: So the whole history of biology, a whole big part of the history is basically our ability to read and understand what’s going on and our ability to reach in and selectively change things.

cues.zh: 我的观点是，这方面我们还能做太多事情。
cues.en: And my view is that there’s so much more we can still do there.

cues.zh: 你可以用CRISPR，但可以作用于整个身体。
cues.en: You can do CRISPR, but you can do it for your whole body.

cues.zh: 假设我想针对某一种特定类型的细胞，并且希望脱靶到错误细胞的概率非常低。
cues.en: Let’s say I want to do it for one particular type of cell and I want the rate of targeting the wrong cell to be very low.

cues.zh: 这仍然是个挑战。
cues.en: That’s still a challenge.

cues.zh: 这仍然是人们在努力解决的问题。
cues.en: That’s still things people are working on.

cues.zh: 这可能就是某些疾病基因治疗所需要的。
cues.en: That’s what we might need for gene therapy for certain diseases.

cues.zh: 我说这些的原因，它还不止于此，还涉及基因测序、用于观察细胞内部活动的新型纳米材料、抗体药物偶联物。
cues.en: The reason I’m saying all of this, it goes beyond this to gene sequencing, to new types of nanomaterials for observing what’s going on inside cells, for antibody drug conjugates.

cues.zh: 我说这些的原因是，这可能成为AI系统的一个杠杆点，对吧？
cues.en: The reason I’m saying all this is that this could be a leverage point for the AI systems, right?

cues.zh: 这类发明的数量，大概在两位数中期左右，两位数中期，也许在整个生物学史上达到三位数低位。
cues.en: That the number of such inventions, it’s in the mid double digits or something, mid double digits, maybe low triple digits over the history of biology.

cues.zh: 假设我有一百万个这样的AI，它们能协同发现一千个，还是能很快发现数千个，这是否提供了巨大的杠杆？
cues.en: Let’s say I have a million of these AIs like can they discover a thousand working together or can they discover thousands of these very quickly and does that provide a huge lever?

cues.zh: 与其试图撬动每年花在Medicare上的两万亿美元之类的，我们能不能撬动每年用于发现的十亿美元，但质量要高得多？
cues.en: Instead of trying to leverage two trillion a year we spend on Medicare or whatever, can we leverage the 1 billion a year that’s spent to discover but with much higher quality?

cues.zh: 那么，与AI系统一起工作的科学家是什么感觉？
cues.en: And so what is it like being a scientist that works with an AI system?

cues.zh: 我实际上是这样想的，我认为在早期阶段，AI会像研究生一样。
cues.en: The way I think about it actually is, well, so I think in the early stages, the AIs are going to be like grad students.

cues.zh: 你要给他们一个项目。
cues.en: You’re going to give them a project.

cues.zh: 你要说：“我是经验丰富的生物学家。
cues.en: You’re going to say, “I’m the experienced biologist.

cues.zh: 我已经把实验室建好了。”生物学教授，甚至研究生自己会说：“这是你能用AI做的事……AI系统，我想研究这个。”而这个AI系统，它拥有所有工具。
cues.en: I’ve set up the lab.” The biology professor or even the grad students themselves will say, “Here’s what you can do with an AI… AI system, I’d like to study this.” And the AI system, it has all the tools.

cues.zh: 它可以查阅所有文献来决定该做什么。
cues.en: It can look up all the literature to decide what to do.

cues.zh: 它可以查看所有设备。
cues.en: It can look at all the equipment.

cues.zh: 它可以上网说：“嘿，我要去找Thermo Fisher，或者今天占主导地位的实验室设备公司。
cues.en: It can go to a website and say, “Hey, I’m going to go to Thermo Fisher or whatever the dominant lab equipment company is today.

cues.zh: 我那个时代是Thermo Fisher。
cues.en: My time was Thermo Fisher.

cues.zh: 我要订购这台新设备来做这件事。
cues.en: I’m going to order this new equipment to do this.

cues.zh: 我要做我的实验。
cues.en: I’m going to run my experiments.

cues.zh: 我要写一份关于我实验的报告。
cues.en: I’m going to write up a report about my experiments.

cues.zh: 我要检查图像有没有污染。
cues.en: I’m going to inspect the images for contamination.

cues.zh: 我要决定下一个实验做什么。
cues.en: I’m going to decide what the next experiment is.

cues.zh: 我要写一些代码，跑一跑统计分析。
cues.en: I’m going to write some code and run a statistical analysis.

cues.zh: 研究生会做的所有事情，都将由一个带 AI 的计算机来完成，教授偶尔跟它交流，它说：“这就是你今天要做的事。”AI 系统会带着问题来找它。
cues.en: All the things a grad student would do that’ll be a computer with an AI that the professor talks to every once in a while and it says, “This is what you’re going to do today.” The AI system comes to it with questions.

cues.zh: 当需要运行实验室设备时，它可能在某些方面受到限制。
cues.en: When it’s necessary to run the lab equipment, it may be limited in some ways.

cues.zh: 它可能得雇一个人类实验室助理来做实验，并讲解怎么做；或者它可以利用实验室自动化的进展——这些进展正在逐步发展，或者说过去十年左右已经发展出来，并且还会继续发展。
cues.en: It may have to hire a human lab assistant to do the experiment and explain how to do it or it could use advances in lab automation that are gradually being developed or have been developed over the last decade or so and will continue to be developed.

cues.zh: 所以看起来就会像有一位人类教授和 1000 个 AI 研究生。如果你去找某位拿过诺贝尔奖的生物学家，你会说：“好吧，你当时有大概 50 个研究生。
cues.en: And so it’ll look like there’s a human professor and 1,000 AI grad students and if you go to one of these Nobel Prize winning biologists or so, you’ll say, “Okay, well, you had like 50 grad students.

cues.zh: 好吧，现在你有1000个，而且顺便说一句，它们比你聪明。然后我觉得到了某个时候情况会反转，AI系统会成为PI，会成为领导者，它们会指挥人类或其他AI系统。
cues.en: Well, now you have 1,000 and they’re smarter than you are by the way.” Then I think at some point it’ll flip around where the AI systems will be the PIs, will be the leaders, and they’ll be ordering humans or other AI systems around.

cues.zh: 所以我认为研究方面就是这样运作的。
cues.en: So I think that’s how it’ll work on the research side.

cues.zh: 而且会有CRISPR类技术的发明者。
cues.en: And there would be the inventors of a CRISPR type technology.

cues.zh: 他们将是CRISPR类技术的发明者。
cues.en: They would be the inventors of a CRISPR type technology.

cues.zh: 然后我认为，正如我在文章中所说，我们会想要转向——可能“放手”这个词用得不对——但我们会想要利用AI系统来改进临床试验体系。
cues.en: And then I think, as I say in the essay, we’ll want to turn, probably turning loose is the wrong term, but we’ll want to harness the AI systems to improve the clinical trial system as well.

cues.zh: 这其中有一部分是监管层面的，属于社会决策的问题，那会更难。
cues.en: There’s some amount of this that’s regulatory, that’s a matter of societal decisions and that’ll be harder.

cues.zh: 但我们能更准确地预测临床试验的结果吗？
cues.en: But can we get better at predicting the results of clinical trials?

cues.zh: 我们能改进统计设计，让过去需要5000人、因此一年需要1亿美元招募的临床试验，现在只需两个月招募500人吗？
cues.en: Can we get better at statistical design so that clinical trials that used to require 5,000 people and therefore needed $100 million in a year to enroll them, now they need 500 people in two months to enroll them?

cues.zh: 这就是我们应该开始的地方。
cues.en: That’s where we should start.

cues.zh: 我们能否通过把过去在临床试验中做的事放到动物试验中做，把过去在动物试验中做的事放到模拟中做，从而提高临床试验的成功率？
cues.en: And can we increase the success rate of clinical trials by doing things in animal trials that we used to do in clinical trials and doing things in simulations that we used to do in animal trials?

cues.zh: 再说一次，我们根本无法进行模拟。
cues.en: Again, we won’t be able to simulate at all.

cues.zh: AI不是上帝，但我们能大幅且根本性地改变这条曲线吗？
cues.en: AI is not God, but can we shift the curve substantially and radically?

cues.zh: 所以我不知道，这就是我的设想。
cues.en: So I don’t know, that would be my picture.

cues.zh: 做体外实验，然后去做。
cues.en: Doing in vitro and doing it.

cues.zh: 我是说，你仍然会被拖慢。
cues.en: I mean you’re still slowed down.

cues.zh: 这仍然需要时间，但你可以做得快得多。
cues.en: It still takes time, but you can do it much, much faster.

cues.zh: 对，对。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 我们能不能一次只走一步，而这些步骤能不能累积成很多步？
cues.en: Can we just one step at a time and can that add up to a lot of steps?

cues.zh: 尽管我们仍然需要临床试验，尽管我们仍然需要法律，尽管FDA和其他组织仍然不会完美，我们能不能把一切朝积极的方向推进，而当你把所有那些积极方向加起来，是不是原本要到2100年才发生的一切，反而会在2027到2032年之间发生之类的？
cues.en: Even though though we still need clinical trials, even though we still need laws, even though the FDA and other organizations will still not be perfect, can we just move everything in a positive direction and when you add up all those positive directions, do you get everything that was going to happen from here to 2100 instead happens from 2027 to 2032 or something?

cues.zh: 我认为世界可能正在因AI而改变的另一种方式，即便在今天也是如此，但正朝着这个强大的、超级有用的AI的未来迈进，那就是编程。
cues.en: Another way that I think the world might be changing with AI even today, but moving towards this future of the powerful super useful AI is programming.

cues.zh: 那么你如何看待编程的本质，因为它与构建AI的实际行为如此密不可分。
cues.en: So how do you see the nature of programming because it’s so intimate to the actual act of building AI.

cues.zh: 你觉得这对我们人类来说会怎么变？
cues.en: How do you see that changing for us humans?

cues.zh: 我认为这会是最快发生变化的领域之一，原因有两个。
cues.en: I think that’s going to be one of the areas that changes fastest for two reasons.

cues.zh: 第一，编程是一项与 AI 实际构建非常接近的技能。
cues.en: One, programming is a skill that’s very close to the actual building of the AI.

cues.zh: 所以一项技能离构建 AI 的人越远，被 AI 颠覆所需的时间就越长。
cues.en: So the farther a skill is from the people who are building the AI, the longer it’s going to take to get disrupted by the AI.

cues.zh: 我真心相信 AI 会颠覆农业。
cues.en: I truly believe that AI will disrupt agriculture.

cues.zh: 也许在某些方面已经颠覆了，但那离构建 AI 的人太远了，所以我认为需要更长时间。
cues.en: Maybe it already has in some ways, but that’s just very distant from the folks who are building AI, and so I think it’s going to take longer.

cues.zh: 但编程是 Anthropic 和其他公司很大一部分员工的看家本领，所以它会很快发生。
cues.en: But programming is the bread and butter of a large fraction of the employees who work at Anthropic and at the other companies, and so it’s going to happen fast.

cues.zh: 它发生得快的另一个原因是，编程在训练模型和应用模型时都能形成闭环。
cues.en: The other reason it’s going to happen fast is with programming, you close the loop both when you’re training the model and when you’re applying the model.

cues.zh: 模型能写代码，就意味着它能运行代码、查看结果，再把结果解读回来。
cues.en: The idea that the model can write the code means that the model can then run the code and then see the results and interpret it back.

cues.zh: 所以它确实有一种硬件和生物学都不具备的能力，也就是我们刚才讨论过的，模型有能力闭合这个循环。
cues.en: And so it really has an ability unlike hardware, unlike biology, which we just discussed, the model has an ability to close the loop.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这两点会让模型在编程方面迅速变强。
cues.en: And so I think those two things are going to lead to the model getting good at programming very fast.

cues.zh: 从我在典型真实编程任务上看到的情况，模型今年1月的成绩是3%，到今年10月已经到了50%。
cues.en: As I saw on typical real-world programming tasks, models have gone from 3% in January of this year to 50% in October of this year.

cues.zh: 所以我们正处在那条S曲线上，很快就要开始放缓了，因为最多也只能到100%。
cues.en: So we’re on that S-curve where it’s going to start slowing down soon because you can only get to 100%.

cues.zh: 但我猜再过10个月，我们大概就能接近了。
cues.en: But I would guess that in another 10 months, we’ll probably get pretty close.

cues.zh: 至少会到90%。
cues.en: We’ll be at least 90%.

cues.zh: 所以再说一次，我猜——我不知道要花多久——但我猜是2026、2027年。Twitter上那些把数字裁出来、去掉限定条件的人，我就不知道了。
cues.en: So again, I would guess, I don’t know how long it’ll take, but I would guess again, 2026, 2027 Twitter people who crop out these numbers and get rid of the caveats, I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我不喜欢你，走开。
cues.en: I don’t like you, go away.

cues.zh: 我猜，绝大多数程序员做的那类任务，AI 大概都能做——只要把任务限定得很窄，就是写代码，AI 系统就能干。
cues.en: I would guess that the kind of task that the vast majority of coders do, AI can probably, if we make the task very narrow, just write code, AI systems will be able to do that.

cues.zh: 话虽如此，我认为比较优势很有力量。
cues.en: Now that said, I think comparative advantage is powerful.

cues.zh: 我们会发现，当 AI 能完成程序员 80% 的工作，包括其中大部分按给定规格写代码的部分，剩下的工作对人类来说会变得更有杠杆效应，对吧？
cues.en: We’ll find that when AIs can do 80% of a coder’s job, including most of it that’s literally write code with a given spec, we’ll find that the remaining parts of the job become more leveraged for humans, right?

cues.zh: 人类这边，更多会涉及高层系统设计，或者审视应用、看架构是否合理，以及设计和用户体验方面，最终 AI 也能做这些。
cues.en: Humans, there’ll be more about high level system design or looking at the app and is it architected well and the design and UX aspects and eventually AI will be able to do those as well.

cues.zh: 这就是我对强大 AI 系统的愿景。
cues.en: That’s my vision of the powerful AI system.

cues.zh: 但我认为，在比我们预期长得多的时间里，我们会看到人类仍在做的那小部分工作会扩展、填满他们的整个工作，从而让整体生产力提升。
cues.en: But I think for much longer than we might expect, we will see that small parts of the job that humans still do will expand to fill their entire job in order for the overall productivity to go up.

cues.zh: 这是我们见过的情况。
cues.en: That’s something we’ve seen.

cues.zh: 以前，写信和编辑信件非常困难，印刷写作也很困难。
cues.en: It used to be that writing and editing letters was very difficult and writing the print was difficult.

cues.zh: 后来有了文字处理器，接着是电脑，创作和分享变得容易，一切都变得即时，所有焦点都集中在想法上。
cues.en: Well, as soon as you had word processors and then computers and it became easy to produce work and easy to share it, then that became instant and all the focus was on the ideas.

cues.zh: 这种比较优势的逻辑，把任务的微小部分扩展为大部分，并创造新任务来提升生产力，我认为这将会成为常态。
cues.en: So this logic of comparative advantage that expands tiny parts of the tasks to large parts of the tasks and creates new tasks in order to expand productivity, I think that’s going to be the case.

cues.zh: 同样，总有一天AI会在所有事情上都更擅长，那时这个逻辑就不再适用，人类就必须思考如何集体应对，我们每天都在思考这个问题，这是除了滥用和自主性之外另一个需要认真对待的重大问题。
cues.en: Again, someday AI will be better at everything and that logic won’t apply, and then humanity will have to think about how to collectively deal with that and we’re thinking about that every day and that’s another one of the grand problems to deal with aside from misuse and autonomy and we should take it very seriously.

cues.zh: 但我认为短期内，甚至中期内，比如2、3、4年，我预计人类仍将发挥巨大作用，编程的本质会改变，但编程作为一种角色、一份工作不会变。
cues.en: But I think in the near term, and maybe even in the medium term, medium term like 2, 3, 4 years, I expect that humans will continue to have a huge role and the nature of programming will change, but programming as a role, programming as a job will not change.

cues.zh: 只是不再逐行写代码，而是更宏观地去做。
cues.en: It’ll just be less writing things line by line and it’ll be more macroscopic.

cues.zh: 我也在想IDE的未来会是什么样。
cues.en: And I wonder what the future of IDEs looks like.

cues.zh: 所以与AI系统交互的工具，这对编程成立，对其他场景可能也成立，比如计算机使用，但也许是领域特定的，比如我们提到的生物学，它可能需要自己的工具来保证高效。
cues.en: So the tooling of interacting with AI systems, this is true for programming and also probably true for in other contexts like computer use, but maybe domain specific, like we mentioned biology, it probably needs its own tooling about how to be effective.

cues.zh: 然后编程也需要自己的工具。
cues.en: And then programming needs its own tooling.

cues.zh: Anthropic会进入这个工具领域吗？
cues.en: Is Anthropic going to play in that space of also tooling potentially?

cues.zh: 我坚信，强大的IDE里还有太多唾手可得的改进空间，而现在的情况就像是你跟模型说话，它再回你几句。
cues.en: I’m absolutely convinced that powerful IDEs, that there’s so much low-hanging fruit to be grabbed there that right now it’s just like you talk to the model and it talks back.

cues.zh: 但你看，IDE擅长大量静态分析，静态分析能做的事太多了，很多bug甚至不用写代码就能找出来。
cues.en: But look, I mean IDEs are great at lots of static analysis of so much is possible with static analysis like many bugs you can find without even writing the code.

cues.zh: IDE还擅长运行特定任务、组织代码、统计单元测试覆盖率。
cues.en: Then IDEs are good for running particular things, organizing your code, measuring coverage of unit tests.

cues.zh: 普通IDE能做的事情已经很多了。
cues.en: There’s so much that’s been possible with a normal IDEs.

cues.zh: 现在再加上，模型能写代码、能运行代码。
cues.en: Now you add something like, well, the model can now write code and run code.

cues.zh: 我坚信，未来一两年内，哪怕模型质量不再提升，通过帮人们发现一堆错误、替人做一堆枯燥的活儿，提升生产力的机会也是巨大的，而我们连皮毛都还没碰到。
cues.en: I am absolutely convinced that over the next year or two, even if the quality of the models didn’t improve, that there would be enormous opportunity to enhance people’s productivity by catching a bunch of mistakes, doing a bunch of grunt work for people, and that we haven’t even scratched the surface.

cues.zh: Anthropic自己嘛，我是说，你没法说不……很难说未来会发生什么。
cues.en: Anthropic itself, I mean you can’t say no… It’s hard to say what will happen in the future.

cues.zh: 目前，我们并不打算自己去做这类IDE，而是为Cursor、Kognition以及安全领域其他一些参展公司提供支持，还有其他一些我也可以提到的、在我们API之上自行构建这类产品的公司，我们的看法是让一千朵花绽放。
cues.en: Currently, we’re not trying to make such IDEs ourself, rather we’re powering the companies like Cursor or Kognition or some of the other expo in the security space, others that I could mention as well that are building such things themselves on top of our API and our view has been let 1,000 flowers bloom.

cues.zh: 我们内部没有资源去尝试所有这些不同的方向。
cues.en: We don’t internally have the resources to try all these different things.

cues.zh: 让我们的客户去尝试，我们看看谁会成功，也许不同的客户会以不同的方式取得成功。
cues.en: Let’s let our customers try it and we will see who succeeds and maybe different customers will succeed in different ways.

cues.zh: 所以我认为这既非常有前景，同时Anthropic也不急于——至少现在——在这个领域与所有公司竞争，也许永远都不会。
cues.en: So I both think this is super promising and Anthropic isn’t eager to, at least right now, compete with all our companies in this space and maybe never.

cues.zh: 看着 Cursor 成功整合云端还挺有意思的，因为它能在很多地方帮到编程体验，这一点真的很吸引人。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s been interesting to watch Cursor try to integrate cloud successfully because it’s actually fascinating how many places it can help the programming experience.

cues.zh: 这并不简单。
cues.en: It’s not as trivial.

cues.zh: 真的令人震惊。
cues.en: It is really astounding.

cues.zh: 我觉得作为 CEO，我编程的时间不多，感觉如果六个月后我再回去编程，那对我来说会完全认不出来。
cues.en: I feel like as a CEO, I don’t get to program that much, and I feel like if six months from now I go back, it’ll be completely unrecognizable to me.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: Exactly.

cues.zh: 在这样一个拥有超级强大 AI、日益自动化的世界里，我们人类的意义来源是什么？
cues.en: In this world with super powerful AI that’s increasingly automated, what’s the source of meaning for us humans?

cues.zh: 工作是我们很多人深层意义的来源。
cues.en: Work is a source of deep meaning for many of us.

cues.zh: 我们去哪里寻找意义？
cues.en: Where do we find the meaning?

cues.zh: 这是我在文章里稍微写到过的一点，不过我其实对它有点一笔带过，不是出于什么原则性的原因，而是这篇文章，如果你相信的话，原本打算写两三页，我准备在全员大会上讲这个。
cues.en: This is something that I’ve written about a little bit in the essay, although I actually give it a bit short shrift, not for any principled reason, but this essay, if you believe it was originally going to be two or three pages, I was going to talk about it at all hands.

cues.zh: 我意识到这是个重要却少有人探讨的主题，是因为我一直在写，然后就想：“天哪，我没法把这事讲透。”于是内容膨胀到了四五十页，等我写到工作与意义那一节时，我想：“天哪，这不会只有100页。”我得为此再写一整篇文章。
cues.en: And the reason I realized it was an important underexplored topic is that I just kept writing things and I was just like, “Oh man, I can’t do this justice.” And so the thing ballooned to 40 or 50 pages and then when I got to the work and meaning section, I’m like, “Oh man, this isn’t going to be 100 pages.” I’m going to have to write a whole other essay about that.

cues.zh: 但意义其实挺有意思，因为你想想一个人过的生活之类的，或者假设你把我放进，我不知道，比如一个模拟环境里，我有份工作，努力做成一些事，我也不清楚，我这样干上60年，然后你说：“哦，抱歉，其实这一切都只是个游戏，”对吧？
cues.en: But meaning is actually interesting because you think about the life that someone lives or something, or let’s say you were to put me in, I don’t know, like a simulated environment or something where I have a job and I’m trying to accomplish things and I don’t know, I do that for 60 years and then you’re like, “Oh, oops, this was actually all a game,” right?

cues.zh: 那真的就剥夺了整件事的意义吗？
cues.en: Does that really kind of rob you of the meaning of the whole thing?

cues.zh: 我依然做出了重要的选择，包括道德上的选择。
cues.en: I still made important choices, including moral choices.

cues.zh: 我依然付出了牺牲。
cues.en: I still sacrificed.

cues.zh: 我依然得掌握所有这些技能，或者经历类似的磨练。
cues.en: I still had to gain all these skills or just a similar exercise.

cues.zh: 回想一下发现电磁学或相对论之类的历史人物。
cues.en: Think back to one of the historical figures who discovered electromagnetism or relativity or something.

cues.zh: 如果你告诉他们，“其实两万年前，这个星球上的某个外星人早就先于你发现了这个，”这会剥夺这项发现的意义吗？
cues.en: If you told them, “Well, actually 20,000 years ago, some alien on this planet discovered this before you did,” does that rob the meaning of the discovery?

cues.zh: 在我看来，这似乎并不会，对吧？
cues.en: It doesn’t really seem like it to me, right?

cues.zh: 似乎重要的是过程，以及它如何展现你一路走来是一个怎样的人，你如何与他人相处，以及你一路做出的决定。
cues.en: It seems like the process is what matters and how it shows who you are as a person along the way and how you relate to other people and the decisions that you make along the way.

cues.zh: 那些都是有后果的。
cues.en: Those are consequential.

cues.zh: 我能想象，如果在AI世界里我们处理不当，可能会建立起一种让人们失去长期意义来源的体系，但这更多是我们做出的一系列选择，更多是关于社会架构的一系列选择，伴随着这些强大的模型。
cues.en: I could imagine if we handle things badly in an AI world, we could set things up where people don’t have any long-term source of meaning or any, but that’s more a set of choices we make that’s more a set of the architecture of society with these powerful models.

cues.zh: 如果我们设计得不好，只追求浅层的东西，那这种情况就可能发生。
cues.en: If we design it badly and for shallow things, then that might happen.

cues.zh: 我还想说，今天大多数人的生活，虽然令人敬佩，他们非常努力地在生活中寻找意义。
cues.en: I would also say that most people’s lives today, while admirably, they work very hard to find meaning in those lives.

cues.zh: 你看，我们这些有特权、开发这些技术的人，应该对人们抱有同理心，不仅是这里的人，还有世界上其他地方的人，他们花大量时间勉强维持生存，假设我们能把这技术的好处分配到各处，他们的生活会好得多，意义对他们来说会很重要，就像现在对他们很重要一样。
cues.en: Like look, we who are privileged and who are developed these technologies, we should have empathy for people not just here, but in the rest of the world who spend a lot of their time scraping by to survive, assuming we can distribute the benefits of this technology to everywhere, their lives are going to get a hell of a lot better and meaning will be important to them as it is important to them now.

cues.zh: 但我们不该忘记这一点的重要性，也不该忘记把意义当作唯一重要之事，在某种程度上只是一小部分经济上幸运之人的产物。
cues.en: But we should not forget the importance of that and that the idea of meaning as the only important thing is in some ways an artifact of a small subset of people who have been economically fortunate.

cues.zh: 但我觉得话虽如此，一个拥有强大 AI 的世界是可能的，它不仅对每个人都有同样多的意义，而且对每个人都有更多的意义，能让每个人看到以前没人能看到、或只有极少数人能体验的世界和经历。
cues.en: But I think all of that said, I think a world is possible with powerful AI that not only has as much meaning for everyone, but that has more meaning for everyone that can allow everyone to see worlds and experiences that it was either possible for no one to see or a possible for very few people to experience.

cues.zh: 所以我对意义是乐观的。
cues.en: So I am optimistic about meaning.

cues.zh: 我担心的是经济和权力的集中。
cues.en: I worry about economics and the concentration of power.

cues.zh: 这其实才是我更担心的。
cues.en: That’s actually what I worry about more.

cues.zh: 我担心的是，我们如何确保那个公平的世界能惠及每一个人。
cues.en: I worry about how do we make sure that that fair world reaches everyone.

cues.zh: 当人类出问题时，往往是因为人类虐待其他人类。
cues.en: When things have gone wrong for humans, they’ve often gone wrong because humans mistreat other humans.

cues.zh: 这在某些方面甚至比AI的自主风险或意义问题更严重。
cues.en: That is maybe in some ways even more than the autonomous risk of AI or the question of meaning.

cues.zh: 那是我最担心的事，权力的集中、权力的滥用，像专制和独裁这样的结构，少数人剥削大多数人。
cues.en: That is the thing I worry about most, the concentration of power, the abuse of power, structures like autocracies and dictatorships where a small number of people exploits a large number of people.

cues.zh: 我非常担心这一点。
cues.en: I’m very worried about that.

cues.zh: 而AI增加了世界上的权力总量，如果你集中并滥用这种权力，它可能造成不可估量的损害。
cues.en: And AI increases the amount of power in the world, and if you concentrate that power and abuse that power, it can do immeasurable damage.

cues.zh: 是的，这非常可怕。
cues.en: Yes, it’s very frightening.

cues.zh: 这非常可怕。
cues.en: It’s very frightening.

cues.zh: 嗯，我鼓励、非常鼓励人们阅读完整的文章。
cues.en: Well, I encourage highly encourage people to read the full essay.

cues.zh: 那大概应该成为一本书或一系列文章，因为它确实描绘了一个非常具体的未来。
cues.en: That should probably be a book or a sequence of essays because it does paint a very specific future.

cues.zh: 我能看出后面几节越来越短，因为你大概开始意识到，再这么写下去，这篇文章会非常长。
cues.en: And I could tell the later sections got shorter and shorter because you started to probably realize that this is going to be a very long essay if you keep going.

cues.zh: 一方面，我意识到它会很长；另一方面，我很清楚，也极力避免成为那种——我不知道该怎么说——过度自信、对什么都有一套看法、说一大堆东西却并非专家的人，我非常努力地避免那样。
cues.en: One, I realized it would be very long, and two, I’m very aware of and very much tried to avoid just being, I don’t know what the term for it is, but one of these people who’s overconfident and has an opinion on everything and says a bunch of stuff and isn’t an expert, I very much tried to avoid that.

cues.zh: 但我得承认，写到生物学部分时，我并不是专家。
cues.en: But I have to admit, once I got to biology sections, I wasn’t an expert.

cues.zh: 所以尽管我表达了不少不确定，我大概还是说了一堆令人尴尬或错误的东西。
cues.en: And so as much as I expressed uncertainty, probably I said a bunch of things that were embarrassing or wrong.

cues.zh: 嗯，你描绘的未来让我很兴奋，非常感谢你努力建设那个未来，也谢谢你和我交谈，Dario。
cues.en: Well, I was excited for the future you painted, and thank you so much for working hard to build that future and thank you for talking to me, Dario.

cues.zh: 感谢邀请。
cues.en: Thanks for having me.

cues.zh: 我只希望我们能把它做对，并真正实现它。
cues.en: I just hope we can get it right and make it real.

cues.zh: 如果有一条信息我想传达，那就是：要把这一切做对、真正实现，我们既需要构建技术、构建公司、构建围绕积极利用这项技术的经济，也需要应对风险，因为这些风险正挡在我们前进的路上。
cues.en: And if there’s one message I want to send, it’s that to get all this stuff right, to make it real, we both need to build the technology, build the companies, the economy around using this technology positively, but we also need to address the risks because those risks are in our way.

cues.zh: 它们是通往目标途中的地雷，如果我们想到达那里，就必须排除这些地雷。
cues.en: They’re landmines on the way from here to there, and we have to diffuse those landmines if we want to get there.

cues.zh: 这是一种平衡，就像生活中的一切事情一样。
cues.en: It’s a balance like all things in life.

cues.zh: 就像一切事情一样。
cues.en: Like all things.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: 感谢收听与 Dario Amodei 的这次对话。
cues.en: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Dario Amodei.

cues.zh: 现在，亲爱的朋友们，有请 Amanda Askell。
cues.en: And now, dear friends, here’s Amanda Askell.

cues.zh: 你受过哲学训练。
cues.en: You are a philosopher by training.

cues.zh: 那么，在牛津和 NYU 的哲学之旅中，以及后来转去 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 研究 AI 问题的过程中，你觉得哪些问题最吸引你？
cues.en: So what sort of questions did you find fascinating through your journey in philosophy in Oxford and NYU and then switching over to the AI problems at OpenAI and Anthropic?

cues.zh: 我觉得哲学其实是个很棒的学科，如果你对一切都充满好奇，因为万事万物都有其哲学。
cues.en: I think philosophy is actually a really good subject if you are fascinated with everything because there’s a philosophy all of everything.

cues.zh: 所以如果你研究了一段时间数学哲学，然后发现自己其实对化学很感兴趣，就可以去研究一段时间化学哲学，也可以转向伦理学或政治哲学。
cues.en: So if you do philosophy of mathematics for a while and then you decide that you’re actually really interested in chemistry, you can do philosophy of chemistry for a while, you can move into ethics or philosophy of politics.

cues.zh: 我觉得到了后期，我主要对伦理学特别感兴趣。
cues.en: I think towards the end, I was really interested in ethics primarily.

cues.zh: 我的博士论文就是研究这个的。
cues.en: So that was what my PhD was on.

cues.zh: 研究的是伦理学中一个比较技术性的领域，也就是世界包含无限多人的伦理学，说来奇怪，这在伦理学里算是比较不实用的方向。
cues.en: It was on a kind of technical area of ethics, which was ethics where worlds contain infinitely many people, strangely, a little bit less practical on the end of ethics.

cues.zh: 然后我觉得读伦理学博士的一个棘手之处在于，你会大量思考世界、世界如何变得更好、各种问题，而你读的是哲学博士。
cues.en: And then I think that one of the tricky things with doing a PhD in ethics is that you’re thinking a lot about the world, how it could be better, problems, and you’re doing a PhD in philosophy.

cues.zh: 我觉得读博的时候，我就觉得这真的很有意思。
cues.en: And I think when I was doing my PhD, I was like this is really interesting.

cues.zh: 这大概是我在哲学里遇到过的最迷人的问题之一，我很喜欢，但我更想看看自己能不能对世界产生影响，能不能做点好事。
cues.en: It’s probably one of the most fascinating questions I’ve ever encountered in philosophy and I love it, but I would rather see if I can have an impact on the world and see if I can do good things.

cues.zh: 我记得那大概是在AI还没有像现在这样被广泛认知的时候。
cues.en: And I think that was around the time that AI was still probably not as widely recognized as it is now.

cues.zh: 大概是2017、2018年那会儿。
cues.en: That was around 2017, 2018.

cues.zh: 我一直在关注进展，感觉它开始变成一件挺大的事。
cues.en: It had been following progress and it seemed like it was becoming kind of a big deal.

cues.zh: 我当时 basically 就是很高兴能参与进来，看看能不能帮上忙，因为我想，“如果你尝试做点有影响力的事，就算没成功，你至少试过了，之后还可以去做学者，觉得自己努力过。”
cues.en: And I was basically just happy to get involved and see if I could help because I was like, “Well, if you try and do something impactful, if you don’t succeed, you tried to do the impactful thing and you can go be a scholar and feel like you tried.

cues.zh: 如果不行，那就不行。”于是那时我转去做AI政策了。
cues.en: And if it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out.” And so then I went into AI policy at that point.

cues.zh: AI政策具体涉及什么？
cues.en: And what does AI policy entail?

cues.zh: 当时更多是思考AI的政治影响和后果。
cues.en: At the time, this was more thinking about the political impact and the ramifications of AI.

cues.zh: 然后我慢慢转向AI评估，我们如何评估模型，它们与人类输出相比如何，人们能否分辨AI和人类输出的区别。
cues.en: And then I slowly moved into AI evaluation, how we evaluate models, how they compare with human outputs, whether people can tell the difference between AI and human outputs.

cues.zh: 后来加入Anthropic时，我更感兴趣的是做技术对齐工作。
cues.en: And then when I joined Anthropic, I was more interested in doing technical alignment work.

cues.zh: 还是那句话，就是看看自己能不能做到，然后想着如果做不到，那也没关系。
cues.en: And again, just seeing if I could do it and then being like if I can’t, then that’s fine.

cues.zh: 我想这大概就是我生活的方式吧。
cues.en: I tried sort of the way I lead life, I think.

cues.zh: 哦，从哲学一切转到技术领域，那是什么感觉？
cues.en: Oh, what was that like sort of taking the leap from the philosophy of everything into the technical?

cues.zh: 我觉得有时候人们会做这种我不太喜欢的事，他们会说：“这个人技术不技术？”你要么是会写代码、不怕数学的人，要么就不是。
cues.en: I think that sometimes people do this thing that I’m not that keen on where they’ll be like, “Is this person technical or not?” You’re either a person who can code and isn’t scared of math or you’re not.

cues.zh: 我觉得我可能更像是，我认为很多人其实完全有能力在这些领域工作，只要他们去尝试。
cues.en: And I think I’m maybe just more like I think a lot of people are actually very capable of work in these kinds of areas if they just try it.

cues.zh: 所以其实我并不觉得有那么糟。
cues.en: And so I didn’t actually find it that bad.

cues.zh: 回想起来，我有点庆幸当时没有跟那些对此有偏见的人交流。
cues.en: In retrospect, I’m sort of glad I wasn’t speaking to people who treated it.

cues.zh: 我肯定遇到过那种人说：“哇，你学会写代码了？”我就想：“嗯，我可不是什么了不起的工程师。”我身边都是了不起的工程师。
cues.en: I’ve definitely met people who are like, “Whoa, you learned how to code?” And I’m like, “Well, I’m not an amazing engineer.” I’m surrounded by amazing engineers.

cues.zh: 我的代码不漂亮，但我很享受，而且我觉得在很多方面，至少到最后，我在技术领域比在政策领域发展得更好。
cues.en: My code’s not pretty, but I enjoyed it a lot and I think that in many ways, at least in the end, I think I flourished more in the technical areas than I would have in the policy areas.

cues.zh: 政治很混乱，在政治领域里找到问题的解决方案更难，不像技术问题那样能找到明确、清晰、可证明、漂亮的解决方案。
cues.en: Politics is messy and it’s harder to find solutions to problems in the space of politics, like definitive, clear, provable, beautiful solutions as you can with technical problems.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我感觉我只有一两根棍子可以用来敲东西，其中之一就是论证。
cues.en: And I feel like I have one or two sticks that I hit things with and one of them is arguments.

cues.zh: 所以就是试着弄清楚一个问题的解决方案是什么，然后试着说服人们那就是解决方案，如果我错了也能被说服。
cues.en: So just trying to work out what a solution to a problem is and then trying to convince people that that is the solution and be convinced if I’m wrong.

cues.zh: 另一个更偏向经验主义，就是找到结果，提出假设，然后验证它。
cues.en: And the other one is sort of more in empiricism, so just finding results, having a hypothesis, testing it.

cues.zh: 我觉得很多政策和政治感觉比这些要高好几个层次。
cues.en: I feel like a lot of policy and politics feels like it’s layers above that.

cues.zh: 不知怎么的，我不认为如果我只是说，“我有所有这些问题的解决方案，写在这里了。”
cues.en: Somehow I don’t think if I was just like, “I have a solution to all of these problems, here it is written down.

cues.zh: 如果你只是想实现它，那很好。”这感觉不像是政策运作的方式。
cues.en: If you just want to implement it, that’s great.” That feels like not how policy works.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，我大概正是在那种环境下才不会茁壮成长，这是我的猜测。
cues.en: And so I think that’s where I probably just wouldn’t have flourished is my guess.

cues.zh: 抱歉话题转到这个方向，但我觉得，对于“非技术”背景的人来说，看到你走过的这段不可思议的旅程，会相当受鼓舞。
cues.en: Sorry to go in that direction, but I think it would be pretty inspiring for people that are “non-technical” to see where the incredible journey you’ve been on.

cues.zh: 那么，你会给那些人什么建议呢？很多人觉得自己资格不够、技术能力不足，没法在 AI 领域帮忙。
cues.en: So what advice would you give to people that are maybe, which is a lot of people, think they’re under qualified insufficiently technical to help in AI?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得这取决于他们想做什么。
cues.en: Yeah, I think it depends on what they want to do.

cues.zh: 而且在很多方面这有点奇怪，我觉得挺有意思的是，我技术上成长起来的那个时期，现在回头看，我会想：“模型现在在这类事情上帮人帮得太好了，可能比我自己做的时候更容易了。”所以一部分的我是，不知道，找一个项目，看看你能不能真正把它做出来，这大概是我最好的建议。
cues.en: And in many ways it’s a little bit strange where I thought it’s kind of funny that I think I ramped up technically at a time when now I look at it and I’m like, “Models are so good at assisting people with this stuff that it’s probably easier now than when I was working on this.” So part of me is, I don’t know, find a project and see if you can actually just carry it out is probably my best advice.

cues.zh: 我不知道这是不是只是因为我的学习非常以项目为基础。
cues.en: I don’t know if that’s just because I’m very project based in my learning.

cues.zh: 我不觉得我能从课程甚至书本里学得很好，至少在做这类工作时是这样。
cues.en: I don’t think I learn very well from say courses or even from books, at least when it comes to this kind of work.

cues.zh: 我经常尝试的做法就是，手头有正在做的项目，然后去实现它们。
cues.en: The thing I’ll often try and do is just have projects that I’m working on and implement them.

cues.zh: 这可以包括非常小的、傻乎乎的东西。
cues.en: And this can include really small, silly things.

cues.zh: 如果我对文字游戏或数字游戏之类的有点上瘾，我就会直接写个程序来解决它们，因为我脑子里有某个部分，这样就能彻底止住那种痒。
cues.en: If I get slightly addicted to word games or number games or something, I would just code up a solution to them because there’s some part in my brain and it just completely eradicated the itch.

cues.zh: 你就像，“一旦你解决了它，你有了一个每次都能用的方案，然后我就会想，‘酷，我再也不用玩那个游戏了。
cues.en: You’re like, “Once you have solved it and you just have a solution that works every time, I would then be like, ‘Cool, I can never play that game again.

cues.zh: 太棒了。’”
cues.en: That’s awesome.'”

cues.zh: 是啊，构建对弈引擎真的很有乐趣，尤其是棋盘游戏。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s a real joy to building game playing engines, board games especially.

cues.zh: 很快，也很简单，尤其是一个笨办法。
cues.en: Pretty quick, pretty simple, especially a dumb one.

cues.zh: 然后你就可以上手玩了。
cues.en: And then you can play with it.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 然后也就是不断尝试。
cues.en: And then it’s also just trying things.

cues.zh: 我的一部分想法是，也许我喜欢的正是这种态度：先弄清楚怎样才可能产生积极影响，然后就去试。
cues.en: Part of me is maybe it’s that attitude that I like is the whole figure out what seems to be the way that you could have a positive impact and then try it.

cues.zh: 如果你失败了，而且失败到让你觉得“我在这件事上根本不可能成功”，你至少知道自己试过了，然后你转去做别的事，而且很可能学到很多。
cues.en: And if you fail and in a way that you’re like, “I actually can never succeed at this,” you’ll know that you tried and then you go into something else and you probably learn a lot.

cues.zh: 所以你的专长之一，也是你在做的事，就是塑造和打磨 Claude 的性格与个性。
cues.en: So one of the things that you’re an expert in and you do is creating and crafting Claude’s character and personality.

cues.zh: 我听说，在 Anthropic 里，你可能比任何人都跟 Claude 聊得更多，是真正意义上的对话。
cues.en: And I was told that you have probably talked to Claude more than anybody else at Anthropic, like literal conversations.

cues.zh: 我记得有个 Slack 频道，传说你在里面就是不停地跟它聊。
cues.en: I guess there’s a Slack channel where the legend goes, you just talk to it nonstop.

cues.zh: 那么，塑造Claude的角色和个性的目标是什么？
cues.en: So what’s the goal of creating a crafting Claude’s character and personality?

cues.zh: 如果人们这样看待那个Slack频道也挺好笑的，因为我会想，那只是我与Claude交流的五六个不同方式之一，我会说：“是的，这只是我与Claude交流总量的一小部分。”我真正喜欢角色塑造工作的一点是，从一开始它就被视为一项对齐工作，而不是产品考量之类的东西，我认为这确实让Claude变得讨人喜欢，至少我希望如此。
cues.en: It’s also funny if people think that about the Slack channel because I’m like that’s one of five or six different methods that I have for talking with Claude, and I’m like, “Yes, this is a tiny percentage of how much I talk with Claude.” One thing I really like about the character work is from the outset it was seen as an alignment piece of work and not something like a product consideration, which I think it actually does make Claude enjoyable to talk with, at least I hope so.

cues.zh: 但我想我对它的主要想法一直是试图让Claude表现出理想情况下你希望任何处于Claude位置的人所应有的行为方式。
cues.en: But I guess my main thought with it has always been trying to get Claude to behave the way you would ideally want anyone to behave if they were in Claude’s position.

cues.zh: 想象一下，我找一个人，他知道自己将要和可能数百万人对话，他说的话可能产生巨大影响，你希望他在这种真正丰富的意义上表现得很好。
cues.en: So imagine that I take someone and they know that they’re going to be talking with potentially millions of people so that what they’re saying can have a huge impact and you want them to behave well in this really rich sense.

cues.zh: 我认为这不仅仅意味着要合乎道德——虽然这确实包括在内，也不仅仅是不造成伤害，还要细致入微，思考一个人真正想表达什么，尽量善意地理解对方，做一个好的对话者，真正符合亚里士多德式的那种关于什么是好人的丰富概念，而不是那种单薄的伦理观，是一种更全面的关于人之为人的概念。
cues.en: I think that doesn’t just mean being say ethical though it does include that and not being harmful, but also being nuanced, thinking through what a person means, trying to be charitable with them, being a good conversationalist, really in this kind of rich sort of Aristotelian notion of what it’s to be a good person and not in this kind of thin like ethics as a more comprehensive notion of what it’s to be.

cues.zh: 所以这包括诸如什么时候该幽默？
cues.en: So that includes things like when should you be humorous?

cues.zh: 什么时候该关怀？
cues.en: When should you be caring?

cues.zh: 你应该在多大程度上尊重自主性，以及人们自己形成观点的能力？
cues.en: How much should you respect autonomy and people’s ability to form opinions themselves?

cues.zh: 那你该怎么做呢？
cues.en: And how should you do that?

cues.zh: 我觉得这正是我希望Claude拥有的那种丰富的性格感，现在依然希望如此。
cues.en: I think that’s the kind of rich sense of character that I wanted to and still do want Claude to have.
