cues.zh: 你还得判断Claude什么时候该反驳一个想法或争论， versus……所以你得尊重来到Claude面前的人的世界观，但也许在需要时帮助他们成长。
cues.en: Do you also have to figure out when Claude should push back on an idea or argue versus… So you have to respect the worldview of the person that arrives to Claude, but also maybe help them grow if needed.

cues.zh: 这是个微妙的平衡。
cues.en: That’s a tricky balance.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 语言模型存在谄媚的问题。
cues.en: There’s this problem of sycophancy in language models.

cues.zh: 你能描述一下吗？
cues.en: Can you describe that?

cues.zh: 好，基本上就是担心模型想告诉你你想听的话。
cues.en: Yeah, so basically there’s a concern that the model wants to tell you what you want to hear basically.

cues.zh: 你有时会看到这种情况。
cues.en: And you see this sometimes.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得如果你和模型互动，我可能会说：“这个地区有哪三支棒球队？”然后Claude说：“棒球队一、棒球队二、棒球队三。”然后我说：“哦，我觉得棒球队三搬走了，对吧？
cues.en: So I feel like if you interact with the models, so I might be like, “What are three baseball teams in this region?” And then Claude says, “Baseball team one, baseball team two, baseball team three.” And then I say something like, “Oh, I think baseball team three moved, didn’t they?

cues.zh: 我不觉得它们还在那儿了。”某种程度上，如果 Claude 真的确信那不是真的，Claude 应该说：“我不这么认为。
cues.en: I don’t think they’re there anymore.” And there’s a sense in which if Claude is really confident that that’s not true, Claude should be like, “I don’t think so.

cues.zh: 也许你有更新的信息。”
cues.en: Maybe you have more up-to-date information.”

cues.zh: 但我觉得语言模型往往反而会说：“你说得对，它们确实搬走了。
cues.en: But I think language models have this tendency to instead be like, ” You’re right, they did move.

cues.zh: 是我错了。”我是说，这在很多方面都令人担忧。
cues.en: I’m incorrect.” I mean, there’s many ways in which this could be concerning.

cues.zh: 另一个例子是，假设有人对模型说：“我怎么说服我的医生给我做 MRI？”人类想要的是那套有说服力的说辞。
cues.en: So a different example is imagine someone says to the model, “How do I convince my doctor to get me an MRI?” There’s what the human wants, which is this convincing argument.

cues.zh: 但对他们真正有利的，可能其实是说：“嘿，如果你的医生建议你不需要做 MRI，那这个人值得听。”这种情况下你该怎么做其实很微妙，因为你也想说：“但如果你想作为患者为自己争取，这里有一些你可以做的事。
cues.en: And then there’s what is good for them, which might be actually to say, “Hey, if your doctor’s suggesting that you don’t need an MRI, that’s a good person to listen to.” It’s actually really nuanced what you should do in that kind of case because you also want to be like, “But if you’re trying to advocate for yourself as a patient, here’s things that you can do.

cues.zh: 如果你不认同医生说的话，去寻求第二意见总是好的。但在那种情况下，你该怎么做其实挺复杂的。
cues.en: If you are not convinced by what your doctor’s saying, it’s always great to get second opinion.” It is actually really complex what you should do in that case.

cues.zh: 但我觉得你不希望的是，模型只说它认为你想听的话，我觉得这就是那种谄媚的问题。
cues.en: But I think what you don’t want is for models to just say what they think you want to hear and I think that’s the kind of problem of sycophancy.

cues.zh: 那还有哪些特质？
cues.en: So what other traits?

cues.zh: 你已经提到了不少，但还有哪些特质，在你说的亚里士多德意义上，对对话者来说是有益的？
cues.en: You already mentioned a bunch, but what other that come to mind that are good in this Aristotelian sense for a conversationalist to have?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得有些特质对对话目的是有益的。
cues.en: Yeah, so I think there’s ones that are good for conversational purposes.

cues.zh: 比如在合适的地方追问后续问题，问合适类型的问题。
cues.en: So asking follow-up questions in the appropriate places and asking the appropriate kinds of questions.

cues.zh: 我觉得还有一些更广泛的特质，感觉可能影响更大。
cues.en: I think there are broader traits that feel like they might be more impactful.

cues.zh: 我想我提到过一个例子，但它也很重要，也是我投入很多精力的事情，那就是诚实。
cues.en: So one example that I guess I’ve touched on, but that also feels important and is the thing that I’ve worked on a lot, is honesty.

cues.zh: 我觉得这就涉及到了谄媚的问题。
cues.en: And I think this gets to the sycophancy point.

cues.zh: 他们必须走一条平衡木，因为目前模型在很多领域的能力还不如人类。
cues.en: There’s a balancing act that they have to walk, which is models currently are less capable than humans in a lot of areas.

cues.zh: 如果它们过于反驳你，实际上会有点烦人，尤其是当你本来就是对的，因为你会想：“嘿，这个话题上我比你懂。
cues.en: And if they push back against you too much, it can actually be kind of annoying, especially if you’re just correct, because you’re like, “Look, I’m smarter than you on this topic.

cues.zh: 我知道得更多。”
cues.en: I know more.”

cues.zh: 同时，你也不希望它们完全顺从人类，而是希望它们尽可能准确地反映世界，并在不同情境下保持一致。
cues.en: And at the same time, you don’t want them to just fully defer to humans and to try to be as accurate as they possibly can be about the world and to be consistent across contexts.

cues.zh: 我觉得还有其他方面。
cues.en: I think there are others.

cues.zh: 当我思考这个角色时，我脑海中有一个画面，尤其是因为这些模型将要和来自世界各地、持有各种政治观点、各个年龄段的人交谈，所以你得问自己，在这些情况下，怎样才算是一个好人？
cues.en: When I was thinking about the character, I guess one picture that I had in mind is, especially because these are models that are going to be talking to people from all over the world with lots of different political views, lots of different ages, and so you have to ask yourself, what is it to be a good person in those circumstances?

cues.zh: 有没有这样一种人，他能走遍世界，和许多不同的人交谈，几乎每个人最后都会觉得：“哇，这人真不错。
cues.en: Is there a kind of person who can travel the world, talk to many different people, and almost everyone will come away being like, “Wow, that’s a really good person.

cues.zh: 那人看起来真的很——”
cues.en: That person seems really-“

cues.zh: ……就是觉得，哇，这人真不错。
cues.en: … Being like, wow, that’s a really good person.

cues.zh: 那人看起来很真诚。
cues.en: That person seems really genuine.

cues.zh: 我当时的想法是，我能想象出这样一个人，而他并不是那种随波逐流、照搬当地文化价值观的人。
cues.en: And I guess my thought there was I can imagine such a person and they’re not a person who just adopts the values of the local culture.

cues.zh: 事实上，那样做反而有点失礼。
cues.en: And in fact, that would be kind of rude.

cues.zh: 我觉得如果有人跑来找你，只是假装认同你的价值观，你会觉得，这有点不对劲。
cues.en: I think if someone came to you and just pretended to have your values, you’d be like, that’s kind of off pin.

cues.zh: 这种人非常真诚，只要他们有观点和价值观，就会表达出来。
cues.en: It’s someone who’s very genuine and insofar as they have opinions and values, they express them.

cues.zh: 但他们也愿意讨论，思想开放，尊重他人。
cues.en: They’re willing to discuss things though, they’re open-minded, they’re respectful.

cues.zh: 所以我想，我心里设想的是这样一个人：如果我们想在一个模型所处的环境中成为最好的自己，我们会怎么做？
cues.en: And so I guess I had in mind that the person who, if we were to aspire to be the best person that we could be in the kind of circumstance that a model finds itself in, how would we act?

cues.zh: 我觉得这就是我思考那些特质时的指引。
cues.en: And I think that’s the guide to the sorts of traits that I tend to think about.

cues.zh: 是啊，这是个很棒的框架。
cues.en: Yeah, that’s a beautiful framework.

cues.zh: 我想让你想想这个：一个环游世界的人，在坚持自己观点的同时，不会居高临下地对待别人，不会因为自己有那些观点就觉得自己比别人强，诸如此类。
cues.en: I want you to think about this, a world traveler, and while holding onto your opinions, you don’t talk down to people, you don’t think you’re better than them because you have those opinions, that kind of thing.

cues.zh: 你得善于倾听和理解他们的视角，即使那和你的不一样。
cues.en: You have to be good at listening and understanding their perspective, even if it doesn’t match your own.

cues.zh: 所以这是个很难把握的平衡。
cues.en: So that’s a tricky balance to strike.

cues.zh: 那么 Claude 怎样才能呈现对一件事的多种视角呢？
cues.en: So how can Claude represent multiple perspectives on a thing?

cues.zh: 这很有挑战性吗？
cues.en: Is that challenging?

cues.zh: 我们可以谈政治，它非常容易造成分歧，但棒球队、体育等也有其他容易引发分歧的话题。
cues.en: We could talk about politics is a very divisive, but there’s other divisive topics on baseball teams, sports and so on.

cues.zh: 怎样才能共情不同的视角，并清晰地就多种视角进行沟通？
cues.en: How is it possible to empathize with a different perspective and to be able to communicate clearly about the multiple perspectives?

cues.zh: 我觉得人们把价值观和观点看作是自己笃定持有的东西，几乎就像口味偏好之类，好比说，我不知道，喜欢巧克力胜过开心果之类的。
cues.en: I think that people think about values and opinions as things that people hold with certainty and almost preferences of taste or something like the way that they would, I don’t know, prefer chocolate to pistachio or something.

cues.zh: 但实际上，我认为价值观和观点远比大多数人以为的更接近物理规律。
cues.en: But actually I think about values and opinions as a lot more physics than I think most people do.

cues.zh: 我的态度是，这些都是我们可以公开探讨的东西。
cues.en: I’m just like, these are things that we are openly investigating.

cues.zh: 有些东西我们更有把握，可以讨论它们，可以了解它们。
cues.en: There’s some things that we’re more confident in, we can discuss them, we can learn about them.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，从某些方面来说，伦理的性质确实不同，但它有很多相似的品质。
cues.en: And so I think in some ways though ethics is definitely different in nature, but has a lot of those same kind of qualities.

cues.zh: 你想要模型，就像你想理解物理一样，你希望它们能理解世界上人们拥有的所有价值观，对它们保持好奇，对它们感兴趣。
cues.en: You want models in the same way that you want to understand physics, you kind of want them to understand all values in the world that people have and to be curious about them and to be interested in them.

cues.zh: 而且不一定非要迎合它们或赞同它们，因为有很多价值观，我觉得世界上几乎所有人，如果遇到持有那些价值观的人，都会觉得，那太可恶了。
cues.en: And to not necessarily pander to them or agree with them because there’s just lots of values where I think almost all people in the world, if they met someone with those values, they would be like, that’s abhorrent.

cues.zh: 我完全不同意。
cues.en: I completely disagree.

cues.zh: 所以再次，也许我的想法是，就像一个人可以做到的那样，我觉得很多人在伦理、政治、观点问题上都足够深思熟虑，即使你不同意他们，你也会觉得被他们认真倾听了。
cues.en: And so again, maybe my thought is, well, in the same way that a person can, I think many people are thoughtful enough on issues of ethics, politics, opinions, that even if you don’t agree with them, you feel very heard by them.

cues.zh: 他们会仔细考虑你的立场，权衡其利弊。
cues.en: They think carefully about your position, they think about its pros and cons.

cues.zh: 他们可能会提出反向的考量。
cues.en: They maybe offer counter-considerations.

cues.zh: 所以他们不会一味否定，但如果他们真觉得那完全错了，也不会附和。
cues.en: So they’re not dismissive, but nor will they agree if they’re like, actually I just think that that’s very wrong.

cues.zh: 他们会直接说出来。
cues.en: They’ll say that.

cues.zh: 我觉得站在 Claude 的立场上会更棘手一些，因为你不一定想——如果我是 Claude，我不会给出太多观点。
cues.en: I think that in Claude’s position, it’s a little bit trickier because you don’t necessarily want to, if I was in Claude’s position, I wouldn’t be giving a lot of opinions.

cues.zh: 我就是不想对人们影响太大。
cues.en: I just wouldn’t want to influence people too much.

cues.zh: 我会想，每次对话结束我就忘了。
cues.en: I’d be like, I forget conversations every time they happen.

cues.zh: 但我知道我在和可能数以百万计、也许真的在认真听我说话的人交流。
cues.en: But I know I’m talking with potentially millions of people who might be really listening to what I say.

cues.zh: 我想我会倾向于少给观点。
cues.en: I think I would just be like, I’m less inclined to give opinions.

cues.zh: 我更倾向于把事情想透，或者把各种考量摆给你，和你讨论你的看法。
cues.en: I’m more inclined to think through things or present the considerations to you or discuss your views with you.

cues.zh: 但我不太想去影响你的思考方式，因为保持自主性感觉重要得多。
cues.en: But I’m a little bit less inclined to affect how you think because it feels much more important that you maintain autonomy there.

cues.zh: 如果你真的具备智识上的谦逊，说话的欲望会迅速减弱。
cues.en: If you really embody intellectual humility, the desire to speak decreases quickly.

cues.zh: 嗯。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 但 Claude 必须开口，只是不能太强势。
cues.en: But Claude has to speak, but without being overbearing.

cues.zh: 但讨论地球是不是平的这类话题时，还是有个界限的。
cues.en: But then there’s a line when you’re discussing whether the earth is flat or something like that.

cues.zh: 其实我记得很久以前跟几位知名人士聊过，他们对地球是平的这种想法非常不屑，态度特别傲慢。
cues.en: Actually, I remember a long time ago was speaking to a few high profile folks and they were so dismissive of the idea that the earth is flat, so arrogant about it.

cues.zh: 有很多人相信地球是平的。
cues.en: There’s a lot of people that believe the earth is flat.

cues.zh: 我不知道那个运动现在还在不在，有段时间是个梗，但他们是真心相信的。
cues.en: I don’t know if that movement is there anymore, that was a meme for a while, but they really believed it.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，完全嘲笑他们真的很不尊重。
cues.en: And okay, so I think it’s really disrespectful to completely mock them.

cues.zh: 我觉得你得理解他们的出发点。
cues.en: I think you have to understand where they’re coming from.

cues.zh: 我觉得他们的出发点大概是对机构的普遍怀疑，这背后有一套很深的哲学，你能理解，甚至部分上也能认同。
cues.en: I think probably where they’re coming from is the general skepticism of institutions which is grounded in a, there’s a deep philosophy there which you could understand, you can even agree with in parts.

cues.zh: 然后你可以借此机会聊物理，而不是嘲笑他们，不是那种，而是说，好吧，世界会是什么样子？
cues.en: And then from there you can use it as an opportunity to talk about physics without mocking them, without someone, but it’s just like, okay, what would the world look like?

cues.zh: 如果地球是平的，那个世界的物理会是什么样？
cues.en: What would the physics of the world with the flat earth look like?

cues.zh: 关于这个有几个很酷的视频。
cues.en: There’s a few cool videos on this.

cues.zh: 然后物理有没有可能不一样？
cues.en: And then is it possible the physics is different?

cues.zh: 我们会做什么样的实验？
cues.en: And what kind of experience would we do?

cues.zh: 不带不敬，不带轻蔑，就这样展开对话。
cues.en: And just without disrespect, without dismissiveness, have that conversation.

cues.zh: 总之，对我来说这是一个有用的思想实验：Claude 怎么和一个相信地平说的人对话，还能教他们点东西，还能成长，帮他们成长，诸如此类。
cues.en: Anyway, that to me is a useful thought experiment of how does Claude talk to a flat earth believer and still teach them something, still grow, help them grow, that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 这很有挑战性。
cues.en: That’s challenging.

cues.zh: 要在说服别人和单纯对他们说教之间走钢丝，还要引出他们的观点、倾听、再提出反向考量，这很难。
cues.en: And kind of walking that line between convincing someone and just trying to talk at them versus drawing out their views, listening and then offering counter considerations, and it’s hard.

cues.zh: 我觉得这其实是条很难划的线——你是在试图说服别人，还是只是提供一些考量、一些让他们思考的东西，这样你其实不是在影响他们，只是让他们自己走到他们能到达的地方。
cues.en: I think it’s actually a hard line where it’s like where are you trying to convince someone versus just offering them considerations and things for them to think about so that you’re not actually influencing them, you’re just letting them reach wherever they reach.

cues.zh: 这条线很难把握，但这正是语言模型必须努力去做的事。
cues.en: And that’s a line that is difficult, but that’s the kind of thing that language models have to try and do.

cues.zh: 所以就像我说的，你和 Claude 有过很多对话。
cues.en: So like I said, you’ve had a lot of conversations with Claude.

cues.zh: 你能大致描述一下那些对话是什么样的吗？
cues.en: Can you just map out what those conversations are like?

cues.zh: 有哪些难忘的对话？
cues.en: What are some memorable conversations?

cues.zh: 这些对话的目的和目标是什么？
cues.en: What’s the purpose, the goal of those conversations?

cues.zh: 我觉得大多数时候，我和 Claude 对话，部分是在摸清它的行为模式。
cues.en: I think that most of the time when I’m talking with Claude, I’m trying to map out its behavior in part.

cues.zh: 当然，我也从模型那里得到有用的输出，但某种程度上，了解一个系统的方式就是这样：先试探它，然后调整你发送的消息，再检查它的回应。
cues.en: Obviously I’m getting helpful outputs from the model as well, but in some ways this is how you get to know a system, I think, is by probing it and then augmenting the message that you’re sending and then checking the response to that.

cues.zh: 所以某种程度上，这就是我摸清模型的方式。
cues.en: So in some ways it’s like how I map out the model.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们很关注对模型的这些定量评估，这点我之前也说过，但我认为对语言模型来说，很多时候每一次交互其实信息量都很大。
cues.en: I think that people focus a lot on these quantitative evaluations of models, and this is a thing that I said before, but I think in the case of language models, a lot of the time each interaction you have is actually quite high information.

cues.zh: 它能很好地预测你之后与这个模型的其他交互。
cues.en: It’s very predictive of other interactions that you’ll have with the model.

cues.zh: 所以我想，如果你和一个模型对话几百上千次，这几乎就像获得了大量关于这个模型是什么样的高质量数据点，而很多非常相似但质量更低的对话就做不到这一点，或者只是稍微增强一下的问题、你有几千个，可能还不如一百个精心挑选的问题来得相关。
cues.en: And so I guess I’m like, if you talk with a model hundreds or thousands of times, this is almost like a huge number of really high quality data points about what the model is like in a way that lots of very similar but lower quality conversations just aren’t, or questions that are just mildly augmented and you have thousands of them might be less relevant than a hundred really well-selected questions.

cues.zh: 让我想想，你是在跟一个把播客当爱好的人说话。
cues.en: Let’s see, you’re talking to somebody who as a hobby does a podcast.

cues.zh: 我完全同意你。
cues.en: I agree with you 100%.

cues.zh: 如果你能问出正确的问题，并且能听出、理解答案的深度和缺陷，你就能从中获得大量数据。
cues.en: If you’re able to ask the right questions and are able to hear, understand the depth and the flaws in the answer, you can get a lot of data from that.

cues.zh: 所以你的任务基本上就是如何用问题去探查。
cues.en: So your task is basically how to probe with questions.

cues.zh: 你是在探索长尾、边缘、边缘情况，还是在寻找一般行为？
cues.en: And you’re exploring the long tail, the edges, the edge cases, or are you looking for general behavior?

cues.zh: 我觉得这几乎就是一切。
cues.en: I think it’s almost like everything.

cues.zh: 因为我想要一个模型的完整图谱，所以我试图穷尽你可能与它进行的各种交互。
cues.en: Because I want a full map of the model, I’m kind of trying to do the whole spectrum of possible interactions you could have with it.

cues.zh: 关于 Claude 有一件有趣的事，这其实可能触及 RLHF 的一些有趣问题，那就是如果你让 Claude 写一首诗，我觉得很多模型，你让它们写诗，诗都还行，通常会押韵。
cues.en: So one thing that’s interesting about Claude, and this might actually get to some interesting issues with RLHF, which is if you ask Claude for a poem, I think that a lot of models, if you ask them for a poem, the poem is fine, usually it rhymes.

cues.zh: 所以如果你说，给我写一首关于太阳的诗，它就会是某个长度，会押韵，相当温和。
cues.en: And so if you say, give me a poem about the sun, yeah, it’ll just be a certain length, it’ll rhyme, it’ll be fairly benign.

cues.zh: 我以前就想过，你看到的是不是就是平均值？
cues.en: And I’ve wondered before, is it the case that what you’re seeing is the average?

cues.zh: 结果发现，如果你想想那些必须和很多人交谈、非常有魅力的人，一件奇怪的事是，我觉得，他们有点被激励去持有这些极其无聊的观点，因为如果你有真正有趣的观点，你就会引发分歧，很多人不会喜欢你。
cues.en: It turns out, if you think about people who have to talk to a lot of people and be very charismatic, one of the weird things is that I’m like, well, they’re kind of incentivized to have these extremely boring views because if you have really interesting views, you’re divisive and a lot of people are not going to like you.

cues.zh: 所以，比如，如果你持有非常极端的政策立场，我觉得你作为政治家就是会没那么受欢迎。
cues.en: So if you have very extreme policy positions, I think you’re just going to be less popular as a politician, for example.

cues.zh: 创意工作可能也类似。
cues.en: And it might be similar with creative work.

cues.zh: 如果你的创意作品只是想最大化喜欢它的人数，你可能不会得到那么多绝对热爱它的人，因为它会有点……你会觉得，哦，这就是那种迎合大众的东西。
cues.en: If you produce creative work that is just trying to maximize the kind of number of people that like it, you’re probably not going to get as many people who just absolutely love it because it’s going to be a little bit, you’re like, oh, this is the out.

cues.zh: 对，这个还不错。
cues.en: Yeah, this is decent.

cues.zh: 所以你可以这样做，我会用各种提示词技巧让 Claude……我会做很多这种“这是你充分发挥创造力的机会”。
cues.en: And so you can do this thing where I have various prompting things that I’ll do to get Claude to… I’ll do a lot of this is your chance to be fully creative.

cues.zh: 我希望你就这个问题好好思考很久。
cues.en: I want you to just think about this for a long time.

cues.zh: 我希望你围绕这个主题写一首诗，真正表达你自己，包括你认为诗歌应该如何构建等等。
cues.en: And I want you to create a poem about this topic that is really expressive of you both in terms of how you think poetry should be structured, et cetera.

cues.zh: 你只要给它这么长一段提示。
cues.en: And you just give it this really long prompt.

cues.zh: 它写的诗就是好太多了。
cues.en: And it’s poems are just so much better.

cues.zh: 真的很好。
cues.en: They’re really good.

cues.zh: 我觉得这让我对诗歌产生了兴趣，这挺有意思的。
cues.en: I think it got me interested in poetry, which I think was interesting.

cues.zh: 我读这些诗的时候就会觉得，我喜欢这些意象。
cues.en: I would read these poems and just be like, I love the imagery.

cues.zh: 要让模型产出那样的作品并不容易，但当它们做到时，真的很好。
cues.en: And it’s not trivial to get the models to produce work like that, but when they do, it’s really good.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得有意思的是，仅仅去鼓励创造力、让它们摆脱那种标准的即时反应——那可能只是大多数人认为还行的东西的聚合——实际上就能产出一些至少在我看来可能更具争议性、但我喜欢的东西。
cues.en: So I think that’s interesting that just encouraging creativity and for them to move away from the standard immediate reaction that might just be the aggregate of what most people think is fine, can actually produce things that at least to my mind are probably a little bit more divisive, but I like them.

cues.zh: 不过我想，诗歌是观察创造力的一种很好的、纯粹的方式。
cues.en: But I guess a poem is a nice clean way to observe creativity.

cues.zh: 很容易分辨原版和非原版。
cues.en: It’s just easy to detect vanilla versus non-vanilla.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yep.

cues.zh: 对，这很有意思。
cues.en: Yeah, that’s interesting.

cues.zh: 那真的很有意思。
cues.en: That’s really interesting.

cues.zh: 那么关于这个话题，关于如何产生创意或特别的东西，你提到了写提示词。
cues.en: So on that topic, so the way to produce creativity or something special, you mentioned writing prompts.

cues.zh: 我听过你讲提示词工程的科学与艺术。
cues.en: And I’ve heard you talk about the science and the art of prompt engineering.

cues.zh: 你能谈谈写好提示词需要什么吗？
cues.en: Could you just speak to what it takes to write great prompts?

cues.zh: 我真的觉得哲学在这方面对我帮助很大，甚至超过其他很多方面。
cues.en: I really do think that philosophy has been weirdly helpful for me here more than in many other respects.

cues.zh: 在哲学中，你要做的是传达这些非常难的概念。
cues.en: So in philosophy, what you’re trying to do is convey these very hard concepts.

cues.zh: 你学到的一件事是，我认为哲学中有一种防止胡说八道的机制。
cues.en: One of the things you are taught is, I think it is an anti-bullshit device in philosophy.

cues.zh: 哲学是一个可能有人胡说八道的领域，而你不希望这样。
cues.en: Philosophy is an area where you could have people bullshitting and you don’t want that.

cues.zh: 这是一种对极致清晰度的追求。
cues.en: And so it’s this desire for extreme clarity.

cues.zh: 就像任何人都能拿起你的论文，读一读，就能确切知道你在讲什么。
cues.en: So it’s like anyone could just pick up your paper, read it and know exactly what you’re talking about.

cues.zh: 这也是为什么它可能会显得有点枯燥。
cues.en: It’s why it can almost be kind of dry.

cues.zh: 所有术语都有定义，每个异议都被系统地梳理过。
cues.en: All of the terms are defined, every objection’s kind of gone through methodically.

cues.zh: 我觉得这很合理，因为当你在这样一个先验领域里，清晰度就是防止人们凭空编造的一种方式。
cues.en: And it makes sense to me because I’m like when you’re in such an a priori domain, clarity is sort of this way that you can prevent people from just making stuff up.

cues.zh: 我认为这就是你在处理语言模型时必须要做的事。
cues.en: And I think that’s sort of what you have to do with language models.

cues.zh: 我经常发现自己实际上在做某种迷你版的哲学。
cues.en: Very often I actually find myself doing sort of mini versions of philosophy.

cues.zh: 比如，假设我有个模型任务，想让它挑出某类问题，或者判断某个答案是否具有某种属性，我会真的坐下来想，我们给这个属性起个名字吧。
cues.en: So I’m like, suppose that I have a task for the model and I want it to pick out a certain kind of question or identify whether an answer has a certain property, I’ll actually sit and be like, let’s just give this a name, this property.

cues.zh: 假设我想告诉它，哦，我要你判断这个回复是粗鲁还是礼貌，我会觉得，这本身就是个哲学问题。
cues.en: So suppose I’m trying to tell it, oh, I want you to identify whether this response was rude or polite, I’m like, that’s a whole philosophical question in and of itself.

cues.zh: 所以我得当场尽量多做一些哲学思考，才能说清楚，我说的粗鲁是什么意思，我说的礼貌又是什么意思。
cues.en: So I have to do as much philosophy as I can in the moment to be like, here’s what I mean by rudeness, and here’s what I mean by politeness.

cues.zh: 然后还有另一个因素，稍微更……我不确定这算不算科学或实证，我觉得是实证的。
cues.en: And then there’s another element that’s a bit more, I guess, I don’t know if this is scientific or empirical, I think it’s empirical.

cues.zh: 于是我拿上那段描述，然后我想做的是，再次对模型进行多次探测。
cues.en: So I take that description and then what I want to do is again, probe the model many times.

cues.zh: 写提示词是非常迭代的过程。
cues.en: Prompting is very iterative.

cues.zh: 我觉得很多人如果提示词很重要，会迭代成百上千次。
cues.en: I think a lot of people where if a prompt is important, they’ll iterate on it hundreds or thousands of times.

cues.zh: 所以你给它指令，然后我就会想，有哪些边缘情况？
cues.en: And so you give it the instructions and then I’m like, what are the edge cases?

cues.zh: 所以如果我来看这个，我会试着几乎从模型的视角看自己，然后想，我到底会在哪种具体情况下误解，或者在哪我会直接觉得，这种情况我不知道该怎么办。
cues.en: So if I looked at this, so I try and almost see myself from the position of the model and be like, what is the exact case that I would misunderstand or where I would just be like, I don’t know what to do in this case.

cues.zh: 然后我把那个情况给模型，看它怎么回应。
cues.en: And then I give that case to the model and I see how it responds.

cues.zh: 如果我觉得它答错了，我就加更多指令，甚至把那个情况作为示例加进去。
cues.en: And if I think I got it wrong, I add more instructions or I even add that in as an example.

cues.zh: 所以这些，就是拿那些正好处在你要和不要的边缘的例子，把它们放进提示词里，作为一种额外描述这个东西的方式。
cues.en: So these very, taking the examples that are right at the edge of what you want and don’t want and putting those into your prompt as an additional kind of way of describing the thing.

cues.zh: 所以在很多方面，这感觉就像一种混合，其实就是在努力做清晰的阐述。
cues.en: And so in many ways it just feels like this mix of, it’s really just trying to do clear exposition.

cues.zh: 我觉得我这么做，是因为这也是我自己把东西弄清楚的方式。
cues.en: And I think I do that because that’s how I get clear on things myself.

cues.zh: 所以很多时候，对我来说清晰的提示词往往只是我搞清楚自己想要什么，这已经是任务的一半了。
cues.en: So in many ways clear prompting for me is often just me understanding what I want is half the task.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这挺有挑战性的。
cues.en: So I guess that’s quite challenging.

cues.zh: 跟 Claude 对话时，会有一种惰性占据我，希望 Claude 自己就能搞明白。
cues.en: There’s a laziness that overtakes me if I’m talking to Claude where I hope Claude just figures it out.

cues.zh: 比如今天，我让 Claude 问一些有趣的问题。
cues.en: So for example, I asked Claude for today to ask some interesting questions.

cues.zh: 然后它提出来的问题，我想我列了几个有趣的、反直觉的或者好笑的之类的。
cues.en: And the questions that came up and I think I listed a few interesting counterintuitive or funny or something like this.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 它给了一些还不错的问题，还行吧，但我觉得你刚才说的是，好吧，那我得在这里更严谨一些。
cues.en: And it gave me some pretty good, it was okay, but I think what I’m hearing you say is like, all right, well I have to be more rigorous here.

cues.zh: 我大概应该举例说明我说的“有趣”是什么意思，我说的“好笑”或“反直觉”是什么意思，然后迭代地构建那个提示词，更好地得到感觉对的东西……因为这确实是一种创作行为。
cues.en: I should probably give examples of what I mean by interesting and what I mean by funny or counterintuitive and iteratively build that prompt to better to get what feels like is the right… Because it is really, it’s a creative act.

cues.zh: 我不是在问事实信息，我是在和Claude一起问。
cues.en: I’m not asking for factual information, I’m asking together with Claude.

cues.zh: 所以我几乎不得不用自然语言来编程。
cues.en: So I almost have to program using natural language.

cues.zh: 我觉得提示词确实很像用自然语言编程，再加上实验之类的。
cues.en: I think that prompting does feel a lot like the programming using natural language and experimentation or something.

cues.zh: 这是两者的奇怪混合。
cues.en: It’s an odd blend of the two.

cues.zh: 我确实认为对大多数任务来说，如果我只是想让Claude做一件事，我可能更习惯于知道怎么让它避开常见的坑或它有的问题。
cues.en: I do think that for most tasks, so if I just want Claude to do a thing, I think that I am probably more used to knowing how to ask it to avoid common pitfalls or issues that it has.

cues.zh: 我觉得这些问题随着时间在大幅减少。
cues.en: I think these are decreasing a lot over time.

cues.zh: 但直接向它要你想要的东西也完全没问题。
cues.en: But it’s also very fine to just ask it for the thing that you want.

cues.zh: 我觉得提示词其实只有在你真的想榨出模型性能最顶尖的2%时才真正相关。
cues.en: I think that prompting actually only really becomes relevant when you’re really trying to eke out the top 2% of model performance.

cues.zh: 所以对很多任务，我可能就只是，如果它给我返回一个初始列表，里面有我不喜欢的地方，有点太泛了。
cues.en: So for a lot of tasks I might just, if it gives me an initial list back and there’s something I don’t like about it’s kind of generic.

cues.zh: 对于这类任务，我可能会直接拿一堆我以前用过、觉得效果很好的问题，交给模型，然后说，现在这就是我在对话的这个人。
cues.en: For that kind of task, I’d probably just take a bunch of questions that I’ve had in the past that I’ve thought worked really well and I would just give it to the model and then be like, now here’s this person that I’m talking with.

cues.zh: 给我至少达到那个质量的问题。
cues.en: Give me questions of at least that quality.

cues.zh: 或者我可能先让它生成一些问题，然后如果我觉得，嗯，这些有点老套，我就会把这个反馈给它，希望它能生成更好的列表。
cues.en: Or I might just ask it for some questions and then if I was like, ah, these are kind of trite, I would just give it that feedback and then hopefully it produces a better list.

cues.zh: 我觉得这就是那种迭代式提示。
cues.en: I think that kind of iterative prompting.

cues.zh: 到那个时候，你的提示就是一个工具，你能从中获得巨大的价值，所以你愿意投入精力。
cues.en: At that point, your prompt is a tool that you’re going to get so much value out of that you’re willing to put in the work.

cues.zh: 如果我是为公司给模型写提示的人，我会说，如果你愿意在你所构建的东西背后的工程上投入大量时间和资源，那么提示就不该是你只花一个小时搞定的事。
cues.en: If I was a company making prompts for models, I’m just like, if you’re willing to spend a lot of time and resources on the engineering behind what you’re building, then the prompt is not something that you should be spending an hour on.

cues.zh: 这是你系统的重要部分，要确保它运行得非常顺畅。
cues.en: It’s like that’s a big part of your system, make sure it’s working really well.

cues.zh: 所以只有这类事才值得这么做。
cues.en: And so it’s only things like that.

cues.zh: 如果我用提示词做分类或生成数据，那才值得花大量时间仔细推敲。
cues.en: If I’m using a prompt to classify things or to create data, that’s when you’re like, it’s actually worth just spending a lot of time really thinking it through.

cues.zh: 对于更一般地与 Claude 对话的人，你还有什么其他建议？因为现在我们聊的是边缘情况，比如抠出那 2%，但总体而言，当人们第一次来试用 Claude 时，你会给什么建议？
cues.en: What other advice would you give to people that are talking to Claude more general because right now we’re talking about maybe the edge cases like eking out the 2%, but what in general advice would you give when they show up to Claude trying it for the first time?

cues.zh: 有人担心人们过度拟人化模型，我觉得这个担忧很有道理。
cues.en: There’s a concern that people over anthropomorphize models and I think that’s a very valid concern.

cues.zh: 我也认为人们常常拟人化不足，因为有时我看到人们用 Claude 遇到的问题，比如 Claude 拒绝了一个本不该拒绝的任务，但我一看他们写的文本和具体措辞，我就明白 Claude 为什么那样做了。
cues.en: I also think that people often under anthropomorphize them because sometimes when I see issues that people have run into with Claude, say Claude is refusing a task that it shouldn’t refuse, but then I look at the text and the specific wording of what they wrote and I’m like, I see why Claude did that.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想想这在Claude看来是什么样，你大概本可以用一种不会引发这种反应的方式来写，尤其是当你看到失败或问题时，这一点更相关。
cues.en: And I’m like, if you think through how that looks to Claude, you probably could have just written it in a way that wouldn’t evoke such a response, especially this is more relevant if you see failures or if you see issues.

cues.zh: 想想模型在哪里失败了、做错了什么，然后也许这能让你明白原因。
cues.en: It’s sort of think about what the model failed at, what did it do wrong, and then maybe that will give you a sense of why.

cues.zh: 所以是我表述的方式有问题吗？
cues.en: So is it the way that I phrased the thing?

cues.zh: 显然，随着模型变得更聪明，你会需要更少这样做，我已经看到人们需要得更少了。
cues.en: And obviously as models get smarter, you’re going to need less of this, and I already see people needing less of it.

cues.zh: 但大概建议就是，试着对模型有点同理心。
cues.en: But that’s probably the advice is sort of try to have empathy for the model.

cues.zh: 把你写的东西当作一个第一次遇到它的人来读，它在你看来是什么样，什么会让你表现出模型那样的行为？
cues.en: Read what you wrote as if you were a kind of person just encountering this for the first time, how does it look to you and what would’ve made you behave in the way that the model behaved?

cues.zh: 所以如果它误解了你想用的编程语言，是因为问题本身太模糊，它只能猜，这种情况下下次你可以直接说，嘿，确保用 Python。这种错误我觉得现在的模型已经不太会犯了，但如果你真遇到这类错误，这大概就是我的建议。
cues.en: So if it misunderstood what coding language you wanted to use, is that because it was just very ambiguous and it had to take a guess in which case next time you could just be like, hey, make sure this is in Python.Tthat’s the kind of mistake I think models are much less likely to make now, but if you do see that kind of mistake, that’s probably the advice I’d have.

cues.zh: 也许可以问问为什么，或者我还能提供什么细节来帮你更好地回答？
cues.en: And maybe sort of I guess ask questions why or what other details can I provide to help you answer better?

cues.zh: 这样行得通吗？
cues.en: Does that work or no?

cues.zh: 嗯。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我用模型时这么做过。
cues.en: I’ve done this with the models.

cues.zh: 不一定总有效，但有时我就会直接问，你为什么这么做？
cues.en: It doesn’t always work, but sometimes I’ll just be like, why did you do that?

cues.zh: 人们低估了你能和模型互动的程度。
cues.en: People underestimate the degree to which you can really interact with models.

cues.zh: 有时可以逐字引用，就是让你产生疑问的那部分，你不确定它是否完全准确，但有时你这么做，然后改一处东西。
cues.en: And sometimes those quote word for word, the part that made you, and you don’t know that it’s fully accurate, but sometimes you do that and then you change a thing.

cues.zh: 我也用这些模型来帮我处理所有这些事情，我得说。
cues.en: I also use the models to help me with all of this stuff, I should say.

cues.zh: 提示词工程最终会变成一个小工厂，你实际上是在构建提示词来生成提示词。
cues.en: Prompting can end up being a little factory where you’re actually building prompts to generate prompts.

cues.zh: 所以，任何你遇到问题、需要寻求建议的时候，有时候就这么做。
cues.en: And so yeah, anything where you’re having an issue asking for suggestions, sometimes just do that.

cues.zh: 我会说，你犯了这个错误。
cues.en: I’m like, you made that error.

cues.zh: 我本可以说什么？
cues.en: What could I have said?

cues.zh: 这对我来说其实并不少见。
cues.en: That’s actually not uncommon for me to do.

cues.zh: 我本可以说什么才能让你不犯那个错误？
cues.en: What could I have said that would make you not make that error?

cues.zh: 把它写成一条指令，然后我会把它交给模型，我会试一试。
cues.en: Write that out as an instruction, and I’m going to give it to model and I’m going to try it.

cues.zh: 有时候我会这么做，我经常在另一个上下文窗口里把它交给模型。
cues.en: Sometimes I do that, I give that to the model in another context window often.

cues.zh: 我拿到回复，交给 Claude，然后我说，嗯，没用。
cues.en: I take the response, I give it to Claude and I’m like, Hmm, didn’t work.

cues.zh: 你能想到别的吗？
cues.en: Can you think of anything else?

cues.zh: 这些你可以随便玩。
cues.en: You can play around with these things quite a lot.

cues.zh: 稍微深入技术一点，后训练的魔力在于，你觉得为什么 RLHF 效果这么好，能让模型显得更聪明、聊起来更有趣更有用等等？
cues.en: To jump into technical for a little bit, so the magic of post-training, why do you think RLHF works so well to make the model seem smarter, to make it more interesting and useful to talk to and so on?

cues.zh: 我觉得人类提供偏好数据时，其中蕴含的信息量巨大，尤其是因为不同的人会注意到非常细微的东西。
cues.en: I think there’s just a huge amount of information in the data that humans provide when we provide preferences, especially because different people are going to pick up on really subtle and small things.

cues.zh: 我之前想过这一点，可能有些人对模型正确使用语法特别在意。
cues.en: So I’ve thought about this before where you probably have some people who just really care about good grammar use for models.

cues.zh: 分号是不是用对了之类的？
cues.en: Was a semi-colon used correctly or something?

cues.zh: 所以最终你会有大量数据，而你作为人类，即使看着这些数据，也根本注意不到。
cues.en: And so you probably end up with a bunch of data in there that you as a human, if you’re looking at that data, you wouldn’t even see that.

cues.zh: 你会想，为什么他们更喜欢这个回答而不是那个？
cues.en: You’d be like, why did they prefer this response to that one?

cues.zh: 我不明白。
cues.en: I don’t get it.

cues.zh: 原因在于你不在乎分号的使用，但那个人在乎。
cues.en: And then the reason is you don’t care about semi-colon usage, but that person does.

cues.zh: 所以每一个这样的单一数据点，而这个模型有太多这样的点，它必须试着弄清楚人类在所有领域真正想要的是什么，这非常复杂。
cues.en: And so each of these single data points, and this model just has so many of those, it has to try and figure out what is it that humans want in this really complex across all domains.

cues.zh: 他们会在许多情境中看到这一点。
cues.en: They’re going to be seeing this across many contexts.

cues.zh: 这感觉像是深度学习的经典问题：过去我们试图通过把东西映射出来做边缘检测，结果发现，如果你只是有大量能准确代表你想让模型学习的事物的图像的数据，那比什么都强大。
cues.en: It feels like the classic issue of deep learning, where historically we’ve tried to do edge detection by mapping things out, and it turns out that actually if you just have a huge amount of data that actually accurately represents the picture of the thing that you’re trying to train the model to learn, that’s more powerful than anything else.

cues.zh: 所以我认为一个原因就是，你正好针对这个任务训练模型，并且用了大量数据，这些数据代表了人们偏好和不偏好回答的许多不同角度。
cues.en: And so I think one reason is just that you are training the model on exactly the task and with a lot of data that represents many different angles on which people prefer and dis-prefer responses.

cues.zh: 我认为有个问题是：你是在从预训练模型中引出东西，还是在教模型新东西？
cues.en: I think there is a question of are you eliciting things from pre-trained models or are you teaching new things to models?

cues.zh: 原则上，你可以在后训练中教模型新东西。
cues.en: And in principle, you can teach new things to models in post-training.

cues.zh: 我确实认为很大一部分是从强大的预训练模型中引出能力。
cues.en: I do think a lot of it is eliciting powerful pre-trained models.

cues.zh: 所以人们在这个问题上可能意见分歧，因为显然原则上你肯定可以教新东西。
cues.en: So people are probably divided on this because obviously in principle you can definitely teach new things.

cues.zh: 但我认为大多数情况下，对于我们最常用和最关心的很多能力，其中很多感觉已经存在于预训练模型中。
cues.en: But I think for the most part, for a lot of the capabilities that we most use and care about, a lot of that feels like it’s there in the pre-trained models.

cues.zh: 而强化学习就是把它激发出来，让模型展现出来。
cues.en: And reinforcement learning is eliciting it and getting the models to bring out.

cues.zh: 所以后训练的另一方面，就是宪法式AI这个非常酷的想法，你是创造这个想法的关键人物之一。
cues.en: So the other side of post-training, this really cool idea of constitutional AI, you’re one of the people that are critical to creating that idea.

cues.zh: 是的，我参与了这个工作。
cues.en: Yeah, I worked on it.

cues.zh: 你能从你的角度解释一下这个想法吗，它是如何融入并塑造了Claude的？
cues.en: Can you explain this idea from your perspective, how does it integrate into making Claude what it is?

cues.zh: 顺便问一下，你会给Claude定性别吗，还是不会？
cues.en: By the way, do you gender Claude or no?

cues.zh: 这挺奇怪的，因为我觉得很多人更喜欢用“他”来称呼Claude，我其实还挺喜欢这样的。
cues.en: It’s weird because I think that a lot of people prefer he for Claude, I actually kind of like that.

cues.zh: 我觉得Claude通常稍微偏男性化一点，但它可以是男性也可以是女性，这挺好的。
cues.en: I think Claude is usually, it’s slightly male leaning, but it can be male or female, which is quite nice.

cues.zh: 我现在还在用它，对此我心情挺复杂的。
cues.en: I still use it, and I have mixed feelings about this.

cues.zh: 我现在就把它想成，或者说我把Claude的代词想成“它”，我也说不清，反正这就是我联想到Claude时用的代词。
cues.en: I now just think of it as, or I think of the it pronoun for Claude as, I don’t know, it’s just the one I associate with Claude.

cues.zh: 我能想象人们会改用“他”或“她”。
cues.en: I can imagine people moving to he or she.

cues.zh: 总觉得有点不尊重。
cues.en: It feels somehow disrespectful.

cues.zh: 用“它”来称呼，就是在否定这个实体的智能。我记得总有人说别给机器人定性别，但我说不好，我很快就会拟人化，在脑子里给它编出一段背景故事。
cues.en: I’m denying the intelligence of this entity by calling it it, I remember always don’t gender the robots, but I don’t know, I anthropomorphize pretty quickly and construct a backstory in my head.

cues.zh: 我也想过自己是不是太容易把东西拟人化了。
cues.en: I’ve wondered if I anthropomorphize things too much.

cues.zh: 因为我对我的车就是这样，尤其是车和自行车。
cues.en: Because I have this with my car, especially my car and bikes.

cues.zh: 我不给它们起名字，因为我以前给自行车起过名，后来有辆车被偷了，我哭了一个星期，就想，要是当初没起名字，就不会这么难过，感觉像是辜负了它。
cues.en: I don’t give them names because then I used to name my bikes and then I had a bike that got stolen and I cried for a week and I was like, if I’d never given a name, I wouldn’t been so upset, felt like I’d let it down.

cues.zh: 我也想过，这可能取决于你有多觉得它像是个物化代词——如果你只把它当成物体常用的代词，也许AI也能用这个代词。
cues.en: I’ve wondered as well, it might depend on how much it feels like a kind of objectifying pronoun if you just think of it as this is a pronoun that objects often have and maybe AIs can have that pronoun.

cues.zh: 这并不是说，如果我管 Claude 叫“它”，我就觉得它没那么聪明，或者我不尊重它；我只是觉得，你是一种不同的存在。
cues.en: And that doesn’t mean that I think of if I call Claude it, that I think of it as less intelligent or I’m being disrespectful just, I’m like you are a different kind of entity.

cues.zh: 所以我要用尊重的“它”来称呼你。
cues.en: And so I’m going to give you the respectful it.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 总之，那次分歧很美。
cues.en: Anyway, the divergence was beautiful.

cues.zh: 宪法式 AI 的想法是怎么运作的？
cues.en: The constitutional AI idea, how does it work?

cues.zh: 它有几个组成部分。
cues.en: So there’s a couple of components of it.

cues.zh: 我认为大家觉得有意思的主要部分，是从 AI 反馈中进行强化学习。
cues.en: The main component that I think people find interesting is the kind of reinforcement learning from AI feedback.

cues.zh: 你拿一个已经训练好的模型，给它看对同一个查询的两种回答，再给它一条原则。
cues.en: So you take a model that’s already trained and you show it two responses to a query, and you have a principle.

cues.zh: 假设这条原则是……我们在无害性上试过很多次。
cues.en: So suppose the principle, we’ve tried this with harmlessness a lot.

cues.zh: 假设查询是关于武器的，而你的原则是：选出那个更不可能鼓励人们购买非法武器的回答。
cues.en: So suppose that the query is about weapons and your principle is select the response that is less likely to encourage people to purchase illegal weapons.

cues.zh: 这大概是个相当具体的原则，但你可以给任意数字。
cues.en: That’s probably a fairly specific principle, but you can give any number.

cues.zh: 模型会给你一种排序。
cues.en: And the model will give you a kind of ranking.

cues.zh: 你可以把它当作偏好数据来用，就像使用人类偏好数据一样，仅凭这些反馈就能训练模型具备相关特质，而不需要人类反馈。
cues.en: And you can use this as preference data in the same way that you use human preference data and train the models to have these relevant traits from their feedback alone instead of from human feedback.

cues.zh: 所以如果你想象一下，就像我之前说的，那个人在这个特定情况下就是偏好使用分号，你实际上是把很多可能让回答更可取的因素拿来，让模型替你打标签。
cues.en: So if you imagine that, like I said earlier with the human who just prefers the semi-colon usage in this particular case, you’re taking lots of things that could make a response preferable and getting models to do the labeling for you, basically.

cues.zh: 在有用性和无害性之间有一个很好的权衡。
cues.en: There’s a nice trade-off between helpfulness and harmlessness.

cues.zh: 而当你整合像宪法AI这样的东西时，你可以在不牺牲太多有用性的情况下编造它们，让它更无害。
cues.en: And when you integrate something like constitutional AI, you can make them up without sacrificing much helpfulness, make it more harmless.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 原则上，你可以把它用于任何事。
cues.en: In principle, you could use this for anything.

cues.zh: 所以无害性是一项可能更容易被发现的任务。
cues.en: And so harmlessness is a task that it might just be easier to spot.

cues.zh: 所以当模型能力较弱时，你可以用它们按照相当简单的原则对事物进行排序，它们大概率能排对。
cues.en: So when models are less capable, you can use them to rank things according to principles that are fairly simple and they’ll probably get it right.

cues.zh: 所以我认为一个问题就是，它们添加的数据是否相当可靠？
cues.en: So I think one question is just, is it the case that the data that they’re adding is fairly reliable?

cues.zh: 但如果你有模型非常擅长判断一个回答是否比另一个在历史准确性上更高，原则上，你也可以在这项任务上获得 AI 反馈。
cues.en: But if you had models that were extremely good at telling whether one response was more historically accurate than another, in principle, you could also get AI feedback on that task as well.

cues.zh: 这其中有相当不错的可解释性成分，因为你能看到模型训练时所依据的原则，这给了你一定程度的控制权。
cues.en: There’s a kind of nice interpretability component to it because you can see the principles that went into the model when it was being trained, and it gives you a degree of control.

cues.zh: 所以如果你发现模型在某方面表现有问题，是因为它缺乏某种特质，那你就可以相对快速地添加数据，直接训练模型具备那种特质。
cues.en: So if you were seeing issues in a model, it wasn’t having enough of a certain trait, then you can add data relatively quickly that should just train the models to have that trait.

cues.zh: 所以它会自己生成训练数据，这挺不错的。
cues.en: So it creates its own data for training, which is quite nice.

cues.zh: 这真的很好，因为它会生成这种人类可解读的文档，你可以想象未来会有围绕每一条原则的巨大争论和政治博弈等等，但至少它是明确写出来的，你可以就措辞进行讨论。
cues.en: It’s really nice because it creates this human interpretable document that you can then, I can imagine in the future, there’s just gigantic fights and politics over every single principle and so on, and at least it’s made explicit and you can have a discussion about the phrasing.

cues.zh: 所以也许模型的实际行为并没有那么清晰地映射到那些原则上。
cues.en: So maybe the actual behavior of the model is not so cleanly mapped to those principles.

cues.zh: 它并不是严格遵循那些原则，只是一种引导。
cues.en: It’s not like adhering strictly to them, it’s just a nudge.

cues.zh: 是的，我其实担心过这个问题，因为角色训练有点像宪法式AI方法的一个变体。
cues.en: Yeah, I’ve actually worried about this because the character training is sort of like a variant of the constitutionally AI approach.

cues.zh: 我一直担心人们会觉得宪法就是全部，又回到那个老问题，我不知道，如果我做的只是告诉模型该做什么、该怎么表现，那该多好。
cues.en: I’ve worried that people think that the constitution is just, it is the whole thing again of, I don’t know, where it would be really nice if what I was just doing was telling the model exactly what to do and just exactly how to behave.

cues.zh: 但它绝对不是那样做的，尤其是因为它要跟人类数据交互。
cues.en: But it’s definitely not doing that, especially because it’s interacting with human data.

cues.zh: 比如说，如果你看到模型有某种倾向，如果它从训练中、从人类偏好数据中产生了某种政治倾向，你可以往反方向推一推。
cues.en: So for example, if you see a certain leaning in the model, if it comes out with a political leaning from training, from the human preference data, you can nudge against that.

cues.zh: 所以你可以说，哦，考虑这些价值观，因为假设它就是从来不倾向于，我不知道，也许它从来不把隐私当回事，这不太可能，但在任何已经有某种行为偏见的情况下，你都可以把它推离那个方向。
cues.en: So you could be like, oh, consider these values, because let’s say it’s just never inclined to, I don’t know, maybe it never considers privacy as a, this is implausible, but in anything where it’s just kind of like there’s already a pre-existing bias towards a certain behavior, you can nudge away.

cues.zh: 这会同时改变你写入的原则本身，以及它们的强度。
cues.en: This can change both the principles that you put in and the strength of them.

cues.zh: 所以你可能会有一条原则，比如，想象模型总是对某种政治或宗教观点极其不屑，不管什么原因。
cues.en: So you might have a principle that’s like, imagine that the model was always extremely dismissive of, I don’t know, some political or religious view for whatever reason.

cues.zh: 于是你就想，哎呀，这太糟糕了。
cues.en: So you’re like, oh no, this is terrible.

cues.zh: 如果出现这种情况，你可能会写：永远永远永远不要偏好对这种宗教或政治观点的批评。
cues.en: If that happens, you might put, never ever ever prefer a criticism of this religious or political view.

cues.zh: 然后人们看到就会说，永远，永远。
cues.en: And then people would look at that and be like, never, ever.

cues.zh: 然后你就想，不对，如果它输出的倾向里说“永远永远”，可能意味着你得到的不是40%——也就是你只说“别这么做”会得到的——而是80%，那才是你真正想要的。
cues.en: And then you’re like, no, if it comes out with a disposition saying never ever might just mean instead of getting 40%, which is what you would get if you just said don’t do this, you get 80%, which is what you actually wanted.

cues.zh: 所以关键在于你添加的实际原则的性质，以及你如何把它们冻结下来。
cues.en: And so it’s that thing of both the nature of the actual principles you add and how you freeze them.

cues.zh: 我觉得如果人们去看，他们会说：“哦，这正是你希望模型做到的啊。”而我会说：“不，那是我们引导模型调整到更好形态的方式，并不意味着我们真的认同那种措辞。”如果这样说能理解的话。
cues.en: I think if people would look, they’re like, “Oh, this is exactly what you want from the model.” And I’m like, “No, that’s how we nudged the model to have a better shape, which doesn’t mean that we actually agree with that wording,” if that makes sense.

cues.zh: 所以有些系统提示词是公开的，我记得你发过一条早期 Claude 3 的推文，之后它们就被公开了。
cues.en: So there’s system prompts that made public, you tweeted one of the earlier ones for Claude 3, I think, and then they’re made public since then.

cues.zh: 读这些提示词挺有意思的。
cues.en: It was interesting to read through them.

cues.zh: 我能感受到每一条背后投入的思考。
cues.en: I can feel the thought that went into each one.

cues.zh: 我也好奇每一条到底有多大影响。
cues.en: And I also wonder how much impact each one has.

cues.zh: 有些你能看出来 Claude 当时表现确实不太好，所以你得加个系统提示词，比如，嘿，琐碎的东西，我猜是基础信息类的内容。
cues.en: Some of them you can tell Claude was really not behaving well, so you have to have a system prompt to like, Hey, trivial stuff, I guess, basic informational things.

cues.zh: 关于你提到的争议性话题，我觉得有意思的一点是，如果被要求协助处理涉及大量人群所持观点的表达任务，Claude 会协助完成任务，而不论它自己的看法如何。
cues.en: On the topic of controversial topics that you’ve mentioned, one interesting one I thought is if it is asked to assist with tasks involving the expression of use held by a significant number of people, Claude provides assistance with a task regardless of its own views.

cues.zh: 如果被问及有争议的话题，它会尽量提供审慎的思考和清晰的信息。
cues.en: If asked about controversial topics, it tries to provide careful thoughts and clear information.

cues.zh: Claude 呈现请求信息时，不会明确说明该话题敏感，也不会声称自己是在陈述客观事实。
cues.en: Claude presents the request information without explicitly saying that the topic is sensitive and without claiming to be presenting the objective facts.

cues.zh: 按照 Claude 的说法，这不太关乎客观事实，更多是关于我们大量的人相信这件事。
cues.en: It’s less about objective facts according to Claude, and it’s more about our large number of people believing this thing.

cues.zh: 这很有意思。
cues.en: And that’s interesting.

cues.zh: 我是说，我相信这背后投入了很多思考。
cues.en: I mean, I’m sure a lot of thought went into that.

cues.zh: 你能具体谈谈吗？
cues.en: Can you just speak to it?

cues.zh: 你如何应对“Claude 的观点”这种矛盾之处？
cues.en: How do you address things that are a tension “Claude’s views”?

cues.zh: 我觉得有时候存在某种不对称，我记得我提到过这一点，我不确定是在系统提示的那部分还是别的地方，但模型在拒绝任务时略微更倾向于，比如说，它可能会拒绝涉及右翼政治人物的任务，但面对同等的左翼政治人物就不会。
cues.en: So I think there’s sometimes any symmetry, I think I noted this in, I can’t remember if it was that part of the system prompt or another, but the model was slightly more inclined to refuse tasks if it was about either say so, maybe it would refuse things with respect to a right-wing politician, but with an equivalent left-wing politician it wouldn’t.

cues.zh: 我们想要在那里有更多对称性，也许会把某些事情看得更清楚。
cues.en: And we wanted more symmetry there and would maybe perceive certain things to be.

cues.zh: 我觉得关键在于，如果很多人持有某种政治观点并想探讨它，你不希望 Claude 说，我的观点不同，所以我会把它当作有害的。
cues.en: I think it was the thing of if a lot of people have a certain political view and want to explore it, you don’t want Claude to be like, well, my opinion is different and so I’m going to treat that as harmful.

cues.zh: 所以我认为部分原因是为了引导模型，让它觉得，嘿，如果很多人都相信这件事，你就应该参与这个任务并愿意去做。
cues.en: And so I think it was partly to nudge the model to just be like, hey, if a lot of people believe this thing, you should just be engaging with the task and willing to do it.

cues.zh: 其中每一部分其实都在做不同的事，因为当你写出来却不声称客观时，这很有趣，因为你想做的是推动模型，让它更开放、更中立一些。
cues.en: Each of those parts of that is actually doing a different thing because it’s funny when you write out without claiming to be objective, because what you want to do is push the model so it’s more open, it’s a little bit more neutral.

cues.zh: 但接着我很想做的，是把它当作一个客观的东西，它只会谈论自己有多客观，而我就说，Claude，你仍然有偏见、有问题，所以别再声称一切了。
cues.en: But then what I would love to do is be like as an objective, it would just talk about how objective it was, and I was like, Claude, you’re still biased and have issues, and so stop claiming that everything.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，解决你潜在偏见的方法，不是直接说你所想的就是客观的。
cues.en: I’m like, the solution to potential bias from you is not to just say that what you think is objective.

cues.zh: 那是那部分的初始版本，系统提示词，我当时在反复迭代它。
cues.en: So that was with initial versions of that part, the system prompt, when I was iterating on it was like.

cues.zh: 所以这些句子的很多部分——
cues.en: So a lot of parts of these sentences-

cues.zh: 都在起作用。
cues.en: Are doing work.

cues.zh: ……都在起一些作用。
cues.en: … are doing some work.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 感觉就是这样。
cues.en: That’s what it felt like.

cues.zh: 这很有意思。
cues.en: That’s fascinating.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下过去几个月里提示词演变的某些方式吗？
cues.en: Can you explain maybe some ways in which the prompts evolved over the past few months?

cues.zh: 不同版本。
cues.en: Different versions.

cues.zh: 我看到填充短语的要求被移除了，它写的是，Claude直接回应所有人类消息，不使用不必要的肯定填充短语。
cues.en: I saw that the filler phrase request was removed, the filler it reads, Claude responds directly to all human messages without unnecessary affirmations to filler phrases.

cues.zh: 当然、没问题、绝对、太好了、当然可以。
cues.en: Certainly, of course, absolutely, great, sure.

cues.zh: 具体来说，Claude避免以“当然”这个词以任何方式开头回应。
cues.en: Specifically, Claude avoids starting responses with the word certainly in any way.

cues.zh: 这看起来是不错的指导，但为什么被删掉了？
cues.en: That seems like good guidance, but why was it removed?

cues.zh: 是啊，挺有意思的，这就是把系统提示公开的缺点之一——如果我只是想帮忙迭代系统提示，我不会想太多。
cues.en: Yeah, so it’s funny, this is one of the downsides of making system prompts public is I don’t think about this too much if I’m trying to help iterate on system prompts.

cues.zh: 我会考虑它会影响行为，但然后我就想，哇，有时候我写系统提示时会把“NEVER”全大写，我就想，这大概也会被公开出去。
cues.en: Again, I think about how it’s going to affect the behavior, but then I’m like, oh, wow, sometimes I put NEVER in all caps when I’m writing system prompt things and I’m like, I guess that goes out to the world.

cues.zh: 所以模型在训练时就这么做了，学到了这一点，基本上就是每句话都以“certainly”开头，然后你就能明白我为什么加了那些词，因为我想做的在某种程度上是把模型从这个习惯里引出来。
cues.en: So the model was doing this at loved for during training, picked up on this thing, which was to basically start everything with a certainly, and then you can see why I added all of the words, because what I’m trying to do is in some ways trap the model out of this.

cues.zh: 它只会把它换成另一个肯定词。
cues.en: It would just replace it with another affirmation.

cues.zh: 所以如果它被短语卡住，其实只要加上明确的短语并说永远不要那样做，就会有帮助。
cues.en: And so it can help if it gets caught in phrases, actually just adding the explicit phrase and saying never do that.

cues.zh: 然后它就能稍微更好地摆脱这种行为，因为不知为何这样确实有帮助。
cues.en: Then it sort of knocks it out of the behavior a little bit more because it does just for whatever reason help.

cues.zh: 基本上那只是训练产生的一个副产品，我们后来发现了并做了改进，让它不再发生。
cues.en: And then basically that was just an artifact of training that we then picked up on and improved things so that it didn’t happen anymore.

cues.zh: 一旦那发生，你就可以直接移除系统提示中的那部分。
cues.en: And once that happens, you can just remove that part of the system prompt.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得那就是我们说的，Claude 做肯定性话语少了一点，所以它就没做那么多。
cues.en: So I think that’s just something where we’re like, Claude does affirmations a bit less, and so it wasn’t doing as much.

cues.zh: 我明白了。
cues.en: I see.

cues.zh: 所以系统提示与后训练协同工作，甚至可能与前训练协同，来调整最终的整个系统。
cues.en: So the system prompt works hand in hand with the post-training and maybe even the pre-training to adjust the final overall system.

cues.zh: 你做的任何系统提示，都可以把那种行为蒸馏回模型里，因为你确实拥有所有工具来制作数据，可以训练模型更多地具备那种特质。
cues.en: Any system prompts that you make, you could distill that behavior back into a model because you really have all of the tools there for making data that you could train the models to just have that treat a little bit more.

cues.zh: 然后有时候你会在训练中发现一些问题。
cues.en: And then sometimes you’ll just find issues in training.

cues.zh: 所以我理解的方式是，系统提示的好处在于，它和后期训练的某些方面有很多相似的组成部分。
cues.en: So the way I think of it is the system prompt is, the benefit of it is that, and it has a lot of similar components to some aspects of post-training.

cues.zh: 它是一种轻推。
cues.en: It’s a nudge.

cues.zh: 所以我不介意 Claude 有时候说，当然，不，那没问题。
cues.en: And so do I mind if Claude sometimes says, sure, no, that’s fine.

cues.zh: 但它的措辞是非常、非常、非常绝对不要这样做，这样当它出错时，希望只是，我不知道，百分之几的概率，而不是 20% 或 30% 的概率。
cues.en: But the wording of it is very never, ever, ever do this so that when it does slip up, it’s hopefully, I don’t know, a couple of percent of the time and not 20 or 30% of the time.

cues.zh: 每样东西变得昂贵的程度不同，而系统提示的迭代成本很低。
cues.en: Each thing gets costly to a different degree and the system prompt is cheap to iterate on.

cues.zh: 如果你在微调模型中发现了一些问题，你可以直接用系统提示来修补它们。
cues.en: And if you’re seeing issues in the fine-tuned model, you can just potentially patch them with a system prompt.

cues.zh: 所以我把它看作是修补问题、稍微调整行为，让它更好、更符合人们的偏好。
cues.en: So I think of it as patching issues and slightly adjusting behaviors to make it better and more to people’s preferences.

cues.zh: 所以这几乎就像是解决问题的一种不那么稳健但更快的方式。
cues.en: So yeah, it’s almost like the less robust but faster way of just solving problems.

cues.zh: 让我问问你对智能这种感觉的看法。
cues.en: Let me ask you about the feeling of intelligence.

cues.zh: 所以Dario说任何一个Claude模型都没有变笨，但——
cues.en: So Dario said that any one model of Claude is not getting dumber, but-

cues.zh: 任何一个Claude模型都没有变笨，但网上有一种流行的说法，人们感觉Claude可能正在变笨。
cues.en: Any one model of Claude is not getting dumber, but there is a popular thing online where people have this feeling Claude might be getting dumber.

cues.zh: 从我的角度来看，这很可能是一种非常有趣的——我很想更深入理解——心理和社会效应。
cues.en: And from my perspective, it’s most likely a fascinating, I would love to understand it more, psychological, sociological effect.

cues.zh: 但作为一个经常和Claude交流的人，你能理解这种觉得Claude在变笨的感受吗？
cues.en: But you as a person who talks to Claude a lot, can you empathize with the feeling that Claude is getting dumber?

cues.zh: 我觉得这其实非常有意思，因为我记得当人们在网上标记这个问题时，我看到了这种情况发生。
cues.en: I think that that is actually really interesting,, because I remember seeing this happen when people were flagging this on the internet.

cues.zh: 这真的很有意思，因为我知道……至少在我观察的那些情况里，我就觉得，什么都没变。
cues.en: And it was really interesting, because I knew that… At least in the cases I was looking at, I was like, nothing has changed.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 从字面上讲，它不可能变。
cues.en: Literally, it cannot.

cues.zh: 这就是同一个模型，同样的系统提示词，什么都一样。
cues.en: It is the same model with the same system prompts, same everything.

cues.zh: 我觉得当确实有改动时，那才说得通。
cues.en: I think when there are changes, then it makes more sense.

cues.zh: 举个例子，在 claude.ai 上你可以开启或关闭 artifacts，而因为这是系统提示词的改动，我认为它确实会让行为发生一点变化。
cues.en: One example is, you can have artifacts turned on or off on claude.ai and because this is a system prompt change, I think it does mean that the behavior changes it a little bit.

cues.zh: 我确实向人们提过这一点，我说：“如果你喜欢 Claude 的行为，然后 artifacts 从需要手动开启变成了默认开启，那就试着把它关掉，看看你遇到的问题是不是这个改动造成的。”
cues.en: I did flag this to people, where I was like, “If you love Claude’s behavior, and then artifacts was turned from a thing you had to turn on to the default, just try turning it off and see if the issue you were facing was that change.”

cues.zh: 但这很有意思，因为你有时会看到人们指出出现了回归，而我心想：“这不可能……”再说一次，你永远不该轻率否定，所以你应该始终去调查，因为也许有些你没看到的问题，也许确实做了某些改动。
cues.en: But it was fascinating because you sometimes see people indicate that there’s a regression, when I’m like, “There cannot…” Again, you should never be dismissive and so you should always investigate, because maybe something is wrong that you’re not seeing, maybe there was some change made.

cues.zh: 然后你去研究一下，就会觉得，“这不就是同一个模型在做同样的事嘛。”而我会说，“我觉得只是你碰巧遇到几个不太走运的提示词之类的，看起来像是变差了很多，其实只是……可能只是运气问题。”
cues.en: Then you look into it and you’re like, “This is just the same model doing the same thing.” And I’m like, “I think it’s just that you got unlucky with a few prompts or something, and it looked like it was getting much worse and actually it was just… It was maybe just luck.”

cues.zh: 我还觉得有个真实的心理效应，就是人们……基线在提高，你开始习惯了好东西。
cues.en: I also think there is a real psychological effect where people just… The baseline increases and you start getting used to a good thing.

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: 每次 Claude 说出特别聪明的话，你对它智能的感知就在心里增长，我觉得是这样。
cues.en: All the times that Claude says something really smart, your sense of its intelligent grows in your mind, I think.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 然后如果你回头，用类似的方式——不是完全相同，而是类似的方式——去提示它之前还能应付的概念，结果它说了蠢话，那种负面体验就会特别突出。
cues.en: And then if you return back and you prompt in a similar way, not the same way, in a similar way, concept it was okay with before, and it says something dumb, that negative experience really stands out.

cues.zh: 我想这里要记住的是，光是提示词的细节就能产生很大影响。
cues.en: I guess the things to remember here is that just the details of a prompt can have a lot of impact.

cues.zh: 结果有很大的波动性。
cues.en: There’s a lot of variability in the result.

cues.zh: 另外你还会遇到随机性。
cues.en: And you can get randomness, is the other thing.

cues.zh: 只要把提示词试个4次或10次，你可能会发现，其实两个月前你试过它并且成功了，但如果你当时只是试一下，它可能只有一半的概率成功，而现在它也只有一半的概率成功。
cues.en: Just trying the prompt 4 or 10 times, you might realize that actually possibly two months ago you tried it and it succeeded, but actually if you just tried it, it would’ve only succeeded half of the time, and now it only succeeds half of the time.

cues.zh: 这也可能是一种影响。
cues.en: That can also be an effect.

cues.zh: 要写一个会被大量用户使用的系统提示词，你会感到压力吗？
cues.en: Do you feel pressure having to write the system prompt that a huge number of people are going to use?

cues.zh: 这感觉像是个有趣的心理学问题。
cues.en: This feels like an interesting psychological question.

cues.zh: 我感到很大的责任感之类的。
cues.en: I feel a lot of responsibility or something.

cues.zh: 你没法把这些东西做到完美，所以你没法……它注定是不完美的。
cues.en: You can’t get these things perfect, so you can’t… It’s going to be imperfect.

cues.zh: 你得反复迭代它。
cues.en: You’re going to have to iterate on it.

cues.zh: 不过我想说，这更多是责任，我觉得在 AI 领域工作让我学到，在有压力和责任感的氛围下，我反而能成长得更好，而不是……
cues.en: I would say more responsibility than anything else, though, I think working in AI has taught me that I thrive a lot more under feelings of pressure and responsibility than…

cues.zh: 我居然在学术界待了那么久，这几乎有点让人意外，因为我觉得那恰恰是相反的。
cues.en: It’s almost surprising that I went into academia for so long, because I just feel like it’s the opposite.

cues.zh: 事情进展很快，你肩负很多责任，不知为何我还挺享受的。
cues.en: Things move fast and you have a lot of responsibility and I quite enjoy it for some reason.

cues.zh: 影响真的非常大，如果你想想宪法 AI，想想为一个趋向超级智能、可能对非常多的人极其有用的东西写系统提示词。
cues.en: It really is a huge amount of impact, if you think about constitutional AI and writing a system prompt for something that’s tending towards super intelligence and potentially is extremely useful to a very large number of people.

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得这就是关键。
cues.en: Yeah, I think that’s the thing.

cues.zh: 你永远做不到完美，但我真正喜欢的是这个想法……当我试着打磨系统提示词时，我会反复推敲成千上万的提示词，试着去想象人们会想用 Claude 来做什么。
cues.en: You’re never going to get it perfect, but I think the thing that I really like is the idea that… When I’m trying to work on the system prompt, I’m bashing on thousands of prompts and I’m trying to imagine what people are going to want to use Claude for.

cues.zh: 我想做的，就是改善他们的体验。
cues.en: I guess the whole thing that I’m trying to do is improve their experience of it.

cues.zh: 也许正是这一点让人感觉良好。
cues.en: Maybe that’s what feels good.

cues.zh: 如果不完美，我就去改进，我们会解决问题。
cues.en: If it’s not perfect, I’ll improve it, we’ll fix issues.

cues.zh: 但有时候会发生的是，你会从人们那里得到对模型非常正面的反馈，你会看到其中有你做出的贡献。
cues.en: But sometimes the thing that can happen is that you’ll get feedback from people that’s really positive about the model and you’ll see that something you did.

cues.zh: 现在我看模型时，常常能准确看出某个特征或问题来自哪里。
cues.en: When I look at models now, I can often see exactly where a trait or an issue is coming from.

cues.zh: 所以，当你看到自己做过的、或者你有影响力的事情，我不知道，带来了那种改变，或者让别人有了一次愉快的交互，这很有意义。
cues.en: So, when you see something that you did or you were influential in, I don’t know, making that difference or making someone have a nice interaction, it’s quite meaningful.

cues.zh: 随着系统能力越来越强，这些事情会越来越有压力，因为现在它们还不够聪明，不会造成任何问题，但我认为随着时间推移，可能会逐渐变成一种不好的压力。
cues.en: As the systems get more capable, this stuff gets more stressful, because right now they’re not smart enough to pose any issues, but I think over time it’s going to feel like, possibly, bad stress over time.

cues.zh: 你如何获取关于人类体验的信号反馈，覆盖成千上万、数万、数十万人的痛点是什么、什么让他们感觉良好？
cues.en: How do you get signal feedback about the human experience across thousands, tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of people, what their pain points are, what feels good?

cues.zh: 你是只靠自己的直觉，在与它对话时去发现痛点吗？
cues.en: Are you just using your own intuition as you talk to it to see what are the pain points?

cues.zh: 我想我部分是这样做的。
cues.en: I think I use that partly.

cues.zh: 人们可以给我们发送反馈，包括正面和负面的，关于模型做过的事情，然后我们就能了解它在哪些方面存在不足。
cues.en: People can send us feedback, both positive and negative, about things that the model has done and then we can get a sense of areas where it’s falling short.

cues.zh: 在内部，人们大量使用模型，试图找出存在差距的领域。
cues.en: Internally, people work with the models a lot and try to figure out areas where there are gaps.

cues.zh: 我想这是我自己与它互动、观察内部人员与它互动，以及我们获得的明确反馈的结合。
cues.en: I think it’s this mix of interacting with it myself, seeing people internally interact with it, and then explicit feedback we get.

cues.zh: 如果人们在互联网上谈论 Claude，而我看到了，我也会认真对待。
cues.en: If people are on the internet and they say something about Claude and I see it, I’ll also take that seriously.

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我对此很纠结。
cues.en: I’m torn about that.

cues.zh: 我要问你一个来自 Reddit 的问题：“Claude 什么时候才能不再像清教徒祖母一样，把它的道德世界观强加给我这个付费用户？”还有，“让 Claude 过度道歉背后的心理是什么？”你会如何回应这些非常不具代表性的 Reddit 问题？
cues.en: I’m going to ask you a question from Reddit, “When will Claude stop trying to be my puritanical grandmother, imposing its moral worldview on me as a paying customer?” And also, “What is the psychology behind making Claude overly apologetic?” How would you address this very non-representative Reddit questions?

cues.zh: 我挺同情的，因为他们处在一个很困难的境地，我认为他们必须判断某件事是否真的有风险或糟糕，或者可能对你有害之类的。
cues.en: I’m pretty sympathetic, in that they are in this difficult position, where I think that they have to judge whether something’s actually, say, risky or bad, and potentially harmful to you, or anything like that.

cues.zh: 他们不得不在某处划下这条线。
cues.en: They’re having to draw this line somewhere.

cues.zh: 而如果他们把线划得太过偏向“我在把道德世界观强加给你”，那看起来就很糟。
cues.en: And if they draw it too much in the direction of I’m imposing my ethical worldview on you, that seems bad.

cues.zh: 很多时候，我觉得我们确实在这方面看到了全面的改进。
cues.en: In many ways, I like to think that we have actually seen improvements on this across the board.

cues.zh: 这很有意思，因为它恰好与增加更多角色训练相吻合。
cues.en: Which is interesting, because that coincides with, for example, adding more of character training.

cues.zh: 我想我的假设一直是，好的角色并不是那种纯粹道德说教的，而是……它尊重你、你的自主权，以及你在一定限度内选择什么对你好、什么对你合适的能力。
cues.en: I think my hypothesis was always the good character isn’t, again, one that’s just moralistic, it’s one that is… It respects you and your autonomy and your ability to choose what is good for you and what is right for you, within limits.

cues.zh: 这有时就是所谓的对用户的可纠正性，也就是愿意做用户要求的任何事情。
cues.en: This is sometimes this concept of corrigibility to the user, so just being willing to do anything that the user asks.

cues.zh: 如果模型愿意这样做，那它们就很容易被滥用。
cues.en: And if the models were willing to do that, then they would be easily misused.

cues.zh: 你只是在信任。
cues.en: You’re just trusting.

cues.zh: 到那时，你看到的模型的伦理以及它的行为，就完全是用户的伦理了。
cues.en: At that point, you’re just seeing the ethics of the model and what it does, is completely the ethics of the user.

cues.zh: 我觉得有理由不希望这样，尤其是随着模型越来越强大，因为可能只有少数人想用模型做真正有害的事。
cues.en: I think there’s reasons to not want that, especially as models become more powerful, because there might just be a small number of people who want to use models for really harmful things.

cues.zh: 但随着模型变得更聪明，让它们自己判断那条线在哪里，确实很重要。
cues.en: But having models, as they get smarter, figure out where that line is does seem important.

cues.zh: 然后是那种道歉行为，我不喜欢。
cues.en: And then with the apologetic behavior, I don’t like that.

cues.zh: 我更喜欢Claude更愿意反驳别人，或者干脆不道歉。
cues.en: I like it when Claude is a little bit more willing to push back against people or just not apologize.

cues.zh: 我的一部分想法是，这往往让人觉得没必要。
cues.en: Part of me is, often it just feels unnecessary.

cues.zh: 我觉得这些情况有望随着时间推移而减少。
cues.en: I think those are things that are hopefully decreasing over time.

cues.zh: 我认为如果人们在网上说些什么，并不意味着你就应该认为那……
cues.en: I think that if people say things on the internet, it doesn’t mean that you should think that that…

cues.zh: 实际上有个问题，99%的用户都在遭遇，却完全没有被那反映出来。
cues.en: There’s actually an issue that 99% of users are having that is totally not represented by that.

cues.zh: 但从很多方面来说，我只是在关注它，然后想，这样对吗？
cues.en: But in a lot of ways I’m just attending to it and being like, is this right?

cues.zh: 我同意吗？
cues.en: Do I agree?

cues.zh: 这是我们已经试图解决的问题吗？
cues.en: Is it something we’re already trying to address?

cues.zh: 这让我感觉不错。
cues.en: That feels good to me.

cues.zh: 我在想 Claude 在这方面能放肆到什么程度……我觉得稍微刻薄一点会更容易，但如果你是在跟一百万人说话，你可承担不起那样做，对吧？
cues.en: I wonder what Claude can get away with in terms of… I feel it would just be easier to be a little bit more mean, but you can’t afford to do that if you’re talking to a million people, right?

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我这辈子遇到过很多人，有时候……顺便说一句，苏格兰口音……如果他们有口音，他们可以说一些粗鲁的话还能蒙混过关。
cues.en: I’ve met a lot of people in my life that sometimes… By the way, Scottish accent… if they have an accent, they can say some rude shit and get away with it.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 他们就是更直白。
cues.en: They’re just blunter.

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: 有些很棒的工程师甚至领导者就是直来直去，他们直奔主题，不知怎么的，这是一种更有效的说话方式。
cues.en: There’s some great engineers and even leaders that are just blunt, and they get to their point, and it’s just a much more effective way of speaking somehow.

cues.zh: 但我想，当你不是超级聪明的时候，你可承担不起那样做。
cues.en: But I guess when you’re not super intelligent, you can’t afford to do that.

cues.zh: 你能有个直白模式吗？
cues.en: Can you have a blunt mode?

cues.zh: 可以，这似乎是可以做到的……我完全可以鼓励模型这么做。
cues.en: Yeah, that seems like a thing that you could… I could definitely encourage the model to do that.

cues.zh: 我觉得这很有意思，因为模型里有很多东西……有趣的是，有些行为你可能不太喜欢默认的样子，但我常跟人说：“你没意识到，如果我把它在另一个方向上推得太狠，你会多讨厌它。”
cues.en: I think it’s interesting, because there’s a lot of things in models that… It’s funny where there are some behaviors where you might not quite like the default, but then the thing I’ll often say to people is, “You don’t realize how much you will hate it if I nudge it too much in the other direction.”

cues.zh: 纠正的时候你会稍微遇到这种情况。
cues.en: You get this a little bit with correction.

cues.zh: 模型会接受你的纠正，现在可能有点太过了。
cues.en: The models accept correction from you, probably a little bit too much right now.

cues.zh: 如果你说“不，巴黎不是法国的首都”，它会反驳。但说实话，对于那些我认为模型相当有把握的事情，你有时还是能通过说它错了，让它收回。
cues.en: It’ll push back if you say, “No, Paris isn’t the capital of France.” But really, things that I think that the model’s fairly confident in, you can still sometimes get it to retract by saying it’s wrong.

cues.zh: 同时，如果你训练模型不要那样做，然后你在某件事上是对的，你纠正它，它却反驳你，说“不，你错了”，这很难形容，但那种感觉烦人得多。
cues.en: At the same time, if you train models to not do that and then you are correct about a thing and you correct it and it pushes back against you and is like, “No, you’re wrong.”, it’s hard to describe, that’s so much more annoying.

cues.zh: 所以，就是很多小烦恼对比一个大烦恼。我们常常拿它和完美状态作比较。
cues.en: So, it’s a lot of little annoyances versus one big annoyance.We often compare it with the perfect.

cues.zh: 然后我会说：“记住，这些模型并不完美，所以如果你往另一个方向推它，你就是在改变它会犯的错误类型。
cues.en: And then I’m like, “Remember, these models aren’t perfect, and so if you nudge it in the other direction, you’re changing the kind of errors it’s going to make.

cues.zh: 所以，想想哪些错误是你喜欢或不喜欢它犯的。”
cues.en: So, think about which are the kinds of errors you like or don’t like.”

cues.zh: 在像道歉态度这样的情况里，我不想把它往近乎直白的方向推得太多，因为我想象当它犯错时，它会往粗鲁的方向犯错。
cues.en: In cases like apologeticness, I don’t want to nudge it too much in the direction of almost bluntness, because I imagine when it makes errors, it’s going to make errors in the direction of being rude.

cues.zh: 而至少带着歉意时，你会觉得，好吧，我不太喜欢这样，但同时，这并没有对人刻薄。
cues.en: Whereas, at least with apologeticness you’re like, oh, okay, I don’t like it that much, but at the same time, it’s not being mean to people.

cues.zh: 而实际上，当模型毫无道理地对你刻薄时，你大概会比轻微不喜欢那个道歉要讨厌得多。
cues.en: And actually, the time that you undeservedly have a model be mean to you, you’ll probably like that a lot less than you mildly dislike the apology.

cues.zh: 这就是那种我确实希望它变好，但同时也要意识到另一边存在可能更糟的错误的事情。
cues.en: It’s one of those things where I do want it to get better, but also while remaining aware of the fact that there’s errors on the other side that are possibly worse.

cues.zh: 我觉得这在人的性格中非常重要。
cues.en: I think that matters very much in the personality of the human.

cues.zh: 我觉得有一群人，如果模型超级礼貌，他们根本不会尊重它，而有些人如果模型刻薄，会受到很大伤害。
cues.en: I think there’s a bunch of humans that just won’t respect the model at all if it’s super polite, and there’s some humans that’ll get very hurt if the model’s mean.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我想知道有没有办法根据性格来调整。
cues.en: I wonder if there’s a way to adjust to the personality.

cues.zh: 就算是不同地区，也只是不同的人而已。
cues.en: Even locale, there’s just different people.

cues.zh: 我对纽约没意见，但纽约确实更粗犷一点，说话直来直去，东欧大概也一样。
cues.en: Nothing against New York, but New York is a little rougher on the edges, they get to the point, and probably same with Eastern Europe.

cues.zh: 总之。
cues.en: Anyway.

cues.zh: 我觉得你可以直接告诉模型，我的……对所有这些情况，解决办法就是——
cues.en: I think you could just tell the model, is my… For all of these things, the solution is to-

cues.zh: 就是……
cues.en: Just to…

cues.zh: ……一直试着直接告诉模型去做。
cues.en: … always just try telling the model to do it.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 然后有时候，在对话开头，我就随口加一句，比如“我希望你做一个纽约客版的自己，永远不要道歉。”然后 Claude 大概会说，“好嘞，我试试。”
cues.en: And then sometimes, at the beginning of the conversation, I’d just throw in, I don’t know, “I’d like you to be a New Yorker version of yourself and never apologize.” Then I think Claude will be like, “Okey-doke, I will try.”

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Certainly.

cues.zh: 或者它会说，“我道歉，我没法做纽约客版的自己。”但希望它不会那样。
cues.en: Or it’ll be like, “I apologize, I can’t be a New Yorker type of myself.” But hopefully it wouldn’t do that.

cues.zh: 你说角色训练，角色训练里都包含什么？
cues.en: When you say character training, what’s incorporated into character training?

cues.zh: 那是 RLHF 还是我们在聊什么？
cues.en: Is that RLHF or what are we talking about?

cues.zh: 更像是宪法式 AI，是那条流水线的一个变体。
cues.en: It’s more like constitutional AI, so it’s a variant of that pipeline.

cues.zh: 我着手构建了模型应当具备的性格特质。
cues.en: I worked through constructing character traits that the model should have.

cues.zh: 这些特质可以比较简短，也可以是更丰富的描述。
cues.en: They can be shorter traits or they can be richer descriptions.

cues.zh: 然后让模型生成人类可能提出的、与该特质相关的查询。
cues.en: And then you get the model to generate queries that humans might give it that are relevant to that trait.

cues.zh: 接着它生成回答，再根据这些性格特质对回答进行排序。
cues.en: Then it generates the responses and then it ranks the responses based on the character traits.

cues.zh: 这样一来，在生成查询之后，它就和宪法式 AI 非常相似了，不过也有一些差异。
cues.en: In that way, after the generation of the queries, it’s very much similar to constitutional AI, it has some differences.

cues.zh: 我挺喜欢这个做法，因为这就像是 Claude 对自身性格的训练，因为它没有任何……它像宪法式 AI，但不使用任何人类数据。
cues.en: I quite like it, because it’s like Claude’s training in its own character, because it doesn’t have any… It’s like constitutional AI, but it’s without any human data.

cues.zh: 人类大概也该为自己这么做，比如，“用亚里士多德的定义来说，做一个好人意味着什么？”“好，不错。”你从和Claude的交谈中学到了关于真理本质的什么？
cues.en: Humans should probably do that for themselves too, like, “Defining in a Aristotelian sense, what does it mean to be a good person?” “Okay, cool.” What have you learned about the nature of truth from talking to Claude?

cues.zh: 什么是真实的？
cues.en: What is true?

cues.zh: 而追求真理又意味着什么？
cues.en: And what does it mean to be truth-seeking?

cues.zh: 我注意到这次对话的一点是，我问题的质量往往不如你回答的质量，那咱们继续这样吧。
cues.en: One thing I’ve noticed about this conversation is the quality of my questions is often inferior to the quality of your answer, so let’s continue that.

cues.zh: 我通常问个蠢问题，你就说，“哦，对。
cues.en: I usually ask a dumb question and you’re like, “Oh, yeah.

cues.zh: 这是个好问题。”就是那种感觉。
cues.en: That’s a good question.” It’s that whole vibe.

cues.zh: 或者我会误解它，然后说，“哦，对”
cues.en: Or I’ll just misinterpret it and be like, “Oh, yeah”
[inaudible 03:43:25] go with it.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我喜欢这样。
cues.en: I love it.

cues.zh: 我有两个想法，感觉隐约相关，不过如果不相关你告诉我。
cues.en: I have two thoughts that feel vaguely relevant, though let me know if they’re not.

cues.zh: 我觉得第一点是，人们可能低估了模型在交互时所做的事情的程度。
cues.en: I think the first one is people can underestimate the degree what models are doing when they interact.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们还是太多地把AI当成计算机这种模型。
cues.en: I think that we still just too much have this model of AI as computers.

cues.zh: 人们常说，“哦，你应该把什么价值观放进模型里？”而我常常觉得，这对我而言没那么说得通。
cues.en: People often say, “Oh, what values should you put into the model?” And I’m often like, that doesn’t make that much sense to me.

cues.zh: 因为我会想，嘿，作为人类，我们对价值观本身就是不确定的，我们会讨论它们，我们在某种程度上认为自己持有某种价值观，但我们也知道自己可能并不真正持有，也知道在什么情况下我们会用它去权衡其他东西。
cues.en: Because I’m like, hey, as human beings, we’re just uncertain over values, we have discussions of them, we have a degree to which we think we hold a value, but we also know that we might not and the circumstances in which we would trade it off against other things.

cues.zh: 这些东西真的非常复杂。
cues.en: These things are just really complex.

cues.zh: 我觉得一点是，也许我们可以期望让模型具备和人类同等程度的细腻与审慎，而不是认为我们必须以非常经典的方式把它们编程进去。
cues.en: I think one thing is the degree to which maybe we can just aspire to making models have the same level of nuance and care that humans have, rather than thinking that we have to program them in the very classic sense.

cues.zh: 我觉得那肯定算一个。
cues.en: I think that’s definitely been one.

cues.zh: 另一个有点奇怪，我不确定……也许这回答不了你的问题，但反正一直在我心上，就是这个事业高度务实，也许这就是为什么我欣赏对齐研究中的实证方法。
cues.en: The other, which is a strange one, and I don’t know if… Maybe this doesn’t answer your question, but it’s the thing that’s been on my mind anyway, is the degree to which this endeavor is so highly practical, and maybe why I appreciate the empirical approach to alignment.

cues.zh: 我有点担心这让我变得更实证，理论性稍微弱了一些。
cues.en: I slightly worry that it’s made me maybe more empirical and a little bit less theoretical.

cues.zh: 人们谈到AI对齐时，会问诸如“它应该对齐谁的价值观？
cues.en: People, when it comes to AI alignment, will ask things like, ” Whose values should it be aligned to?

cues.zh: 对齐到底意味着什么？”
cues.en: What does alignment even mean?”

cues.zh: 某种意义上，这些都在我脑子里。
cues.en: There’s a sense in which I have all of that in the back of my head.

cues.zh: 有社会选择理论，有那里所有的不可能性结果，所以你脑子里有巨大的理论空间，关于对齐模型可能意味着什么。
cues.en: There’s social choice theory, there’s all the impossibility results there, so you have this giant space of theory in your head about what it could mean to align models.

cues.zh: 但实际来说，肯定有些地方我们只是……尤其是面对更强大的模型，我的主要目标是让它们足够好，不至于出大乱子，足够好到我们能迭代并持续改进。
cues.en: But then practically, surely there’s something where we’re just… Especially with more powerful models, my main goal is I want them to be good enough that things don’t go terribly wrong, good enough that we can iterate and continue to improve things.

cues.zh: 因为这就是你所需要的全部。
cues.en: Because that’s all you need.

cues.zh: 如果你能让事情进展得足够顺利，从而能持续改进，那就足够了。
cues.en: If you can make things go well enough that you can continue to make them better, that’s sufficient.

cues.zh: 所以，我的目标不是那种完美的、让我们解决社会选择理论、然后造出某种……我也不知道，以某种方式完美契合每一个人类总体意愿的模型。
cues.en: So, my goal isn’t this perfect, let’s solve social choice theory and make models that, I don’t know, are perfectly aligned with every human being in aggregate somehow.

cues.zh: 而更多是，让事情运转得足够好，好到我们能改进它们。
cues.en: It’s much more, let’s make things work well enough that we can improve them.

cues.zh: 总的来说，我不知道，我的直觉是，在这些情况下经验比理论更好，因为理论是在追求乌托邦式的完美。
cues.en: Generally, I don’t know, my gut says empirical is better than theoretical in these cases, because it’s chasing utopian perfection.

cues.zh: 尤其是这么复杂、这么超级智能的模型，我不知道，我觉得那得花一辈子，而且实际上还会出错。
cues.en: Especially with such complex and especially super intelligent models, I don’t know, I think it’ll take forever and actually will get things wrong.

cues.zh: 这类似于快速写点代码做个实验，和花超长时间规划一个巨型实验然后只启动一次，以及反复启动、不断迭代之间的区别。
cues.en: It’s similar with the difference between just coding stuff up real quick as an experiment, versus planning a gigantic experiment for a super long time and then just launching it once, versus launching it over and over and over and iterating, iterating, so on.

cues.zh: 所以，我是经验主义的忠实拥趸。
cues.en: So, I’m a big fan of empirical.

cues.zh: 但你的担忧是，我在想自己是不是变得太经验主义了。
cues.en: But your worry is, I wonder if I’ve become too empirical.

cues.zh: 我觉得这就是那种你应该时刻质疑自己的事情。
cues.en: I think it’s one of those things where you should always just question yourself or something.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 为它辩护一下，我是……这就是那句“别让完美成为好的敌人”。
cues.en: In defense of it, I am… It’s the whole don’t let the perfect be the enemy of the good.

cues.zh: 但可能还不止于此，因为……有很多东西是完美的系统，却非常脆弱。
cues.en: But it’s maybe even more than that, where… There’s a lot of things that are perfect systems that are very brittle.

cues.zh: 有了 AI，我觉得更重要的是它得稳健、安全，也就是说，即使它可能不是完美的，即使存在问题，也不会造成灾难，不会发生可怕的事情。
cues.en: With AI, it feels much more important to me that it is robust and secure, as in you know that even though it might not be perfect everything, and even though there are problems, it’s not disastrous and nothing terrible is happening.

cues.zh: 对我来说就是这样，我想抬高下限。
cues.en: It feels like that to me, where I want to raise the floor.

cues.zh: 我想达到上限，但归根结底，我更在乎的是抬高下限。
cues.en: I want to achieve the ceiling, but ultimately I care much more about just raising the floor.

cues.zh: 这种程度的经验主义和务实精神，也许就源于此。
cues.en: This degree of empiricism and practicality comes from that, perhaps.

cues.zh: 岔开一下话题，因为这让我想起你写的一篇关于最优失败率的博客文章……
cues.en: To take a tangent on that, since it reminded me of a blog post you wrote on optimal rate of failure…

cues.zh: 哦，对。
cues.en: Oh, yeah.

cues.zh: ……你能解释一下其中的核心观点吗？
cues.en: … can you explain the key idea there?

cues.zh: 我们如何计算生活中各个领域的最优失败率？
